# CL-OA-015 — Assessment Completion Timeframe Compliance
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-015 |
| Policy Title | Assessment Completion Timeframe Compliance |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the complete assessment completion timeframe compliance framework for all comprehensive OASIS assessments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., establishing specific operational deadlines, a real-time monitoring system, individual clinician accountability standards, organizational escalation procedures, and the supervisory documentation requirements that together ensure the agency's OASIS completion rates remain within acceptable regulatory and operational standards at all times.
This policy is distinct from CL-OA-001 (OASIS Completion Timeliness & Accountability) in its operational emphasis. While CL-OA-001 defines the regulatory deadlines and the tracking dashboard, this policy focuses on the compliance framework — the specific accountability standards for each role, the performance threshold definitions that trigger action, the corrective action process that is applied when thresholds are breached, and the integration of timeframe compliance into the agency's broader quality and performance management systems. Together, CL-OA-001 and CL-OA-015 establish a two-layer OASIS timeliness governance structure: the tracking infrastructure and the accountability framework that enforces it.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the Director of Nursing, the OASIS Transmission Coordinator, Clinical Coordinators, and Revenue Cycle staff. It governs all OASIS time points at all assessment windows.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. establishes the following performance standards for OASIS assessment completion, in addition to the regulatory deadlines defined in CL-OA-001:

| Standard Level | Metric | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agency-Level Standard — Operations Target | Percentage of all OASIS assessments completed within agency operational targets (SOC/ROC/RECERT/FU: 3 calendar days; TRN/DC: 2 calendar days) | ≥90% |
| Agency-Level Standard — Regulatory Compliance | Percentage of all OASIS assessments completed within CMS regulatory deadlines (5 calendar days for most time points) | ≥98% |
| Individual Assessor Standard — Operations Target | No individual assessor shall have more than 2 OASIS assessments exceeding the operational target in any 30-day period | Maintained continuously |
| Individual Assessor Standard — Regulatory Compliance | No individual assessor shall have any OASIS assessment exceed the regulatory deadline for any reason other than a documented external circumstance | Zero-tolerance for preventable regulatory deadline breaches |

4.2 All assessors are individually accountable for completing their assigned OASIS assessments within the operational targets defined in CL-OA-001. Individual accountability is tracked at the assessor level in the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard and reported to each assessor monthly with specific performance data.
4.3 The Director of Nursing is organizationally accountable for the agency's aggregate OASIS timeliness performance and shall implement corrective action when agency-level or individual-level performance standards are not met.
4.4 OASIS timeliness compliance is a component of each assessor's annual performance evaluation per HR-ER-001. Chronic timeliness failures that meet the criteria defined in Section 6.4 shall result in a formal Documentation Improvement Plan per HR-ER-001.
4.5 Revenue Cycle shall not submit any claim for any episode dependent on an OASIS assessment that has not been completed and locked within the CMS regulatory deadline. Claims submission status shall be linked to OASIS completion status in the agency's billing workflow.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Operational Target | The agency's internally established OASIS completion deadline, which is more stringent than the CMS regulatory deadline, providing a buffer for quality review and error correction before submission. Per CL-OA-001: SOC/ROC/RECERT/FU within 3 calendar days; TRN/DC within 2 calendar days. |
| Regulatory Deadline | The CMS-mandated deadline for OASIS assessment completion — 5 calendar days from the trigger event for most time points. Missing the regulatory deadline is a CoP compliance deficiency. |
| Operational Target Breach | Any OASIS assessment completed after the operational target but before the regulatory deadline. Tracked and reported; triggers monitoring and coaching. |
| Regulatory Deadline Breach | Any OASIS assessment not completed within the regulatory deadline. A compliance deficiency — triggers mandatory corrective action and, when attributable to an assessor's preventable delay, progressive discipline. |
| Preventable Delay | A regulatory deadline breach that is caused by the assessor's failure to complete the assessment within the required timeframe, without a documented external circumstance (patient hospitalization, documented EHR outage, assessor medical emergency). |
| External Circumstance | A regulatory deadline breach attributable to an event beyond the assessor's control — patient hospitalized before assessment completion, documented EHR system outage exceeding 4 hours, assessor medical emergency. External circumstances must be documented contemporaneously; retroactive documentation of external circumstances is not accepted. |
| OASIS Completion Rate | The percentage of OASIS assessments at each time point completed and locked by their respective deadline within a defined reporting period. Calculated separately for operational targets and regulatory deadlines, and separately by time point and by individual assessor. |
| Assessment Completion Report | The weekly report generated from the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard documenting each assessor's completion rate, pending assessments, and any operational target or regulatory deadline breaches from the prior reporting period. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Individual Assessor Accountability

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Upon completing an assessment visit (SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU), initiate OASIS documentation immediately — at the visit using mobile EHR access, or within 2 hours of returning to the office/home. The goal is same-day or next-day completion; the operational target of 3 calendar days is the maximum, not the expectation. | At or immediately after each assessment visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | Monitor personal OASIS completion status in the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard daily. Each assessor is responsible for ensuring their assigned assessments are on track to meet operational targets. Do not wait for the coordinator alert at the operational target date — self-monitor and complete assessments proactively. | Daily. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | When an assessor identifies that they will be unable to complete a scheduled assessment within the operational target due to a clinical or personal circumstance, notify the Director of Nursing on the same business day. The Director of Nursing may authorize a 24-hour extension to the operational target (not the regulatory deadline) for documented valid reasons and may arrange reassignment if needed. | On the business day the barrier is identified. |
| 6.1.4 | Assessing RN | Document any external circumstance that affects assessment completion timing contemporaneously — in the EHR with a timestamp — at the time the circumstance occurs. Do not attempt to document external circumstances after the deadline has passed. | At the time the external circumstance occurs. |

### 6.2 — OASIS Transmission Coordinator Daily Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Generate and review the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard per CL-OA-001 every business day. Identify all assessments at Yellow status (approaching operational target) and Orange status (operational target passed). | Daily by 9:00 AM. |
| 6.2.2 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For Yellow status assessments: send an automated EHR reminder to the responsible assessor. Document the reminder in the tracking log. | Same day as Yellow alert. |
| 6.2.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For Orange status assessments: contact the responsible assessor by telephone. Verify the assessment status and expected completion time. If the assessor cannot confirm completion before the regulatory deadline, immediately escalate to the Director of Nursing. | Within 2 hours of Orange alert. |
| 6.2.4 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For Red status assessments (regulatory deadline passed): immediately notify the Director of Nursing. Document the breach in the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard with the date identified, the assessor, and the time point. | Immediately upon Red status. |

### 6.3 — Director of Nursing Oversight and Escalation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Review the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard weekly. Generate the weekly Assessment Completion Report and review each assessor's completion rate, pending assessments, and any breaches from the prior week. | Weekly; documented in the Director of Nursing's supervisory log. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | For any operational target breach identified (assessment completed after the operational target but before the regulatory deadline): contact the responsible assessor within 24 hours; discuss the reason for the delay; provide corrective guidance; document the contact. | Within 24 hours of identification. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | For any regulatory deadline breach: (a) contact the responsible assessor within 4 hours; (b) assess whether the breach was a preventable delay or attributable to an external circumstance; (c) direct immediate assessment completion if not yet completed; (d) notify the Compliance Officer within 24 hours; (e) assess the billing implications with Revenue Cycle within 48 hours; (f) initiate corrective action per Section 6.4 if the breach was preventable. | Within 4 hours of identification; Compliance Officer within 24 hours. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | Calculate monthly OASIS completion rates for the agency and for each individual assessor. Report the data in the monthly Documentation Quality Dashboard per CL-CD-001. Present to the QAPI Committee quarterly. | Monthly dashboard; quarterly QAPI presentation. |

### 6.4 — Corrective Action for Timeframe Non-Compliance

| Threshold | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1st operational target breach in any 30-day period (individual assessor) | Verbal corrective guidance from Director of Nursing, documented in supervisory log | Director of Nursing | Within 24 hours of identification |
| 2nd operational target breach in any 30-day period (same assessor) | Written corrective guidance; increased supervisor monitoring of that assessor's assessments for 30 days | Director of Nursing | Within 24 hours of 2nd breach |
| 3rd or subsequent operational target breach in any 30-day period (same assessor) | Formal corrective counseling per HR-ER-002; initiation of Documentation Improvement Plan per HR-ER-001; completion of additional OASIS timeliness training | Director of Nursing / HR Director | Within 7 calendar days of 3rd breach |
| 1st preventable regulatory deadline breach (any individual assessor) | Written corrective action per HR-ER-002; mandatory OASIS timeliness training within 14 calendar days; increased monitoring for 60 days | Director of Nursing / HR Director | Within 5 business days of identification |
| 2nd preventable regulatory deadline breach within 180 days (same assessor) | Formal disciplinary action per HR-ER-002; suspension of OASIS assessment authorization pending competency re-evaluation per CL-OA-003; OASIS authorization restored only after competency re-validation | Director of Nursing / HR Director | Within 5 business days of 2nd breach |
| Agency-level OASIS completion rate below 98% regulatory target in any quarter | QAPI Performance Improvement Project initiated per QA-PI-001; Director of Nursing presents root cause analysis to QAPI Committee | Director of Nursing / QAPI Coordinator | PIP initiated within 14 calendar days of quarterly data review |

### 6.5 — Integration with Claims Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Revenue Cycle | Before preparing any Medicare home health claim for submission, verify in the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard that all OASIS assessments for the episode (SOC/ROC at minimum; RECERT for claims spanning multiple certification periods) are completed, locked, and showing Green status (completed within deadline). | Before each claim preparation. |
| 6.5.2 | Revenue Cycle | If any assessment for the episode is not completed within the regulatory deadline and the episode claim is being prepared for submission, place the claim on billing hold and notify the Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer immediately. | Immediately upon identifying an incomplete or late assessment during claim preparation. |
| 6.5.3 | Revenue Cycle | Release the billing hold and proceed with claim submission only after the Director of Nursing confirms: (a) the assessment has been completed (even if late); and (b) the Compliance Officer has assessed the billing implications of the late completion and authorized submission. | After Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer confirmation. |

# CL-OA-016 — Scoring Methodology Integrity for Multi-Item Assessments
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-016 |
| Policy Title | Scoring Methodology Integrity for Multi-Item Assessments |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that for all OASIS items derived from multi-component standardized assessment tools — specifically the BIMS, PHQ-2, PHQ-9, and MAHC-10 — the individual component scores are correctly calculated, summed, and applied to the corresponding OASIS item responses in strict accordance with the scoring algorithms defined in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and the validated tool-specific scoring protocols at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Scoring methodology integrity is the technical precision layer of OASIS accuracy. A BIMS can be administered correctly — all three components in the correct sequence, using the correct items — but scored incorrectly, producing a total score that does not match the component responses. A PHQ-9 can be administered with the correct items in the correct order but have the frequency response options mis-scored (e.g., assigning 2 points for "Several days" instead of 1 point), producing a total score that systematically overstates or understates symptom severity. These scoring errors are distinct from administration errors (governed by CL-OA-011) and are distinct from coding errors (governed by CL-OA-004) — they are arithmetic and algorithmic failures in translating correctly administered tool results into the scores that drive OASIS item responses.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors who administer and score the BIMS, PHQ-2/PHQ-9, and MAHC-10, and to the OASIS Quality Reviewer and Director of Nursing who validate scoring accuracy.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The scoring of all multi-component standardized assessment tools shall follow exactly the scoring algorithms specified in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and the validated tool-specific scoring guides. No agency-created scoring shortcuts, simplified scoring algorithms, or score estimation methods shall be used.
4.2 Individual component scores shall be calculated independently for each component before the total score is computed. Total scores shall not be estimated from clinical impression or from recall of prior administration results.
4.3 The OASIS item response derived from each standardized tool result shall correspond exactly to the score range-to-response mapping specified in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. When a total score falls at a boundary between two response categories, the CMS guidance for that specific boundary shall govern the response selection.
4.4 All component scores and total scores shall be documented in the assessment narrative per CL-OA-011 before the derived OASIS item is coded. The coded OASIS response and the documented scores shall be internally consistent — an assessor cannot document a BIMS total of 14 (Cognitively Intact) and code M1700 at the Moderate Impairment level without a documented clinical explanation.
## 5. Scoring Algorithms — Required Methodology
### 5.1 BIMS Scoring Algorithm

| Component | Items | Maximum Score | Scoring Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Component A — Word Repetition | 3 specific words (sock, blue, bed) | 3 | 1 point per word repeated correctly immediately; 0 points for each word not repeated |
| Component B — Temporal Orientation | Year (1 pt), Month (1 pt, with near-miss rule), Day of Week (1 pt) | 3 | Year: correct = 1, incorrect = 0. Month: correct = 1, within 5 calendar days of month boundary = 0.5 per CMS guidance, incorrect = 0. Day of week: correct = 1, incorrect = 0. |
| Component C — Word Recall | Same 3 words from Component A | 3 | 1 point per word recalled without cueing; 0 points for words not recalled or recalled only with cueing |
| BIMS Total Score | Sum of Components A + B + C | 15 |  |

Score-to-M1700 Response Mapping:
Total Score 13–15: M1700 = Cognitively Intact (Code per current CMS OASIS-E2 guidance)
Total Score 8–12: M1700 = Moderately Impaired (Code per current CMS OASIS-E2 guidance)
Total Score 0–7: M1700 = Severely Impaired (Code per current CMS OASIS-E2 guidance)
Scoring Integrity Rules:
Component A (word repetition) and Component C (word recall) use the same three words. The three words must be stated once in Component A and recalled without prompting in Component C. Any prompting during Component C recall results in 0 for that word.
The month temporal orientation question scoring rule for near-month-boundary responses must follow the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual exactly — this rule has specific instructions that differ from a simple correct/incorrect binary. Assessors must reference the Guidance Manual for this item.
BIMS total score = Component A score + Component B score + Component C score. There is no weighting — all components contribute equally on a point-for-point basis.
### 5.2 PHQ-2 Scoring Algorithm

| Item | Question | Response Options | Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Item 1 | "Little interest or pleasure in doing things" | Not at all = 0; Several days = 1; More than half the days = 2; Nearly every day = 3 | 0–3 |
| Item 2 | "Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless" | Not at all = 0; Several days = 1; More than half the days = 2; Nearly every day = 3 | 0–3 |
| PHQ-2 Total | Sum of Items 1 + 2 |  | 0–6 |

Scoring Rule: PHQ-2 total ≥3 = positive screen requiring PHQ-9 administration. PHQ-2 total < 3 = negative screen (PHQ-9 not required unless clinical presentation indicates depression regardless of PHQ-2 score).
### 5.3 PHQ-9 Scoring Algorithm
All 9 items use the same frequency response scale: Not at all = 0; Several days = 1; More than half the days = 2; Nearly every day = 3.
| PHQ-9 Item | | Maximum Score | |:-----------|:|:-------------| | Items 1–9 | Each scored 0–3 | 3 per item | | PHQ-9 Total | Sum of Items 1–9 | 27 |
Score-to-Severity Mapping:
1–4: Minimal depression
5–9: Mild depression
10–14: Moderate depression
15–19: Moderately Severe depression
20–27: Severe depression
Score-to-OASIS Response Mapping: Follow the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual response-to-score mapping for M1730 and M1750. Do not use alternative depression severity classifications.
Item 9 Special Rule: PHQ-9 Item 9 ("Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself in some way?") must be scored using the same 0–3 frequency scale as all other items. Any response of ≥1 (any frequency of suicidal ideation) triggers the suicidality assessment protocol per CL-SD-022 Section 6.5. The PHQ-9 Item 9 score is not reduced or excluded from the total score — it contributes to the total score exactly as scored.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Scoring Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Immediately following tool administration, score each component of the administered tool before moving to the next clinical activity. Do not rely on memory — score while the patient's responses are still immediately available. | Immediately after tool administration. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | Calculate the total score by summing the individual component scores per the algorithm in Section 5. Verify the arithmetic by re-adding the component scores. | At the time of scoring. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | Apply the score-to-OASIS-response mapping from the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. Verify that the coded OASIS item response corresponds to the total score band. | At the time of OASIS item coding. |
| 6.1.4 | Assessing RN | Document all individual component scores, the total score, the score band, and the OASIS item response in the assessment narrative per CL-OA-011. The documentation sequence (components → total → score band → OASIS response) must be visible in the narrative and must be internally consistent. | Before locking the assessment. |
| 6.1.5 | Assessing RN | Before locking, perform a final self-check: re-verify that the documented OASIS item response matches the documented total score's score band. If there is any discrepancy between the documented score and the coded OASIS response, do not lock — correct the discrepancy first. | Before locking. |

### 6.2 — OASIS Quality Reviewer Scoring Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | For every SOC assessment reviewed per CL-OA-002: (a) independently re-calculate the BIMS total score from the documented component scores; (b) independently re-calculate the PHQ-2 total score from the documented item scores; (c) if PHQ-9 was administered, independently re-calculate the PHQ-9 total score from all 9 item scores; (d) verify that the calculated totals match the documented totals; (e) verify that the documented totals map to the coded OASIS item responses. | Within the Level 2 review timeline per CL-OA-002. |
| 6.2.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If any scoring discrepancy is identified (component scores that do not sum to the documented total, or a total score that does not map to the coded OASIS response), classify the discrepancy as a scoring error and initiate the correction process per CL-OA-002. | Within 24 hours of identification. |

### 6.3 — Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BIMS component scores documented but do not sum to the documented total | OASIS Quality Reviewer initiates correction | Correct the total score. Verify which component score is in error if the total and components are inconsistent. Correct the OASIS item response if the corrected total falls in a different score band. | Correction within 5 business days. |
| PHQ-9 total documented as 0 when individual item scores sum to >0 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Correct the total. If the correction changes M1730/M1750 from "No depression" to a positive depression code, assess whether physician notification per CL-SD-022 was triggered and is documented. | Correction within 5 business days; physician notification assessment immediately. |
| Assessor routinely scores BIMS without documenting component scores, only total | Director of Nursing identifies in monthly audit | Targeted BIMS scoring competency retraining. Implement direct observation of BIMS scoring during the next assessment. | Retraining within 7 calendar days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BIMS component scores (A, B, C) and total | Individual component scores and summed total | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Before locking; retained minimum 7 years |
| PHQ-2 item scores (1, 2) and total | Individual item scores and summed total | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Before locking; retained minimum 7 years |
| PHQ-9 item scores (items 1–9) and total | All 9 individual item scores and summed total | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Before locking (if PHQ-9 administered); retained minimum 7 years |
| Score-band-to-OASIS-response notation | Documentation that total score falls in the applicable score band | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Before locking |
| Quality Reviewer scoring re-verification | Documentation of independent score recalculation | OASIS Quality Reviewer | OASIS Quality Review Log | At each Level 2 review; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |

| BIMS component scores documented and sum to documented total | Monthly OASIS audit — Quality Reviewer independent recalculation | ≥98% — zero scoring arithmetic errors on audited records |
| PHQ total scores consistent with individual item scores | Monthly audit | ≥98% |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |

| BIMS total documented without component scores; total appears estimated | Cannot verify scoring accuracy; suggests informal administration | Annual BIMS competency requires component score documentation in the EHR template |

# CL-OA-017 — Contemporaneous Documentation Requirement
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-017 |
| Policy Title | Contemporaneous Documentation Requirement |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that all clinical findings, observations, assessment data, standardized tool results, and clinical reasoning supporting OASIS assessment item responses at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. be documented at or near the time of the clinical encounter — not reconstructed from memory after the fact, not interpolated from subsequent clinical contacts, and not reverse-engineered from the OASIS item responses that were selected before the documentation was written. The contemporaneous documentation requirement is the foundational integrity standard of clinical recordkeeping. It applies broadly across all clinical documentation per CL-CD-001 and CL-CD-004, but carries heightened significance in the OASIS context because OASIS documentation directly drives regulatory compliance, billing classification, and public quality reporting in ways that make reconstruction-based documentation not merely a documentation shortcut but a clinical integrity failure with measurable systemic consequences.
The EHR audit trail — which is immutable, timestamped, and accessible to CMS surveyors, MAC auditors, and OIG investigators — records when every entry was created and when every OASIS response was selected. A visit that occurred on July 5 with OASIS documentation created on July 9 is visible in the audit trail as a non-contemporaneous entry. An assessor who coded the OASIS responses on July 5 and then wrote the supporting narrative on July 9 is documenting in reverse sequence — and the audit trail will show this. This policy establishes the specific standards, timelines, and accountability requirements that prevent non-contemporaneous documentation from occurring and address it definitively when it does.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the Director of Nursing, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, and Medical Records staff. It governs the timing and sequence of all clinical documentation created in connection with comprehensive OASIS assessments at all applicable time points.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All clinical findings, physical examination results, patient and caregiver interview responses, standardized tool component scores and totals, and clinical reasoning entries that support OASIS item responses shall be documented in the EHR within 24 hours of the clinical encounter at which they were obtained. The 24-hour standard is the absolute maximum — same-day documentation is the agency's expected standard.
4.2 Clinical documentation supporting OASIS items shall be created in a sequence that reflects the actual clinical process: observations are made, data is collected, documentation is written, and OASIS responses are selected based on the documented evidence. The reverse sequence — selecting OASIS responses first and then writing documentation to support them — constitutes reverse-engineered documentation and is explicitly prohibited.
4.3 Late entry documentation — clinical narrative created after the 24-hour documentation standard of CL-CD-004 — is permissible when genuinely required by a documented clinical circumstance (clinical emergency during the visit, EHR system outage, assessor medical emergency). Late entries shall comply with the late entry standards of CO-DC-003, including the required attestation language identifying the actual date and time of documentation and the reason for the delay. Late entries that are created for the purpose of providing post-hoc justification for OASIS responses already coded do not constitute valid clinical documentation regardless of their content or the attestation applied.
4.4 OASIS item responses shall not be locked in the EHR without completed, authenticated supporting documentation in the assessment narrative. An OASIS item that is coded without corresponding narrative documentation at the time of coding is an unsupported response per CL-OA-007. The EHR workflow shall enforce narrative completion as a prerequisite for OASIS response entry where technically feasible.
4.5 The audit trail generated by the EHR for all OASIS-related documentation entries is a compliance record. It shall be maintained per CO-DC-001 and CO-HP-007, shall not be altered or deleted, and shall be available for review by the Compliance Officer, Director of Nursing, OASIS Quality Reviewer, CMS surveyors, and authorized audit entities.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Contemporaneous Documentation | Documentation created at or within 24 hours of the clinical encounter it describes, reflecting actual clinical observations and findings as they occurred — not reconstructed from memory after a longer interval. |
| Non-Contemporaneous Documentation | Documentation created more than 24 hours after the clinical encounter it describes, without a documented clinical justification for the delay. A form of late entry requiring compliance with CO-DC-003. |
| Reverse-Engineered Documentation | Documentation created for the specific purpose of justifying OASIS responses that were selected before the documentation was written. An integrity violation regardless of the accuracy of the underlying documentation. Distinguished from contemporaneous documentation in which the sequence is: observe → document → code. |
| Late Entry | Documentation created after the deadline applicable to the type of entry (24 hours for visit notes and OASIS supporting narratives per CL-CD-004), documented with a clear attestation identifying it as a late entry per CO-DC-003. Permissible when genuinely required by a documented external circumstance. |
| Audit Trail Timestamp | The EHR-generated, immutable record of the date and time each documentation entry was created, modified, or authenticated — maintained per CO-DC-001. |
| Documentation Sequence | The order in which clinical documentation entries are created in the EHR — the sequence of: (1) clinical encounter occurs; (2) clinical findings are documented; (3) OASIS items are coded from the documented findings. The correct sequence is 1→2→3; reverse-engineering inverts to 1→3→2. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Standards for Assessment-Day and Next-Day Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Begin documenting clinical findings during the assessment visit using mobile EHR access wherever feasible. At minimum, record vital signs, standardized tool component scores, and key physical examination findings at the time of the visit — before leaving the patient's home. These real-time entries constitute the most contemporaneous documentation available. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | Complete the full assessment narrative — including all required clinical descriptions per CL-OA-007 substantiation standards — within 24 hours of the assessment visit. Complete the narrative before selecting OASIS item responses. The narrative drives the OASIS selection; the OASIS selection does not drive the narrative. | Within 24 hours of the assessment visit; before OASIS item selection. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | Complete OASIS item selection after the narrative is sufficiently complete to provide evidentiary support for each item being coded. Lock the assessment only after both the narrative and the OASIS responses are complete and the pre-submission quality review per CL-OA-019 and cross-document verification per CL-OA-013 have been completed. | Within the operational target per CL-OA-001; always before the regulatory deadline. |
| 6.1.4 | Assessing RN | For standardized tool results (BIMS, PHQ-2/PHQ-9, MAHC-10), document the individual component/item scores at the time of tool administration or within 2 hours of the assessment visit. Component scores documented days after administration cannot represent contemporaneous recording of actual patient responses. | At the time of tool administration or within 2 hours of the visit. |

### 6.2 — Late Entry Compliance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assessing RN | When clinical documentation cannot be completed within 24 hours of the assessment visit due to a documented external circumstance: (a) create the late entry as soon as the circumstance is resolved; (b) include the late entry attestation per CO-DC-003: "LATE ENTRY — Clinical visit date: [date]. Documentation delayed due to [specific reason]. Documented on: [current date/time]. Author: [name/credential]."; (c) document the clinical circumstances of the external circumstance in the attestation or in the EHR administrative notes contemporaneously with the external circumstance. | At the earliest opportunity after the external circumstance is resolved. |
| 6.2.2 | Assessing RN | Do not create a late entry for the purpose of adding narrative support for OASIS responses that were already selected. If OASIS responses were selected before narrative documentation exists, this is a sequencing error. The appropriate action is: (a) do not add narrative after the fact without documenting the situation; (b) notify the Director of Nursing of the sequencing error; (c) if the unsupported OASIS responses were already locked, assess with the Director of Nursing and OASIS Quality Reviewer whether a correction per CL-OA-002 is needed. | Immediately upon identifying a sequencing error. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | When a late entry is created for an assessment-related document, review the EHR audit trail to verify: (a) the clinical visit timestamp vs. the documentation creation timestamp; (b) whether the stated reason for late entry is clinically plausible; (c) whether the OASIS item selections were made before or after the supporting documentation was created. Flag any entries where the OASIS responses pre-date the supporting narrative. | Within 5 business days of identifying a late entry. |

### 6.3 — Audit Trail Review for Documentation Sequence Integrity

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | During the monthly OASIS accuracy audit per CL-OA-002, review the EHR audit trail for a sample of assessed records to verify documentation sequence integrity: (a) the assessment narrative entries precede the OASIS item selection entries in chronological order; (b) all narrative entries have timestamps within 24 hours of the visit date; (c) standardized tool scores are documented at or near the visit timestamp. | Monthly audit. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | When the audit trail reveals a pattern of OASIS item selections preceding narrative documentation, treat this as a Priority 1 documentation integrity concern. Notify the Compliance Officer within 24 hours. Conduct a full review of all assessments by the affected assessor(s) from the prior 90 days. | Within 24 hours of pattern identification; 90-day review initiated within 5 business days. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | When notified of a documentation sequence integrity concern: assess whether the pattern constitutes a systemic documentation integrity failure; determine whether any submitted OASIS assessments are unsupported by contemporaneous clinical evidence; assess False Claims Act implications if PDGM payment was collected for episodes with integrity-compromised assessments. | Assessment within 5 business days of notification. |

### 6.4 — Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A single assessment's narrative is created more than 24 hours after the visit without a late entry attestation | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing directs the assessor to immediately add a late entry attestation per CO-DC-003. Provides corrective guidance on the 24-hour documentation standard. | Attestation within 24 hours of identification; counseling within 5 business days. |
| EHR audit trail shows OASIS item selections created before supporting narrative entries for multiple assessments by the same assessor | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Compliance Officer and Director of Nursing jointly investigate. Assess all affected assessments for documentation integrity. Initiate OASIS corrections per CL-OA-002 where supported by contemporaneous evidence; flag for Compliance Officer review where contemporaneous evidence cannot be established. Initiate HR corrective action per HR-ER-002 against the assessor. | Investigation within 5 business days; HR action within 14 calendar days. |
| A system-wide EHR outage prevents documentation during or following assessment visits | IT Director initiates recovery; Director of Nursing manages clinical documentation protocol | All assessors document on paper during the outage per the paper backup protocol. Upon EHR restoration, all paper entries are transcribed as late entries with outage-specific attestation. The EHR audit trail will record the transcription date, which is expected and acceptable for documented outages. | Paper documentation immediately during outage; EHR transcription within 24 hours of restoration. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment narrative entries | All clinical findings per CL-OA-007 standards | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Within 24 hours of assessment; before OASIS item selection |
| Standardized tool component scores | Individual scores at time of tool administration | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | At tool administration or within 2 hours of visit |
| Late entry attestations | Attestation language per CO-DC-003 for any entry >24 hours post-visit | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Concurrent with late entry creation |
| EHR audit trail — documentation timestamps | Immutable system-generated log of all entry timestamps | EHR system (automatic) | EHR audit trail | Maintained continuously; retained minimum 7 years |
| Monthly documentation sequence audit results | Audit trail sequence verification for sample | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Monthly; retained minimum 7 years |
| Compliance Officer documentation integrity investigation | Investigation findings and corrective actions | Compliance Officer | Compliance file | At each investigation; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment narratives created within 24 hours of visit | EHR audit trail timestamp analysis — monthly audit | ≥95% of assessment narratives created within 24 hours |
| Narrative documentation precedes OASIS item selection in EHR sequence | Monthly audit trail sequence review for sample | ≥98% of assessments with narrative-preceding-OASIS sequence |
| Late entries include required CO-DC-003 attestation language | Monthly audit of all late entries | 100% — zero late entries without attestation |
| No identified patterns of reverse-engineered documentation | Monthly audit trail review | Zero pattern findings; any individual instance triggers investigation |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessors complete OASIS items in the EHR during or immediately after the visit without documenting narrative — then write the narrative later | Audit trail shows OASIS before narrative; reverse-engineering appearance | Train assessors to enter narrative notes before OASIS item entries; EHR workflow design enforces narrative-first sequence where technically feasible |
| Late entries created to add clinical justification for OASIS responses after audit finding | Documentation integrity violation; potential fraud | Compliance Officer notification required for sequencing errors; late entry attestation distinguishes genuine lateness from post-hoc justification |
| Paper documentation during EHR outage not transcribed within 24 hours of restoration | Documentation gap; audit trail interruption | Outage-specific protocol with mandatory 24-hour transcription timeline; IT Director monitors restoration and triggers transcription protocol |

# CL-OA-018 — Clinician Competency Validation for OASIS Assessment
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-018 |
| Policy Title | Clinician Competency Validation for OASIS Assessment |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the complete validated competency assessment process — including all assessment instruments, performance standards, evaluation methodologies, evaluator qualifications, documentation requirements, remediation protocols, and ongoing competency maintenance standards — for all clinicians authorized to independently conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy is the operational companion to CL-OA-003 (OASIS Clinician Authorization & Competency), which defines the authorization structure and the OASIS Competency Program curriculum. CL-OA-018 defines how competency is measured, what tools are used to measure it, what passing standards apply, who is qualified to evaluate, and what happens when an assessor does not meet competency standards.
The distinction between having completed a training program and having demonstrated competency is clinically and legally significant. An assessor who has sat through an OASIS training module has met a training attendance requirement. An assessor who has demonstrated OASIS competency through validated performance evaluation has met a clinical governance standard. Only the latter qualifies an assessor to independently produce OASIS assessments that are submitted to the federal government as the basis for Medicare payment. This policy establishes the standards that distinguish training attendance from demonstrated competency.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all registered nurses who are candidates for OASIS assessor authorization, all currently authorized OASIS assessors, the Director of Nursing who serves as the designated Competency Evaluator, and the OASIS Quality Reviewer who has evaluator responsibilities for certain competency domains.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All clinicians must demonstrate competency across the domains defined in Section 5 before being authorized to independently conduct OASIS assessments. Competency demonstration is distinct from training completion — it requires performance evaluation against defined standards, not merely attendance at or completion of training content.
4.2 Competency shall be evaluated by the Director of Nursing or a designated evaluator who: (a) holds current OASIS assessor authorization; (b) has administered the specific competency evaluation instruments used in this policy for at least 12 months; (c) has been designated in writing by the Director of Nursing as qualified to conduct competency evaluations for the specific competency domain being assessed.
4.3 Competency evaluation results — including all scores, evaluator observations, and determination of pass or fail — shall be documented using the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) and filed in each assessor's personnel file per HR-WM-007.
4.4 Annual competency re-validation is required for all authorized assessors. The re-validation process is abbreviated compared to the initial validation but must include all components defined in Section 6.2. An assessor whose annual re-validation is not completed by their authorization anniversary date is in lapsed authorization status per CL-OA-003 and may not independently conduct OASIS assessments until re-validation is completed.
4.5 An assessor who fails any single competency domain during initial or annual validation shall be immediately suspended from independent OASIS assessment pending remediation and re-evaluation of the failed domain. The assessor may conduct OASIS assessments only in a supervised capacity during the suspension period.
4.6 An assessor who fails the same competency domain twice in any 12-month period shall have their OASIS assessor authorization revoked and shall be required to complete the full initial OASIS Competency Program before re-applying for authorization.
## 5. Competency Domains
The following seven competency domains must be demonstrated for initial authorization and maintained through annual re-validation:

| Domain | Description | Evaluation Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain 1: OASIS Regulatory Framework | Understanding of 42 CFR § 484.55, CMS OASIS-E2 requirements, PDGM linkage, and quality measure implications | Written knowledge assessment |
| Domain 2: Assessment Time Points and Deadlines | Knowledge of all OASIS time point triggers, assessment windows, operational targets, and regulatory deadlines | Written knowledge assessment; case scenario questions |
| Domain 3: Standardized Tool Administration | Correct administration of BIMS (all three components in sequence), PHQ-2/PHQ-9 (all items, correct response scale), and MAHC-10 (where applicable) | Direct observation performance evaluation using standardized patient simulation |
| Domain 4: Standardized Tool Scoring | Correct calculation of component scores and totals for BIMS and PHQ-2/PHQ-9; correct score-to-OASIS-response mapping | Written scoring exercise using provided simulated patient response sets |
| Domain 5: OASIS Item-Level Coding | Accurate application of CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual response selection rules for GG functional items, wound items, and behavioral health items | Case study coding exercise with scored response key |
| Domain 6: Documentation and Substantiation | Adequate documentation of clinical findings to support OASIS item responses per CL-OA-007; narrative-OASIS consistency | Documentation review of supervised SOC assessment |
| Domain 7: Supervised OASIS Assessment | Completion of a comprehensive SOC OASIS assessment in the physical presence of the Director of Nursing or designated evaluator | Direct observation with real-time feedback and post-assessment coding review |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Initial Competency Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Before scheduling initial competency evaluation, verify that the candidate has completed all modules of the OASIS Competency Program per CL-OA-003. Competency evaluation shall not be administered before program completion. | Before scheduling evaluation. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Written Knowledge Assessment covering Domains 1 and 2 (Appendix B). The assessment consists of 50 multiple-choice questions with a time limit of 90 minutes. Each question addresses a specific knowledge area from the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, assessment time point rules, or PDGM linkage concepts. All questions have a single correct answer determined by the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. Passing score: ≥85%. | At the scheduled evaluation session. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Standardized Tool Performance Evaluation for Domain 3 (Appendix C). The candidate demonstrates complete administration of: (a) the BIMS to a standardized patient (simulation model or role-play partner) including the word repetition component, all three temporal orientation questions, a pause activity, and the word recall component in the correct sequence; (b) the PHQ-2 with correct verbatim question reading and correct response scale; (c) the PHQ-9 continuation from PHQ-2 (if PHQ-2 score ≥3 in the scenario). The evaluator rates each step of each tool using the pass/fail tool-specific checklist in Appendix C. Passing standard: all steps rated "Satisfactory" or "Acceptable with Minor Deviation"; any step rated "Unsatisfactory" constitutes a domain failure. | At the evaluation session, following the written assessment. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Standardized Tool Scoring Exercise for Domain 4 (Appendix D). The candidate receives 5 complete simulated patient BIMS response sets and 5 complete simulated PHQ-9 response sets. The candidate calculates component scores and totals for each, and determines the correct OASIS item response for each. Passing standard: ≥90% of scoring exercises completed correctly with correct score-to-response mapping. | At the evaluation session, following the performance evaluation. |
| 6.1.5 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the OASIS Item-Level Coding Case Study Exercise for Domain 5 (Appendix E). The candidate receives 3 complete clinical case vignettes and is required to code specified OASIS items for each case using the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual as the reference. The answer key is derived from the current Guidance Manual. Passing standard: ≥85% of coded items match the answer key. | At the evaluation session. |
| 6.1.6 | Director of Nursing | Arrange the Supervised SOC Assessment for Domains 6 and 7. The candidate conducts a complete SOC assessment on a real patient in the Director of Nursing's or designated evaluator's physical presence. The evaluator observes the entire assessment without intervening unless a patient safety concern arises, and reviews the completed OASIS narrative and item selections immediately following the assessment. The evaluator rates each domain using the Supervised Assessment Rating Form (Appendix F). Passing standard per domain: overall rating of "Meets Standard" or better. | Within 14 calendar days of completing Domains 1–5 with passing scores. |
| 6.1.7 | Director of Nursing | Review all domain evaluation results. If the candidate has passed all 7 domains, authorize the assessor per CL-OA-003. If the candidate has failed any domain, initiate the remediation process per Section 6.3. Complete the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) and file in the personnel file. | Within 5 business days of completing all evaluation components. |

### 6.2 — Annual Re-Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Alert each assessor 60 days before their authorization anniversary date that annual re-validation is required. Schedule the re-validation to be completed before the anniversary date. | 60 days before anniversary date per CL-OA-003. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Annual Re-Validation Written Assessment covering: (a) any changes to the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual since the prior re-validation; (b) items where the assessor had documented accuracy deficiencies in the prior year's monthly audit results; (c) high-risk coding areas (GG functional items, wound staging, BIMS scoring). 25-item assessment; minimum 85% passing score. | At the annual re-validation session. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer BIMS Direct Observation Re-Demonstration (mandatory annually regardless of prior-year accuracy): the assessor demonstrates the complete BIMS administration to a simulated patient using the Domain 3 evaluation checklist (Appendix C). Passing standard: same as initial. | At the annual re-validation session. |
| 6.2.4 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor had any Domain 4 (scoring accuracy) or Domain 5 (item-level coding) deficiency in the prior year's monthly audits (any item category below 90%): administer the targeted re-validation exercise for the deficient domain(s) using the same instruments as the initial evaluation. If no prior-year deficiency, Domains 4 and 5 re-validation is waived for the current annual cycle. | At the annual re-validation session if deficiency present. |
| 6.2.5 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor had no prior-year deficiencies in Domains 6 and 7 (documentation and supervised assessment), the Supervised SOC Assessment is waived for the annual re-validation. If a Domain 6 or 7 deficiency was identified in the prior year's audits, a supervised assessment is required. | At the annual re-validation session if deficiency present. |
| 6.2.6 | Director of Nursing | Complete the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) for the annual re-validation and file in the personnel file. Update the Authorized Assessor Roster per CL-OA-003. | Within 5 business days of re-validation completion. |

### 6.3 — Remediation Protocol for Domain Failure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Immediately upon identifying a domain failure during initial or annual validation: (a) suspend the assessor from independent OASIS assessment; (b) notify the assessor in writing of the specific domain failure, the performance standard not met, and the remediation requirements; (c) arrange supervised assessment coverage for the assessor's caseload. | Within 24 hours of domain failure identification. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Develop a targeted remediation plan for the failed domain: (a) for Domain 1/2 written assessment failure — assign additional reading from the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual chapters covering the failed areas; re-administer the written assessment or a comparable alternate assessment within 14 calendar days; (b) for Domain 3 tool administration failure — provide direct hands-on coaching with repeat demonstration practice; re-evaluate within 14 calendar days; (c) for Domain 4/5 coding failures — provide focused coding practice exercises with answer key review; re-administer the failed exercise within 14 calendar days; (d) for Domain 6/7 documentation/supervised assessment failure — provide documentation standard review and additional supervised assessments before re-evaluation; re-evaluate supervised assessment within 21 calendar days. | Within 5 business days of domain failure; remediation plan documented. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Re-administer the failed domain evaluation after remediation. Passing standard is the same as the initial evaluation. If the assessor passes the re-evaluation, restore authorization per CL-OA-003. Document the remediation and re-evaluation in the OASIS Competency Validation Record. | Within 14–21 calendar days of remediation initiation per domain type. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor fails the re-evaluation of the same domain: revoke OASIS assessor authorization. The assessor must complete the full initial OASIS Competency Program before re-applying for authorization. Document the revocation in the OASIS Competency Validation Record and update the Authorized Assessor Roster. Notify HR per HR-ER-002 regarding employment implications. | Within 24 hours of second domain failure; HR notification within 5 business days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS Competency Validation Record — initial | All domain scores, evaluator observations, pass/fail determination | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Personnel file per HR-WM-007 | At initial authorization; retained minimum 7 years |

| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix G | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All assessors have current, documented competency validation | Personnel file and Authorized Assessor Roster audit | 100% — zero assessors with expired or undocumented competency |
| Initial competency validation precedes first independent assessment | Authorized Assessor Roster first authorization date vs. first locked assessment date | 100% |
| Annual re-validation completed before authorization anniversary | Roster anniversary date vs. re-validation completion date | 100% — zero lapsed authorizations |
| Domain failure triggers immediate suspension | Audit trail of suspension and OASIS access restriction | 100% |
| Second same-domain failure triggers authorization revocation | Documentation audit | 100% |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual re-validation treated as a brief attestation without substantive evaluation | Competency degradation over time; OASIS accuracy deterioration | Annual re-validation requires BIMS direct observation as mandatory minimum plus targeted domain re-evaluation based on prior-year audit findings |
| Remediation period assessments not supervised | Unsupported OASIS assessments during suspension period | EHR access restriction during suspension period; Director of Nursing arranges supervised coverage |
| Competency validation records not filed in personnel files | Survey deficiency; inability to demonstrate assessor qualification | Personnel file audit quarterly per HR-WM-007; HR Director quarterly cross-check |
