## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the structured pre-submission quality review process that every authorized OASIS assessor at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. must complete for every OASIS assessment at every applicable time point before locking and transmitting the assessment to the CMS repository. The pre-submission quality review is the final quality control gate between the assessor's work product and the federal data system — the last opportunity to identify and correct errors before they become compliance deficiencies, payment classification errors, or quality measure distortions.
The pre-submission quality review is not a post-completion re-read. It is a structured, checklist-driven systematic review that verifies specific, predefined quality criteria for each major OASIS item category. Its purpose is to catch the categories of errors that are most common, most consequential, and most detectable at the pre-submission stage: items left at default values without clinical justification; internal inconsistencies between related item groups; items where the documented evidence does not support the coded response; standardized tool scores that are inconsistent with the coded OASIS item; and homebound status documentation that does not meet the standards of CL-CA-005.
This policy establishes the complete Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A), the required completion standards for each checklist section, the documentation requirements for the completed review, and the escalation process when the review identifies issues that cannot be resolved before the OASIS completion deadline.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, and the Director of Nursing. The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) is the operative document of this policy — no assessment shall be locked without the checklist being completed.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every OASIS assessment at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall undergo a structured pre-submission quality review using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) before the assessment is locked in the EHR. The review shall be conducted by the assessing RN as a self-review after completing all OASIS item selections and all supporting narrative documentation.
4.2 The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist is a required clinical record document — its completion shall be recorded in the EHR OASIS quality review module with the assessor's electronic signature and the date and time of completion. An OASIS assessment that is locked without a completed, authenticated checklist is a documentation compliance deficiency.
4.3 When the pre-submission quality review identifies a correctable issue — an item response that is not supported by documentation, an internal inconsistency, a missing required element — the assessor shall correct the issue before locking the assessment. Do not lock the assessment with known uncorrected issues.
4.4 When the pre-submission quality review identifies an issue that cannot be immediately resolved by the assessing RN — for example, an ambiguous clinical situation requiring Director of Nursing adjudication, or a missing document that requires clinical judgment about its absence — the assessor shall document the issue in the checklist, escalate to the Director of Nursing, and delay locking until the issue is resolved or the Director of Nursing authorizes locking with the documented limitation.
4.5 The OASIS Quality Reviewer's Level 2 review per CL-OA-002 shall include verification that the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist was completed for the reviewed assessment and that the checklist findings are consistent with the Level 2 reviewer's independent assessment of the assessment quality.
4.6 The pre-submission quality review is the assessor's responsibility and accountability. It is not a substitute for the OASIS Quality Reviewer's Level 2 review — both are required. The pre-submission review catches issues the assessor can self-identify; the Level 2 review provides independent expert validation.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review | The structured, checklist-driven review of a completed OASIS assessment conducted by the assessing RN before locking, using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) to verify completeness, internal consistency, evidence substantiation, and homebound documentation adequacy. |
| Default Value | The pre-populated or default response option that the EHR may apply to an OASIS item before the assessor makes a selection. An item left at its default value without a clinical basis for that value is not a valid assessment response. |
| Internal Inconsistency | A contradiction between two or more OASIS item responses within the same assessment that cannot simultaneously be true given the patient's clinical presentation — for example, coding a patient as requiring maximal assistance for all GG mobility items while coding them as having no pressure injuries, without clinical explanation. |
| Completeness Check | The verification that all OASIS items applicable to the current assessment time point have been addressed with a valid response — either a clinician-selected response or a documented not-applicable designation with clinical basis. |
| Evidence Check | The verification that the clinical narrative in the assessment contains documentation that supports the coded OASIS response for each item reviewed, per the substantiation standards of CL-OA-007. |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist | The structured form (Appendix A) that the assessing RN completes for every OASIS assessment before locking, systematically verifying quality criteria for each major OASIS item category. |

## 6. Pre-Submission Quality Review — Required Review Sections
The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) consists of the following five review sections, each addressing a distinct quality dimension:
### Section 1 — Completeness Check
Purpose: Verify that all applicable OASIS items for the current time point have been addressed with a clinician-selected response.
Required Actions:
Open the CMS OASIS-E2 item applicability table for the applicable time point (SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, or DC).
For each applicable item, verify that a response has been selected and that the response is not a default value that was not reviewed.
For any item left blank, not applicable, or at a default value, verify that the clinical record contains a documented basis for that status (the patient's condition makes the item genuinely not applicable; the patient could not complete the required assessment).
Flag and correct any item that appears incomplete without a documented clinical basis.
Checklist Recording: Rate each item category as: ☐ Complete ☐ Incomplete — Issue Identified and Corrected ☐ Incomplete — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 2 — Internal Consistency Check
Purpose: Verify that logically related OASIS items produce a coherent clinical picture without internal contradictions.
Required Item-Pair Consistency Reviews:

| Item Pair | Consistency Check |
| --- | --- |
| GG0130 (Self-Care) and GG0170 (Mobility) | The overall pattern of self-care and mobility independence should be clinically coherent — a patient who requires maximal assistance for all self-care activities would typically also require assistance for most mobility activities, absent a specific clinical explanation for the discrepancy |
| M1700 (Cognitive Function / BIMS score) and M2020 (Oral Medication Management) | A patient with severe cognitive impairment (BIMS 0–7) would not be expected to independently manage complex oral medication regimens — a discrepancy between high cognitive impairment and high medication management independence requires clinical explanation |
| M1700 (Cognitive Function) and M1710/M1720 (Confusion/Anxiety frequency) | The frequency of confusion/anxiety behavioral items should be consistent with the overall cognitive function rating |
| GG mobility items and M1311 (Pressure Injury presence) | A patient with high GG mobility independence (independent ambulation, transfer) would not typically develop pressure injuries attributable to immobility — any pressure injury in a highly mobile patient requires documented clinical explanation |
| Respiratory severity items and GG0170 mobility activity items | A patient with the highest respiratory impairment (dyspnea at rest) would be expected to have significant GG mobility limitations — a highly mobile patient also coded as having severe resting dyspnea requires clinical documentation of how the patient achieves that mobility level despite the respiratory severity |

Checklist Recording: Rate each pair as: ☐ Consistent ☐ Inconsistency Identified and Resolved (resolution documented in narrative) ☐ Inconsistency — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 3 — Evidence Substantiation Check
Purpose: Verify that the clinical narrative contains documented evidence supporting the coded OASIS response for each high-risk item category, per CL-OA-007.
Required Evidence Checks:

| OASIS Item Category | Evidence Substantiation Verification |
| --- | --- |
| GG0130 Self-Care items | Narrative contains activity-specific observation descriptions for each sub-item coded (not general mobility statements) |
| GG0170 Mobility items | Narrative contains activity-specific observation descriptions including assistance level and environmental context |
| M1311–M1324 Pressure Injury items | Narrative contains direct wound observation documentation (NPIAP stage, measurements, wound bed, drainage, periwound) — dressing removal confirmed |
| M1340–M1342 Surgical Wound items | Narrative contains surgical wound observation documentation — wound type, stage, character |
| M1700 Cognitive Function | Narrative contains BIMS component scores (A, B, C) and total score — not just total; administration confirmed |
| M1730/M1750 Depressive Feelings | Narrative contains PHQ-2 item scores and total; PHQ-9 item scores and total if PHQ-2 ≥3 |
| M2001 Drug Regimen Review | Narrative documents review methodology, medications reviewed, issues found or not found |
| Homebound Status | Narrative documents both CMS homebound criteria with patient-specific functional language |
| Skilled Need | Narrative documents the clinical justification for each ordered skilled discipline |

Checklist Recording: For each item category: ☐ Adequate substantiation documented ☐ Substantiation gap identified and corrected ☐ Substantiation gap — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 4 — Standardized Tool Score Consistency Check
Purpose: Verify that standardized tool scores are documented correctly and map to the corresponding OASIS item response.
Required Score-to-Response Verifications:

| Tool | Verification Required |
| --- | --- |
| BIMS total score → M1700 | BIMS total (Component A + B + C = Total) maps to the correct M1700 response: 13–15 = Cognitively Intact; 8–12 = Moderately Impaired; 0–7 = Severely Impaired. Arithmetic verified. |
| PHQ-2 total → PHQ-9 required? | PHQ-2 total ≥3 requires PHQ-9 administration. If PHQ-2 ≥3 and PHQ-9 not documented, flag immediately. |
| PHQ-9 total → M1730/M1750 | PHQ-9 total maps to the correct M1730/M1750 response per CMS guidance. Arithmetic verified (sum of 9 items). |
| PHQ-9 Item 9 | If PHQ-9 Item 9 score ≥1, suicidality assessment documentation present in clinical record. |

Checklist Recording: For each tool: ☐ Score arithmetic correct; response mapping correct ☐ Arithmetic/mapping error identified and corrected ☐ PHQ-9 required but not administered — immediate action required before locking
### Section 5 — Look-Back Period and Time-Point Accuracy Check
Purpose: Verify that look-back periods were correctly applied and that the assessment reflects the correct OASIS time point.
Required Verifications:
Confirm the assessment time point code is correct for the clinical event (SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, or DC).
For each look-back item category, verify that the look-back window was measured from the assessment date — not from the discharge date or any other reference date.
For post-hospitalization SOC/ROC assessments, verify that the look-back window correctly encompasses the inpatient period per CL-OA-010.
Verify that point-in-time items (GG items at SOC/ROC) reflect the patient's status at the assessment visit — not at any other time point.
For RECERT assessments, verify the assessment date falls within the Day 56–60 window.
Checklist Recording: For each verification: ☐ Confirmed ☐ Issue identified and corrected ☐ Issue requiring Director of Nursing consultation
## 7. Procedures
### 7.1 — Pre-Submission Review Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.1.1 | Assessing RN | After completing all OASIS item selections and all supporting narrative documentation, open the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) in the EHR. Do not lock the assessment before opening the checklist. | Before locking. |
| 7.1.2 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 1 (Completeness Check) by reviewing each applicable OASIS item for the current time point. Allow a minimum of 5 minutes for this section — it requires opening the CMS item applicability table and reviewing each item. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.3 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 2 (Internal Consistency Check) by reviewing each required item-pair. For each pair, look at both coded responses simultaneously and assess whether they produce a coherent clinical picture. Allow a minimum of 5 minutes for this section. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.4 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 3 (Evidence Substantiation Check) by opening the assessment narrative alongside the OASIS item responses and verifying that each high-risk item category has adequate narrative documentation. Allow a minimum of 10 minutes for this section — it is the most detailed review. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.5 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 4 (Standardized Tool Score Consistency Check) by re-calculating tool totals from the documented component scores and verifying that the calculated totals match the coded OASIS responses. Allow a minimum of 3 minutes for this section. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.6 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 5 (Look-Back Period and Time-Point Accuracy Check) by verifying time point code, look-back windows, and point-in-time application. Allow a minimum of 3 minutes. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.7 | Assessing RN | Review the overall pre-submission quality status. If all sections are rated "Confirmed" or "Issue Identified and Corrected," sign and submit the checklist and proceed to locking. If any section has a "Director of Nursing Consultation Required" flag, notify the Director of Nursing before locking. | After all sections are completed. |
| 7.1.8 | Assessing RN | Lock the OASIS assessment immediately after submitting the checklist and, if required, receiving Director of Nursing authorization. Do not delay locking after the checklist is complete — unnecessary delay beyond the checklist completion creates additional operational target risk per CL-OA-001 and CL-OA-015. | Immediately after checklist submission and Director of Nursing authorization (if required). |

### 7.2 — Issue Resolution During Pre-Submission Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.2.1 | Assessing RN | When a correctable issue is identified during any checklist section: (a) correct the OASIS item response or the narrative documentation as appropriate; (b) re-verify the affected section of the checklist after correction; (c) document the issue and correction in the checklist issue field. | During the pre-submission review. |
| 7.2.2 | Assessing RN | When an issue requiring Director of Nursing consultation is identified: (a) document the issue in the checklist consultation field; (b) notify the Director of Nursing immediately by telephone or secure message; (c) do not lock the assessment pending Director of Nursing response. | Before locking; Director of Nursing notification immediately. |
| 7.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Upon notification of a consultation-required issue: respond within 4 hours during business hours or at the earliest practicable time outside business hours. Provide specific clinical adjudication guidance. Document the guidance provided in the EHR communication notes. | Within 4 hours during business hours. |

### 7.3 — OASIS Quality Reviewer Checklist Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.3.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | During every Level 2 review per CL-OA-002: (a) verify that the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist is present in the EHR for the reviewed assessment; (b) review the checklist for completeness — all five sections completed; (c) assess whether any issues identified in the checklist were appropriately resolved; (d) independently verify Section 2 (internal consistency) and Section 3 (evidence substantiation) using the Quality Reviewer's own assessment. | Within the Level 2 review timeline. |
| 7.3.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If the Level 2 review identifies issues not flagged in the pre-submission checklist, document the finding in the OASIS Quality Review Log and classify the assessment as having an inadequate pre-submission review — initiate the correction process per CL-OA-002 and provide targeted feedback to the assessing RN. | Within 24 hours of finding. |

### 7.4 — Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment locked without completed Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist | Director of Nursing identifies during monthly audit | Director of Nursing directs the assessing RN to retroactively complete the checklist. If the retroactive review identifies unresolved issues, initiate OASIS correction per CL-OA-002. Document corrective counseling. | Retroactive checklist within 5 business days; correction within 10 business days. |
| Pre-submission review consistently takes less than 15 minutes (below the section-minimum time allocations) | Director of Nursing identifies through EHR timestamp comparison | Director of Nursing assesses whether the review is being conducted with adequate rigor. If the timestamp analysis suggests the review is perfunctory (e.g., under 5 minutes total), provide corrective guidance and consider requiring supervised pre-submission reviews for the affected assessor. | Corrective guidance within 7 calendar days. |
| Pre-submission review identifies a patient safety concern (e.g., unidentified adverse drug reaction, new pressure injury not in the plan of care) | Assessing RN follows applicable clinical protocol simultaneously | Pre-submission review identification of a clinical concern triggers both the clinical response (physician notification per applicable policy) and the OASIS correction/update. The assessment should not be locked until the clinical response has been initiated and the OASIS reflects the current clinical picture. | Clinical response immediately; OASIS update within the applicable deadline. |

## 9. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 9.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist completed and authenticated before every OASIS lock | EHR quality review module completion log | ≥98% of locked assessments with completed, authenticated checklist |
| All five checklist sections completed for each assessment | Checklist completeness audit | ≥98% of checklists with all five sections completed |
| Issues identified in checklist are appropriately resolved before locking | OASIS Quality Reviewer Level 2 review finding correlation | ≥95% of issues identified in checklists have documented resolutions |
| Assessments with consultation-required flags are not locked before Director of Nursing authorization | EHR lock timestamp vs. Director of Nursing communication note timestamp | 100% |
| Level 2 review does not identify material issues absent from pre-submission checklist | Quality Review Log audit — new issues identified at Level 2 not present in pre-submission checklist | ≤5% of Level 2 reviews identify material issues not flagged in pre-submission checklist |

### 9.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting OASIS validation surveys will request evidence of the agency's OASIS quality assurance process. The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist — when consistently completed and when it demonstrates a pattern of assessors actively identifying and resolving issues before submission — is direct evidence of a functioning OASIS quality governance program. An agency that cannot demonstrate a systematic pre-submission review process has no structural mechanism for preventing OASIS errors that are detectable before submission.
ADR auditors will look for evidence that errors that could have been caught before submission were not caught — particularly internal consistency errors (BIMS score inconsistent with M1700 coding) and substantiation gaps (GG items with no activity-specific observation documentation). These are precisely the errors a properly conducted pre-submission review should catch. When an ADR auditor finds them, the absence of a documented pre-submission review suggests the agency lacked the quality governance to prevent them.
### 9.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-submission review treated as a checkbox exercise without genuine item-by-item review | Errors that should be caught before submission are not caught; Level 2 review finds issues that were reviewable at pre-submission | Time allocation minimums in Section 6; Director of Nursing reviews checklist completion times in monthly audit |
| Section 4 (tool score consistency) skipped because assessor believes scores are correct | PHQ/BIMS scoring errors not caught; M1700/M1730 miscoding | Make Section 4 mandatory with required score recalculation; OASIS Quality Reviewer validates score recalculation at Level 2 |
| Assessor locks assessment before completing Section 3 (evidence substantiation) because the narrative feels adequate | Substantiation gaps not identified; OASIS locked without supporting narrative | EHR workflow requires Section 3 completion rating before lock button is enabled |
| No documentation that the checklist was completed — assessors sign but do not complete | No evidence of compliance with the review requirement | EHR checklist requires each section to be rated before the attestation signature can be applied |

## 11. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
11.1 All authorized OASIS assessors shall receive training on the Pre-Submission Quality Review process within their initial OASIS Competency Program and at each annual re-competency per CL-OA-003, including: the purpose and structure of each checklist section; the minimum time allocations for each section; the issue escalation process; and the consequences of locking an assessment without a completed checklist.
11.2 Training shall include a simulated pre-submission review exercise in which assessors complete the checklist for a case study OASIS assessment that intentionally contains issues in each of the five checklist sections — requiring assessors to identify the issues, document them, and apply the appropriate resolution.
11.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
11.4 The Director of Nursing shall maintain training completion records for all authorized assessors and shall report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of any training deadline.
## 12. Version Control
12.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
12.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
12.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
12.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

# CO-CP-001 — Corporate Compliance Program
## Policy Header

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the Corporate Compliance Program ("Program") for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Program is the agency's formal, systematic commitment to conducting all operations with integrity, in full conformity with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and the standards issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the Office of Inspector General (OIG), and all other regulatory bodies having jurisdiction over the agency's operations. The Program satisfies the requirements set forth in the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies and supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.100 (Condition of Participation: Compliance with Federal, State, and Local Laws) and the agency's obligation to maintain Medicare certification. The Program provides the structural foundation upon which all other compliance-related policies in the CO domain operate.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All Governing Body members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
The Agency Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Compliance Officer and Compliance Committee members
All full-time, part-time, per diem, and contracted employees
All volunteers performing services on behalf of the agency
All third-party vendors, contractors, and business associates who interact with agency operations, billing, or patient care
Note: This policy does not supersede any applicable federal or state law. Where this policy conflicts with a law or regulation, the more stringent requirement governs.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a fully operational Corporate Compliance Program that satisfies the seven foundational elements of an effective compliance program as defined by the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.
4.2 The seven required elements of the Program are:
Written policies, procedures, and standards of conduct
Designation of a Compliance Officer and Compliance Committee
Effective training and education
Effective lines of communication
Internal monitoring and auditing
Enforcement of standards and well-publicized disciplinary guidelines
Prompt response to detected offenses and development of corrective action
4.3 The Governing Body shall maintain ultimate accountability for the effectiveness of the Program and shall receive compliance reports at no less than quarterly intervals per policy GV-GB-001.
4.4 The Program shall be operationally independent. The Compliance Officer shall have direct reporting access to the Governing Body and shall not be subject to retaliation, pressure, or interference in performing compliance functions.
4.5 Participation in compliance training and adherence to the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) are conditions of continued employment and/or contract with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
4.6 The agency shall not employ or contract with any individual or entity that appears on the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) or the System for Award Management (SAM) exclusion database, per policy HR-TA-003.
4.7 All known or suspected violations of law, regulation, agency policy, or the Code of Conduct shall be reported promptly through mechanisms established in policy CO-CP-006 and investigated per policy CO-CP-007.
4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within scope within 14 calendar days.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Corporate Compliance Program | The formal, structured system of policies, procedures, oversight mechanisms, training, and accountability structures designed to prevent, detect, and correct violations of law, regulation, or ethical standards. |
| Compliance Officer | The individual designated by the Governing Body with authority and independence to operate the Corporate Compliance Program, per policy CO-CP-002. |
| Compliance Committee | The multi-disciplinary body chaired by the Compliance Officer that provides operational oversight of the Program, per policy CO-CP-003. |
| OIG | Office of Inspector General of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — the federal body responsible for combating fraud, waste, and abuse in federal health care programs. |
| LEIE | List of Excluded Individuals/Entities — the OIG database of individuals and entities excluded from participation in federal health care programs. |
| SAM | System for Award Management — the federal database that includes parties excluded from receiving federal contracts, certain subcontracts, and certain federal financial and non-financial assistance and benefits. |
| False Claims Act | Federal law (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733) imposing civil and criminal liability for knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims to the federal government. |
| Fraud, Waste, and Abuse (FWA) | Fraud: intentional deception to obtain unauthorized benefits. Waste: overutilization or misuse of resources. Abuse: practices inconsistent with sound fiscal, business, or medical practices. |
| Code of Conduct | The written document that defines the ethical standards, behavioral expectations, and legal obligations of all workforce members, per policy CO-CP-004. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Program Establishment and Governance

| 6.1.2 | Governing Body | Designate a qualified Compliance Officer per the requirements of policy CO-CP-002. Document the designation in Governing Body minutes. | Prior to agency operation; within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Establish and chair the Compliance Committee per policy CO-CP-003. | Within 30 calendar days of Compliance Officer designation. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a current written description of the Program, its seven elements, the authority of the Compliance Officer, and the Program's reporting structure. | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.1.5 | Administrator | Ensure adequate resources are allocated in the annual budget to support Program operations including staffing, training, auditing, and technology, per policy FN-FP-005. | Annually, prior to budget approval. |

| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all workforce members have access to the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) in a readable format at the time of hire and upon each revision. | At hire; upon each revision. |

| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all workforce members complete annual compliance refresher training per policy CO-CP-008. | Annually; completed within 30 calendar days of the start of each calendar year. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain training completion logs and report compliance to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |

The report must address: (a) active compliance investigations (without compromising confidentiality); (b) audit findings and trends; (c) regulatory changes affecting the agency; (d) training completion rates; (e) exclusion screening status; (f) corrective action plan status. | 7 calendar days before each quarterly Governing Body meeting. |

The work plan shall prioritize: (a) billing and claims accuracy; (b) OASIS data integrity; (c) medical necessity documentation; (d) exclusion screening compliance; (e) policy acknowledgment rates; (f) fraud and abuse risk areas identified by OIG Work Plan. | Approved at first Compliance Committee meeting of each calendar year. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct or commission audits per the annual work plan and document all findings, methodology, sample sizes, and corrective actions, per policy CO-RA-002. | Per audit work plan schedule. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Present audit findings and status of corrective actions at each quarterly Compliance Committee meeting and Governing Body meeting. | Quarterly. |

### 6.6 Enforcement and Discipline

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Compliance Officer / HR Director | Ensure disciplinary standards for compliance violations are defined in the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) and Employee Handbook. Disciplinary standards must be consistently applied without exception for seniority or role. | Continuously. |
| 6.6.2 | HR Director | Apply progressive discipline for compliance violations per policy HR-ER-002. All disciplinary actions related to compliance violations shall be reported to the Compliance Officer within 5 calendar days. | Within 5 calendar days of disciplinary action. |
| 6.6.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a disciplinary action log for all compliance-related violations. Report aggregate trends to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |

### 6.7 Response to Detected Offenses

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.7.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receipt of a compliance report or self-identified concern, initiate investigation per policy CO-CP-007 within 7 calendar days. | Within 7 calendar days of receipt. |
| 6.7.2 | Compliance Officer | If investigation confirms an overpayment, initiate refund process per policy FN-BC-004 within the CMS 60-day repayment window. | Within 60 calendar days of identification. |
| 6.7.3 | Compliance Officer | Develop and implement corrective action plans for all confirmed violations per policy QA-AE-003. | Within 14 calendar days of confirmation. |
| 6.7.4 | Compliance Officer | Determine whether voluntary self-disclosure to OIG, CMS, or other regulatory bodies is required. Engage legal counsel for any disclosure determination. | Within 30 calendar days of confirmed violation. |

| 6.8.2 | Governing Body | Review the annual Program effectiveness assessment and direct any structural improvements. Document review and directives in meeting minutes. | Annually at Q1 meeting. |
| 6.8.3 | Compliance Officer | Update the Program description and all CO-domain policies as needed based on the effectiveness review. | Within 60 calendar days of Q1 meeting. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program is formally adopted by Governing Body. | Review of Governing Body minutes for adoption resolution. | Documented adoption on file at all times. |
| Compliance Officer is designated and functioning. | Review of designation documentation; Governing Body minutes. | Current designation documented; no vacancy exceeds 30 days without interim designee. |
| Annual audit work plan is approved. | Review of Compliance Committee minutes; work plan document. | Approved at Q1 Compliance Committee meeting; 100% of planned audits initiated. |
| Quarterly compliance reports submitted to Governing Body. | Review of report submission dates vs. quarterly meeting dates. | 100% of reports submitted at least 7 days before each meeting. |
| All workforce members complete annual compliance training. | Review of training completion logs. | 95% completion rate within 30 days of deadline; 100% within 45 days. |
| Investigations initiated within required timeframes. | Review of investigation log with initiation dates. | 100% initiated within 7 calendar days of report receipt. |
| Confirmed overpayments refunded within 60 days. | Review of refund documentation and identification dates. | 100% compliance with 60-day repayment rule. |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points and Mitigation

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program exists on paper but is not operationally active. | OIG and CMS will treat a non-functional Program as equivalent to having no Program. | Compliance Officer must demonstrate active operations through documented audits, meeting minutes, and training records. |
| Compliance Officer reports to Administrator rather than directly to Governing Body. | Independence is compromised; conflicts of interest may be suppressed. | Governing Body must establish direct reporting line in the designation document. |
| Training completion rates fall below 95%. | OIG views low completion as evidence of a non-effective Program. | Compliance Officer must track and escalate to Governing Body Chair within 7 days of missed deadline. |
| Investigations are not documented in writing. | Undocumented investigations are treated as not having occurred in any subsequent audit or survey. | All investigations must be opened, tracked, and closed in writing per CO-CP-007. |

All Governing Body members shall receive orientation to this policy and the Program structure within 14 calendar days of appointment.
Training completion shall be tracked and reported to the Governing Body quarterly.

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the qualifications, designation process, authority, independence, reporting structure, and responsibilities of the Compliance Officer of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Compliance Officer is the individual designated by the Governing Body who holds primary accountability for the day-to-day operation of the Corporate Compliance Program established under policy CO-CP-001. This policy ensures that the agency satisfies the OIG requirement that an effective compliance program include a designated Compliance Officer with sufficient authority and operational independence to fulfill all compliance functions without conflict or interference.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Governing Body (as the designating authority)
The individual designated as Compliance Officer
The Administrator
Any individual serving in an interim Compliance Officer capacity
The Compliance Committee
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall designate a qualified Compliance Officer prior to agency operation and maintain that designation continuously thereafter.
4.2 The Compliance Officer shall be designated by the Governing Body and the designation shall be documented in Governing Body meeting minutes with the full Designation and Authority Letter (Appendix A).
4.3 The Compliance Officer shall have the authority, independence, and resources necessary to fulfill all compliance functions. No member of agency leadership — including the Administrator — shall have the authority to override, impede, or retaliate against the Compliance Officer's performance of their duties.
4.4 The Compliance Officer shall have a direct reporting line to the Governing Body. The Compliance Officer may also have an administrative reporting relationship to the Administrator for operational purposes, provided that this reporting relationship does not compromise the independence of the Compliance Officer.
4.5 Any vacancy in the Compliance Officer role shall be filled within 30 calendar days. An interim Compliance Officer shall be designated within 14 calendar days of a vacancy and documented in writing.
4.6 The Compliance Officer role shall not be combined with the role of Agency Administrator or any clinical role that would create a conflict of interest in performing compliance oversight functions.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Officer | The individual designated by the Governing Body to operate the Corporate Compliance Program, investigate compliance concerns, coordinate auditing and monitoring, and report directly to the Governing Body on all compliance matters. |
| Independence | The ability to conduct compliance oversight functions, investigations, and reporting without interference, pressure, or retaliation from any member of agency management or the Governing Body. |
| Designation | The formal act of the Governing Body appointing an individual to serve as Compliance Officer, documented in meeting minutes and the Designation and Authority Letter. |
| Interim Compliance Officer | An individual temporarily fulfilling Compliance Officer responsibilities during a vacancy, with full authority granted by the Governing Body. |
| Conflict of Interest | Any situation in which the Compliance Officer's personal, financial, or professional interests could reasonably be perceived to compromise the independent performance of compliance functions. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Minimum Qualifications

| Requirement | Standard |
| --- | --- |
| Education | Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent professional compliance experience may substitute. |
| Experience | Minimum 2 years of experience in healthcare compliance, regulatory affairs, or health care law; home health experience strongly preferred. |
| Knowledge | Working knowledge of: Medicare home health Conditions of Participation (42 CFR Part 484); OIG Compliance Program Guidance; HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules; False Claims Act; Anti-Kickback Statute; CMS billing requirements for home health. |
| Certification | Certified in Healthcare Compliance (CHC) through the Compliance Certification Board preferred; not required if experience standard is met. |
| Exclusion Screening | Must not appear on OIG LEIE or SAM exclusion lists at time of designation and must clear monthly screening thereafter per policy HR-TA-003. |
| Background | Must pass criminal background check per policy HR-TA-002. |

### 6.2 Designation Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Governing Body | Identify, evaluate, and select a qualified candidate for the Compliance Officer role. Evaluate qualifications against Section 6.1 minimum standards. | Prior to agency operation; within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.2.2 | Governing Body | Formally designate the Compliance Officer through a documented vote recorded in Governing Body meeting minutes. | At the Governing Body meeting at which designation is approved. |
| 6.2.3 | Governing Body Chair | Execute the Designation and Authority Letter (Appendix A) and provide a signed copy to: (a) the Compliance Officer; (b) the Administrator; (c) the governance file. | Within 7 calendar days of Governing Body vote. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Complete any required orientation to agency operations, the existing compliance program, and current regulatory requirements. | Within 30 calendar days of designation. |
| 6.2.5 | Compliance Officer | Conduct OIG/SAM exclusion screening on own name at designation and submit results to Governing Body Chair. | At designation; monthly thereafter. |

### 6.3 Authority and Responsibilities

| Authority/Responsibility | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Policy authority | Authority to draft, revise, and recommend approval of all CO-domain policies. |
| Investigation authority | Authority to initiate, conduct, or commission investigations of any compliance concern without prior approval from the Administrator. |
| Records access | Unrestricted access to all agency records, files, systems, and personnel necessary to conduct compliance functions, subject to applicable law. |
| Reporting access | Direct, unfiltered access to the Governing Body — may request a special Governing Body meeting at any time for matters of significant compliance concern. |
| Corrective action authority | Authority to direct implementation of compliance-related corrective action plans in coordination with the Administrator. |
| External reporting authority | Authority to consult legal counsel and, in consultation with the Governing Body, engage with OIG, CMS, or other regulatory bodies on compliance matters. |
| Staff interview authority | Authority to conduct confidential interviews of any workforce member in furtherance of compliance investigations or audits. |

### 6.4 Vacancy Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Notify all Governing Body members in writing within 48 hours of a Compliance Officer vacancy. | Within 48 hours of vacancy. |
| 6.4.2 | Governing Body | Designate an interim Compliance Officer in writing with full authority. The interim may not be the Administrator. | Within 14 calendar days of vacancy. |
| 6.4.3 | Governing Body | Initiate recruitment and selection process for permanent Compliance Officer. | Immediately upon vacancy; permanent appointment within 90 calendar days. |
| 6.4.4 | Governing Body Chair | Execute a new Designation and Authority Letter upon permanent appointment. | Within 7 calendar days of permanent appointment vote. |

### 6.5 Annual Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Governing Body | Conduct or commission an annual performance evaluation of the Compliance Officer in executive session. Evaluation must address: (a) Program effectiveness metrics from CO-CP-001; (b) audit completion rates; (c) training completion rates; (d) investigation timeliness; (e) reporting quality. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of end of each fiscal year. |
| 6.5.2 | Governing Body Chair | Document evaluation findings and any directives in executive session minutes. | At time of evaluation. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the structure, composition, responsibilities, meeting requirements, and documentation standards for the Compliance Committee of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Compliance Committee is the multi-disciplinary operational body that supports the Compliance Officer in implementing, monitoring, and evaluating the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001). The Committee provides the mechanism by which compliance risk, audit findings, regulatory changes, and corrective actions are reviewed at a cross-functional level and escalated to the Governing Body as appropriate.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all Compliance Committee members, all departments represented on the Committee, and all senior leadership personnel whose operational decisions affect the agency's compliance posture.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a functioning Compliance Committee, chaired by the Compliance Officer.
4.2 The Compliance Committee shall meet at minimum quarterly and shall maintain formal meeting minutes.
4.3 The Compliance Committee shall serve as the primary operational body for reviewing audit findings, monitoring corrective actions, evaluating training compliance, and preparing compliance reports to the Governing Body.
4.4 The Compliance Committee shall not have authority to override Governing Body directives or the Compliance Officer's independent compliance determinations.
4.5 Attendance at Compliance Committee meetings is a professional obligation for all designated members. Absence without advance notice and a designated alternate is not acceptable.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Committee | The multi-disciplinary body chaired by the Compliance Officer that provides operational oversight of the Corporate Compliance Program. |
| Quorum | A majority of standing Committee members must be present to conduct official business. |
| Compliance Risk | Any identified area of agency operations where regulatory violation, FWA exposure, billing error, clinical documentation deficiency, or privacy breach could occur. |
| Corrective Action Plan (CAP) | A documented plan with specific actions, responsible parties, and deadlines to remediate an identified compliance deficiency. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Committee Composition

| Standing Member | Role on Committee | Alternate Required? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compliance Officer | Chair | Yes — designated in writing |
| Administrator | Member | Yes |
| Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager | Member | Yes (Clinical Designee) |
| Revenue Cycle Director / CFO | Member | Yes |
| HR Director | Member | Yes |
| Risk Manager | Member | Yes |
| QAPI Coordinator | Member | Yes |
| IT Director / CISO | Member (may attend via video) | Yes |

Ad hoc members may be invited at the Chair's discretion for specific agenda items. Ad hoc members are not standing members and do not count toward quorum.
### 6.2 Committee Standing Agenda Items
Every Compliance Committee meeting shall include the following standing agenda items:

| # | Standing Agenda Item | Presenter | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Approval of prior meeting minutes | Chair | Minutes |
| 2 | Compliance Officer report (hotline, investigations update, regulatory changes) | Compliance Officer | Written report |
| 3 | Audit findings update (current period) | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Audit summary |
| 4 | Corrective action plan status review | CAP owners | CAP tracking log |
| 5 | Training completion rate report | Compliance Officer / HR | Training log summary |
| 6 | Exclusion screening status | Compliance Officer | Screening log |
| 7 | QAPI linkage items | QAPI Coordinator | QAPI report excerpt |
| 8 | Financial compliance indicators | Revenue Cycle Director | Revenue cycle summary |
| 9 | Regulatory change notifications | Compliance Officer | Regulatory update memo |
| 10 | Old business | All | Minutes |
| 11 | New business | All | Minutes |

### 6.3 Meeting Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Schedule Compliance Committee meetings for the calendar year no later than December 15 of the preceding year. | December 15 annually. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Distribute the meeting agenda to all members at least 5 calendar days before each meeting. | 5 calendar days prior. |
| 6.3.3 | Designated Secretary | Record formal minutes for each meeting (Appendix B template). Draft minutes distributed within 7 calendar days of meeting. | Draft within 7 calendar days; approved at next meeting. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer | Confirm quorum before conducting official business. If quorum not met, reschedule within 7 calendar days. | At start of each meeting. |
| 6.3.5 | Compliance Officer | Prepare a summary of each Compliance Committee meeting for inclusion in the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body. | Within 14 calendar days of each meeting. |

### 6.4 Escalation to Governing Body

| Condition | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-risk compliance deficiency identified | Compliance Officer notifies Governing Body in writing; special meeting may be requested. | Within 14 calendar days of identification. |
| Active investigation of fraud, waste, or abuse | Compliance Officer reports to Governing Body per CO-CP-001 Section 6.4.3. | At next quarterly meeting or sooner if risk warrants. |
| Corrective action plan not completed within deadline | Compliance Officer escalates to Governing Body with updated risk assessment. | At next quarterly meeting. |
| Regulatory agency contact or survey findings | Compliance Officer notifies Governing Body Chair within 24 hours; written summary within 5 days. | Within 24 hours of contact; written summary within 5 days. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the Code of Conduct and Ethics ("Code") of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Code defines the ethical standards, behavioral expectations, legal obligations, and prohibited conduct applicable to every individual who works for or on behalf of the agency. The Code is a foundational element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and reflects the agency's commitment to conducting all operations with honesty, integrity, and respect for patients, employees, referral partners, and payers.
## 3. Scope
This Code applies without exception to:
All Governing Body members
The Administrator and all senior leadership
All full-time, part-time, per diem, and contracted employees
All volunteers
All vendors, business associates, and contractors acting on behalf of the agency
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every individual within the scope of this policy shall conduct themselves in accordance with the standards of this Code at all times, whether on or off agency premises, when representing the agency in any capacity.
4.2 Adherence to this Code is a condition of employment or contract with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Violations are subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination or contract cancellation.
4.3 No one in a position of authority — including the Administrator or Governing Body members — may authorize conduct that violates this Code, applicable law, or regulation.
4.4 All workforce members have the affirmative obligation to report known or suspected violations of this Code through the mechanisms established in policy CO-CP-006.
4.5 No individual shall be retaliated against for good-faith reporting of a Code violation, per policy CO-CP-005.
## 5. Core Standards of Conduct
### 5.1 Patient-Centered Care and Dignity
All workforce members shall:
Treat every patient with dignity, respect, and compassion regardless of diagnosis, age, race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, or ability to pay.
Protect patient privacy and confidentiality at all times per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002.
Honor patient rights as defined in policy CL-PR-001.
Never exploit, abuse, neglect, or mistreat a patient. All suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation shall be reported immediately per policies CL-PR-006 and HR-ER-009.
Provide only services that are ordered, medically necessary, and within their scope of practice.
### 5.2 Integrity in Billing and Documentation
All workforce members shall:
Document clinical services accurately, completely, and truthfully.
Never document services not actually rendered, alter clinical records to support billing, or fail to document care that was provided.
Never submit or participate in the submission of a false claim to Medicare, Medicaid, or any other payer.
Report suspected billing irregularities or documentation falsification through CO-CP-006.
### 5.3 Conflict of Interest
All workforce members shall:
Disclose any personal, financial, or professional interest that could conflict with the agency's interests or their professional obligations.
Never allow a conflict of interest to influence a patient care decision, business decision, or compliance determination.
Governing Body members shall comply with the full conflict of interest management requirements of policy GV-GB-003.
### 5.4 Gifts, Gratuities, and Kickbacks
All workforce members shall:
Never accept or offer gifts, meals, entertainment, or gratuities that exceed $25 per occurrence or $50 annually from any patient, vendor, referral source, or competitor.
Never offer, pay, solicit, or receive anything of value in exchange for patient referrals, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b).
Report any solicitation of a kickback or improper referral arrangement immediately to the Compliance Officer.
### 5.5 Confidentiality and Privacy
All workforce members shall:
Never access, use, or disclose patient health information beyond the minimum necessary for their assigned duties.
Never discuss patient information in non-private settings (hallways, vehicles, social settings).
Never share login credentials, access patient records on behalf of another, or circumvent system access controls.
Report any known or suspected breach of patient information per policy CO-HP-003.
### 5.6 Workplace Respect and Anti-Harassment
All workforce members shall:
Treat colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates with respect and professionalism at all times.
Never engage in harassment, discrimination, or hostile conduct based on any protected characteristic.
Report harassment or discrimination per policy HR-ER-004.
### 5.7 Compliance with Laws and Regulations
All workforce members shall:
Comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and agency policies relevant to their role.
Never perform, authorize, or conceal any act that they know or reasonably believe violates applicable law.
Cooperate fully with all internal compliance audits and investigations.
### 5.8 Stewardship of Agency Resources
All workforce members shall:
Use agency resources (equipment, supplies, technology, time) only for legitimate agency business purposes.
Never misappropriate, steal, or misuse agency property.
Report waste, misuse, or misappropriation of agency resources through CO-CP-006.
### 5.9 Social Media and Public Communications
All workforce members shall:
Never post patient information, clinical photographs, or identifiable patient details on any social media platform.
Never make public statements that misrepresent the agency's services, credentials, or compliance status.
Comply with policy IT-UP-003 for all social media and public communications.
## 6. Reporting Violations
6.1 All workforce members have an affirmative obligation to report suspected violations of this Code, applicable law, or agency policy.
6.2 Reports may be made through any of the following mechanisms (per policy CO-CP-006):
Direct contact with the Compliance Officer
Agency compliance hotline (anonymous option available)
Direct contact with the Governing Body Chair (for matters involving the Compliance Officer or Administrator)
6.3 Reports may be made anonymously. Anonymous reports will be investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided.
6.4 No individual will be retaliated against for making a good-faith compliance report, per policy CO-CP-005.
## 7. Consequences of Violations

| Severity Level | Examples | Potential Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 — Minor | Unintentional policy deviation; minor documentation error (without billing impact); failure to attend required training by deadline. | Documented counseling; mandatory retraining; corrective action plan. |
| Level 2 — Moderate | Repeated policy violations; unauthorized PHI disclosure; gift acceptance above threshold; failure to report a known violation. | Written warning; performance improvement plan; suspension; retraining. |
| Level 3 — Serious | Fraudulent billing; falsification of records; patient abuse or neglect; kickback participation; retaliation against a reporter; intentional HIPAA violation. | Immediate suspension pending investigation; termination; regulatory reporting; referral for civil or criminal prosecution. |

Discipline shall be applied consistently regardless of seniority, role, or tenure. The Administrator shall be notified of all Level 2 and Level 3 violations within 24 hours. The Governing Body shall be notified of all Level 3 violations within 24 hours.
## 8. Procedures — Acknowledgment and Distribution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.1 | Administrator | Ensure all workforce members receive a copy of the Code at hire and upon each revision. | At hire; within 14 days of revision. |
| 8.2 | All workforce members | Read the Code and sign the Policy Acknowledgment and Code of Conduct Attestation (Appendix A). | Within 14 days of hire or revision. |
| 8.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain attestation records and report completion rates to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |
| 8.4 | Compliance Officer | Post the Code (or an accessible summary) in a location visible to all agency staff and patients. | Continuously. |
| 8.5 | Compliance Officer | Review the Code annually and present any recommended revisions to the Governing Body for approval. | Annually at Q1 meeting. |

## 9. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

# CO-CP-005 — Whistleblower Protection & Non-Retaliation
## Policy Header

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the protections afforded to individuals who, in good faith, report suspected violations of law, regulation, agency policy, or the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004), and prohibits retaliation of any kind against such individuals. Effective compliance programs depend on a workforce that feels safe reporting concerns. This policy provides the legal and operational framework for non-retaliation consistent with the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. § 3730), applicable California whistleblower statutes (California Labor Code § 1102.5), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., including Governing Body members, the Administrator, all employees, contractors, volunteers, and business associates. It applies to all reports of suspected violations, regardless of whether the report ultimately results in a finding of wrongdoing.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. strictly prohibits retaliation of any form against any individual who, in good faith, reports a suspected compliance violation, cooperates with a compliance investigation, or refuses to participate in conduct they reasonably believe violates law or agency policy.
4.2 Retaliation is defined broadly and includes but is not limited to: termination, demotion, suspension, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, harassment, intimidation, exclusion from meetings, negative performance evaluations influenced by the report, or any other adverse employment or contractual action.
4.3 The protection of this policy applies to all good-faith reporters regardless of whether the reported concern is ultimately substantiated.
4.4 An individual who knowingly makes a false or malicious report with the intent to harm another individual or the agency is not protected by this policy and is subject to disciplinary action per CO-CP-004.
4.5 The Governing Body shall be directly notified of any alleged retaliation against a reporter within 24 hours of the allegation. The Compliance Officer may not serve as the sole investigator if they are the subject of the retaliation allegation.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Whistleblower | Any individual who reports, in good faith, a suspected violation of law, regulation, or agency policy, including suspected fraud, waste, abuse, patient harm, privacy breach, or Code of Conduct violation. |
| Good Faith | A sincere belief, based on reasonable information available to the reporter at the time, that a violation may have occurred or is occurring. |
| Retaliation | Any adverse action taken against an individual because they made a good-faith compliance report, participated in an investigation, or refused to participate in unlawful conduct. |
| False Claims Act (FCA) qui tam provision | The federal law provision (31 U.S.C. § 3730(h)) that specifically prohibits retaliation against employees who take action in furtherance of a False Claims Act lawsuit. |
| California Labor Code § 1102.5 | California state law prohibiting employer retaliation against employees who disclose information about suspected legal violations to government agencies or internal compliance authorities. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 How to Make a Protected Report

| Method | Contact | Anonymity Available? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct report to Compliance Officer | [Compliance Officer contact maintained in agency directory] | No (but confidentiality maintained) |
| Compliance Hotline | [Hotline number maintained in agency directory per CO-CP-006] | Yes |
| Anonymous written report | Submitted per CO-CP-006 instructions | Yes |
| Direct report to Governing Body Chair | [Governing Body Chair contact per GV-GB-001 roster] | No (but confidentiality maintained) |
| External report to OIG Hotline | 1-800-HHS-TIPS (1-800-447-8477) | Yes |
| External report to California DHCS | Per DHCS complaint process | Variable |

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain strict confidentiality of reporter identity to the maximum extent practicable. Disclose identity only if: (a) the reporter consents; (b) disclosure is required by law or legal proceedings; (c) disclosure is unavoidable due to the nature of the investigation. | Continuously throughout investigation. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Notify the reporter (if known) before disclosing their identity in any proceeding and provide an explanation of why disclosure is necessary. | Before any disclosure. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Document all disclosures of reporter identity, the justification, and any consent obtained. | At time of disclosure. |

### 6.3 Non-Retaliation Enforcement

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receipt of an allegation of retaliation, open a formal retaliation investigation within 5 calendar days, separate from any underlying compliance investigation. | Within 5 calendar days of allegation. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Notify the Governing Body Chair in writing within 24 hours of receiving a retaliation allegation. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | If the Compliance Officer is the subject of the retaliation allegation, the Governing Body Chair shall designate an independent investigator (may be external legal counsel or independent HR professional). | Within 5 calendar days of allegation. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer / Investigator | Conduct retaliation investigation per CO-CP-007 standards. Interview the reporter, the alleged retaliator, and relevant witnesses. Document all findings. | Within 30 calendar days of initiation. |
| 6.3.5 | Governing Body / Administrator | If retaliation is substantiated, impose disciplinary action per CO-CP-004 severity scale, up to and including immediate termination. Any substantiated retaliatory termination shall be subject to an offer of reinstatement with back pay. | Upon conclusion of investigation. |
| 6.3.6 | Compliance Officer | Document investigation findings, disciplinary action, and corrective measures. Report to Governing Body at next quarterly meeting. | At meeting following investigation conclusion. |

| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Include whistleblower rights and reporting mechanisms in the annual compliance training curriculum per CO-CP-008. | Annually. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the multiple accessible mechanisms through which any workforce member, patient, family member, vendor, or business associate may report suspected compliance violations, fraud, waste, or abuse to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The existence of accessible, well-publicized reporting mechanisms is a required element of the Corporate Compliance Program under OIG guidance. Effective reporting channels are essential to the agency's ability to detect, investigate, and correct compliance violations promptly.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all individuals who interact with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. — including workforce members, patients, family members, vendors, business associates, and members of the public who have reason to report a compliance concern.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain multiple accessible reporting mechanisms at all times, including at minimum: a compliance hotline (with anonymous option), a direct email to the Compliance Officer, and a physical mailbox.
4.2 All reporting mechanisms shall be publicized to all workforce members at hire, in annual training, and through posted notices in accessible locations.
4.3 All reports received through any mechanism shall be logged, assigned a tracking number, and responded to within the timeframes established in this policy.
4.4 Anonymous reports shall be accepted and investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided. The agency shall not attempt to identify anonymous reporters.
4.5 No individual who makes a good-faith report through any mechanism shall be retaliated against, per policy CO-CP-005.
4.6 Reports involving the Compliance Officer shall be directed to the Governing Body Chair. Reports involving the Administrator shall be directed to the Compliance Officer and Governing Body Chair simultaneously.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Hotline | A dedicated telephone line (or third-party service) for receiving compliance reports, available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, with an anonymous option. |
| Report Tracking Number | A unique identifier assigned to each compliance report upon receipt, used to track the status of investigation and resolution. |
| Substantiated Report | A report in which the investigation finds that the reported concern is supported by sufficient evidence to conclude that a violation occurred. |
| Unsubstantiated Report | A report in which the investigation does not find sufficient evidence to support the reported concern. Unsubstantiated reports are closed with documentation; reporters are not penalized. |
| Anonymous Report | A report submitted without the reporter identifying themselves. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standardized process for initiating, conducting, documenting, and closing compliance investigations at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A structured, consistent investigation process is essential to ensure that reported concerns are addressed promptly, that evidence is properly preserved and assessed, that confidentiality is maintained, that corrective action is implemented where warranted, and that the agency fulfills its obligations under the False Claims Act, OIG guidance, and applicable federal and state law.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All compliance investigations initiated under the reporting mechanisms of CO-CP-006
All self-identified compliance concerns identified through internal auditing (CO-RA-002)
All retaliation investigations under CO-CP-005
All investigations directed by the Governing Body
All investigations of potential fraud, waste, or abuse under CO-FA-003
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every compliance report or self-identified concern shall be evaluated for investigation within 5 business days of receipt.
4.2 Formal investigations shall be initiated within 7 calendar days of receipt of a compliance report that, upon triage, warrants investigation.
4.3 All compliance investigations shall be documented in writing from initiation through closure.
4.4 All investigation records are confidential compliance documents. Access shall be restricted to the Compliance Officer, legal counsel (when engaged), and the Governing Body.
4.5 The Compliance Officer shall preserve investigation records under a litigation hold protocol if there is any indication that civil or criminal proceedings may arise from the subject matter.
4.6 The agency shall cooperate fully and promptly with any government investigation. All document requests or inquiries from government agencies shall be immediately routed to the Compliance Officer and legal counsel.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Investigation | A structured, documented inquiry into a reported or self-identified compliance concern to determine whether a violation occurred, its scope, its cause, and the appropriate remedial response. |
| Investigator | The Compliance Officer or designee appointed to conduct the investigation. Must be independent of the subject matter and individuals under review. |
| Investigation File | The complete documentation package for an investigation including the opening memo, evidence collected, interview notes, findings memo, and closure documentation. |
| Litigation Hold | A directive to preserve all records, communications, and data that may be relevant to anticipated or active legal proceedings. |
| Voluntary Disclosure | The proactive disclosure of a confirmed compliance violation to a federal or state regulatory agency. May mitigate penalties if conducted promptly and in good faith. |
| Overpayment | Any funds received from Medicare, Medicaid, or another payer to which the agency is not entitled. Must be reported and refunded within 60 days of identification per the False Claims Act. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Investigation Initiation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receiving a report (via CO-CP-006) or self-identifying a compliance concern, complete the Initial Triage Assessment (Appendix A) within 5 business days. | Within 5 business days of receipt. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Based on triage, classify the concern as: (a) Requires Formal Investigation — credible allegation of violation; (b) Administrative Review — policy question or minor deviation; (c) No Action Required — report not credible or not a violation; (d) Referral — matter outside agency jurisdiction (e.g., patient abuse requiring mandatory reporting). Document triage decision with rationale. | Within 5 business days. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | For matters classified as Requires Formal Investigation: open a formal investigation file, assign a tracking number (linked to CO-CP-006 log), designate the investigator, and prepare an Investigation Opening Memorandum (Appendix B). | Within 7 calendar days of report receipt. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Notify the Governing Body Chair in writing of investigations involving: (a) fraud, waste, or abuse; (b) Level 3 Code of Conduct violations; (c) potential False Claims Act exposure; (d) patient harm. | Within 24 hours of opening Level 3 investigations; at next quarterly meeting for others. |
| 6.1.5 | Compliance Officer | Determine whether an interim protective measure is needed pending investigation conclusion (e.g., temporary reassignment of an employee under review, suspension of a billing function, interim clinical oversight enhancement). Document the determination with rationale. | Within 5 business days of investigation opening. |

### 6.2 Evidence Collection

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Investigator | Identify and collect all relevant evidence including: (a) clinical records; (b) billing records; (c) scheduling records; (d) email and electronic communications; (e) system audit logs; (f) personnel records (if applicable). | Within 10 business days of investigation opening. |
| 6.2.2 | Investigator | Preserve all original evidence. Do not alter, destroy, or allow access to evidence under review. If litigation hold is applicable, issue written hold notice to all custodians of relevant records. | Immediately upon opening investigation. |
| 6.2.3 | Investigator | Conduct confidential interviews of relevant witnesses. Notify each interviewee that: (a) the interview is confidential; (b) their supervisor may not be present; (c) they may have HR representation if subject to potential discipline; (d) retaliation for participating is prohibited. Document interview notes contemporaneously (Appendix C). | Within 14 business days of investigation opening. |
| 6.2.4 | Investigator | Where applicable, engage external subject matter experts (e.g., coding auditor, legal counsel, clinical expert) if the investigation requires specialized expertise. | As needed; no later than 10 business days of opening. |

### 6.3 Investigation Analysis and Findings

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Investigator | Analyze all evidence against the applicable regulatory standard, policy requirement, or Code of Conduct provision. Prepare a written Findings Memorandum (Appendix D) that documents: (a) the allegation or concern; (b) evidence reviewed; (c) findings (substantiated/unsubstantiated); (d) root cause (if applicable); (e) financial exposure (if applicable). | Within 30 calendar days of investigation opening for standard matters; within 14 days for expedited/urgent matters. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Review and approve the Findings Memorandum. Consult legal counsel if: (a) the matter may involve mandatory government disclosure; (b) there is potential civil or criminal exposure; (c) the matter involves a False Claims Act violation and potential 60-day repayment obligation. | Within 5 business days of Investigator submission. |

### 6.4 Corrective Action

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | For substantiated investigations: develop a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) per policy QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days of the Findings Memorandum approval. The CAP must address: (a) root cause; (b) immediate corrective measures; (c) systemic process improvements; (d) responsible parties; (e) deadlines; (f) monitoring metrics. | Within 14 calendar days of Findings Memorandum approval. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer / HR Director | For substantiated investigations involving individual employee misconduct: recommend disciplinary action per CO-CP-004 severity scale and HR-ER-002 progressive discipline policy. | Within 5 business days of Findings Memorandum approval. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | For substantiated overpayment identification: initiate refund process per FN-BC-004 and track against the 60-day repayment deadline. | Immediately upon identification of overpayment. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | For matters requiring voluntary disclosure: engage legal counsel and present recommendation to Governing Body. | Within 30 calendar days of Findings Memorandum approval. |

### 6.5 Investigation Closure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Prepare an Investigation Closure Memorandum (Appendix E) upon: (a) completion of investigation and CAP implementation; (b) determination of no further action required; (c) referral to external authority. | Within 7 days of CAP confirmation or determination of no action. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Update the Compliance Report Log (CO-CP-006 Appendix A) with investigation outcome and closure date. | Within 1 business day of closure. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Notify non-anonymous reporters of investigation closure and outcome (without disclosing confidential details) per CO-CP-006 Section 6.4. | Within 7 days of closure. |
| 6.5.4 | Compliance Officer | Present investigation summary (without identifying details) to the Compliance Committee at the next regular meeting and to the Governing Body in the quarterly compliance report. | At next quarterly meeting. |
