## 2. Purpose
Establishes the agency's comprehensive HIPAA Privacy Program in compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164, Subparts A and E). The Privacy Program ensures the confidentiality of protected health information (PHI) while enabling appropriate use and disclosure for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations.
## 3. Scope
All workforce members, business associates, vendors, and any individual who creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall maintain a HIPAA Privacy Program that protects all PHI in any form (oral, written, electronic).
4.2 The Compliance Officer shall serve as the Privacy Officer (or designate a qualified individual).
4.3 The agency shall maintain a current Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) and provide it to all patients at the start of care.
4.4 PHI shall be used and disclosed only as permitted by the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with the minimum necessary standard applied to all uses and disclosures.
4.5 Patient rights under HIPAA shall be honored including: access, amendment, accounting of disclosures, restrictions, and confidential communications.
4.6 All workforce members shall receive HIPAA privacy training at orientation and annually.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| PHI | Protected Health Information — individually identifiable health information transmitted or maintained in any form. |
| NPP | Notice of Privacy Practices — the document informing patients of their privacy rights and the agency's PHI practices. |
| Privacy Officer | The individual designated to oversee the HIPAA Privacy Program. |
| Treatment, Payment, Healthcare Operations (TPO) | The three primary categories under which PHI may be used or disclosed without patient authorization. |
| Authorization | A patient's written permission for uses or disclosures of PHI not otherwise permitted under the Privacy Rule. |
| De-identified Information | Health information from which all 18 HIPAA identifiers have been removed. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Privacy Program Administration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer / Privacy Officer | Establish and maintain the HIPAA Privacy Program. Designate a Privacy Officer (may be the Compliance Officer) in writing. | Prior to agency operation; maintained continuously. |
| 6.1.2 | Privacy Officer | Develop and maintain all required privacy policies and procedures per 45 CFR § 164.530(i). | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.1.3 | Privacy Officer | Maintain the current Notice of Privacy Practices (Appendix A). Update upon any material change and distribute revised NPP to patients. | Maintained continuously; distributed to patients at SOC. |
| 6.1.4 | Privacy Officer | Ensure all workforce members receive HIPAA privacy training at orientation and annually per CO-CP-008. | At hire; annually. |
| 6.1.5 | Privacy Officer | Maintain documentation of all privacy policies, NPP, training, complaints, and sanctions for minimum 6 years per 45 CFR § 164.530(j). | 6 years minimum (agency standard: 7 years per CO-HP-007). |

### 6.2 Patient Rights

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Staff (SOC) | Provide the NPP to each patient at the start of care. Obtain signed acknowledgment (Appendix B). If patient refuses to sign, document the refusal. | At SOC. |
| 6.2.2 | Privacy Officer | Process patient requests per CO-HP-006: (a) access to records within 30 calendar days; (b) amendment requests within 60 calendar days; (c) accounting of disclosures within 60 calendar days; (d) restriction requests per applicable standards; (e) confidential communication requests. | Per applicable timeframes. |

### 6.3 Uses and Disclosures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | All workforce members | Use or disclose PHI only for: (a) TPO; (b) as authorized by the patient; (c) as required by law; (d) as otherwise permitted by the Privacy Rule. Apply the minimum necessary standard per CO-HP-004. | Continuously. |
| 6.3.2 | Privacy Officer | Maintain a log of all disclosures not for TPO (Disclosure Tracking Log — Appendix C) to support accounting of disclosures requests. | Updated within 5 business days of each qualifying disclosure. |

### 6.4 Complaints and Violations

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Privacy Officer | Accept and investigate all privacy complaints per CO-CP-007 standards. Maintain a Privacy Complaint Log (Appendix D). | Investigation initiated within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.4.2 | Privacy Officer | Apply sanctions per CO-CP-004 for workforce member privacy violations. | Per CO-CP-004 severity scale. |
| 6.4.3 | Privacy Officer | Evaluate whether a privacy incident constitutes a breach requiring notification per CO-HP-003. | Within 5 business days of incident identification. |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for electronic protected health information (ePHI) per the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C).
## 3. Scope
All workforce members and systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall designate a Security Officer responsible for the HIPAA Security Program.
4.2 The agency shall conduct a Security Risk Assessment annually and upon significant system changes.
4.3 The agency shall implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards per 45 CFR §§ 164.308, 164.310, and 164.312.
4.4 All security incidents shall be reported, investigated, and documented per IT-DR-005 and CO-HP-003.
## 5–6. Definitions & Procedures
(Full security program procedures aligned to IT-SC-001 through IT-SC-006, including access control, encryption, audit logging, workforce training, device security, and incident response — per HIPAA Security Rule implementation specifications)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conduct annual Security Risk Assessment | Security Officer / IT Director | Complete SRA per NIST/OCR methodology. Document findings, risk levels, and mitigation plans. | Annually by end of Q2. |
| Implement access controls | IT Director | Role-based access; unique user IDs; automatic logoff; encryption per IT-SC-002, IT-SC-003. | Continuously. |
| Maintain audit logs | IT Director | System access logs retained per IT-DR-003. | Continuously; logs retained 7 years. |
| Conduct security awareness training | Security Officer | Per IT-UP-004 and CO-CP-008. | At hire; annually. |
| Business continuity for ePHI | IT Director | Per IT-DR-001, IT-DR-002. | Tested annually. |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes breach identification, risk assessment, notification, and documentation procedures per the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.400–164.414).
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall identify, investigate, and report breaches of unsecured PHI per federal requirements.
4.2 Individual notification shall be provided within 60 calendar days of discovery.
4.3 HHS notification shall be provided: (a) within 60 days for breaches affecting 500+ individuals; (b) annually for breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals.
4.4 Media notification shall be provided for breaches affecting 500+ residents of a state/jurisdiction.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Breach Identification and Risk Assessment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Any workforce member | Report any suspected breach to the Privacy Officer immediately. | Immediately. |
| 6.1.2 | Privacy Officer | Conduct a four-factor risk assessment per 45 CFR § 164.402: (a) nature and extent of PHI involved; (b) unauthorized person who used/accessed PHI; (c) whether PHI was actually acquired or viewed; (d) extent to which risk has been mitigated. Document using the Breach Risk Assessment Form (Appendix A). | Within 10 business days of report. |
| 6.1.3 | Privacy Officer | Determine whether the incident constitutes a reportable breach or falls within an exception (unintentional access, inadvertent disclosure, good faith belief PHI not retained). | Within 10 business days. |

### 6.2 Notification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Privacy Officer | For confirmed breaches: prepare individual notification letters (Appendix B) containing: (a) description of breach; (b) types of information involved; (c) steps individuals should take; (d) what the agency is doing; (e) contact information. | Within 60 calendar days of discovery. |
| 6.2.2 | Privacy Officer | Notify HHS: (a) within 60 days for ≥500 individuals; (b) within 60 days of end of calendar year for <500 individuals. | Per above timeframes. |
| 6.2.3 | Privacy Officer | For breaches ≥500 in a state: notify prominent media outlets. | Within 60 calendar days of discovery. |

### 6.3 Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Privacy Officer | Maintain a Breach Log (Appendix C) documenting all suspected and confirmed breaches. | Updated within 1 business day; retained 7 years. |

## 2. Purpose
Defines the minimum necessary standard for PHI access, use, and disclosure per 45 CFR § 164.502(b) and § 164.514(d). The agency shall make reasonable efforts to limit PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall identify workforce members who need access to PHI and the categories/conditions of PHI each role requires.
4.2 For routine and recurring disclosures: standard protocols shall limit PHI to the minimum necessary.
4.3 For non-routine requests: individual review and approval by the Privacy Officer is required.
4.4 The minimum necessary standard does not apply to: (a) disclosures to or requests by a healthcare provider for treatment; (b) disclosures to the individual; (c) uses or disclosures authorized by the individual; (d) disclosures to HHS for compliance investigation; (e) uses or disclosures required by law.
## 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Privacy Officer | Maintain a Role-Based PHI Access Matrix (Appendix A) defining the categories of PHI each workforce role may access. | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.2 | IT Director | Configure EHR system access controls to enforce role-based PHI access per the Matrix. | Continuously. |
| 6.3 | Privacy Officer | Review all non-routine disclosure requests to ensure minimum necessary compliance before release. | Before each non-routine disclosure. |

4.4 Any business associate breach or non-compliance shall be addressed per the BAA terms and CO-HP-003.

| 6.3 | Compliance Officer | Review all BAAs annually for compliance with current HIPAA requirements. | Annually. |
| 6.4 | Compliance Officer | If a business associate breaches the BAA: (a) investigate per CO-CP-007; (b) cure the breach if feasible; (c) terminate the agreement if not cured; (d) report to HHS if necessary. | Per BAA terms; investigation within 7 days. |

## 2. Purpose
Defines procedures for fulfilling patient requests to access, amend, or receive an accounting of disclosures of their health information per 45 CFR §§ 164.524, 164.526, and 164.528.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Patients have the right to access their PHI in a designated record set within 30 calendar days of request.
4.2 Patients have the right to request amendment of their PHI. The agency shall respond within 60 calendar days.
4.3 Patients have the right to receive an accounting of disclosures not for TPO within 60 calendar days.
4.4 The agency shall not charge unreasonable fees for providing access to records.
## 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Any staff member | Direct all patient record requests to the Privacy Officer. | Immediately upon receipt. |
| 6.2 | Privacy Officer | Log the request in the Patient Records Request Log (Appendix A). | Within 1 business day. |
| 6.3 | Privacy Officer | For access requests: provide records in the format requested (if readily producible) within 30 calendar days. One 30-day extension permitted with written notice to patient. | 30 calendar days; extension with notice. |
| 6.4 | Privacy Officer | For amendment requests: evaluate and respond within 60 calendar days. Accept or deny with written explanation. If denied, inform patient of right to submit a statement of disagreement. | 60 calendar days. |
| 6.5 | Privacy Officer | For accounting of disclosures: compile from Disclosure Tracking Log (CO-HP-001 Appendix C) and provide within 60 calendar days. | 60 calendar days. |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes retention periods, storage requirements, and secure destruction procedures for all agency records per HIPAA, CMS, California state law, and applicable federal requirements.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall retain all clinical, financial, compliance, governance, and personnel records for the minimum retention periods defined in this policy.
4.2 No records shall be destroyed before the applicable retention period expires.
4.3 Records subject to litigation hold, government investigation, or audit shall not be destroyed regardless of retention schedule.
4.4 Destruction of records containing PHI shall be performed using methods that render PHI unreadable and indecipherable.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Retention Schedule

| Record Type | Minimum Retention Period | Regulatory Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical/patient records | 7 years from discharge (or 3 years after death if sooner) | California H&S Code; 42 CFR § 484.110 |
| OASIS records | 7 years | CMS requirements |
| Billing/claims records | 7 years | 31 U.S.C. § 3731(b); CMS |
| Compliance records (audits, investigations, reports) | 7 years | OIG guidance; agency standard |
| HIPAA documentation | 6 years from creation or last effective date | 45 CFR § 164.530(j) (agency applies 7-year standard) |
| Governing Body records | Permanent | Agency standard |
| Personnel records | 7 years after separation | California law; EEOC |
| Training records | 7 years | Agency standard |
| BAAs | 6 years after termination (agency applies 7 years) | 45 CFR § 164.530(j) |
| Financial records | 7 years | IRS; CMS |
| Contracts | 7 years after expiration | Agency standard |

### 6.2 Destruction Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Approve all record destruction. No records shall be destroyed without written Compliance Officer authorization. | Before destruction. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Verify no litigation hold or investigation applies to records scheduled for destruction. | Before destruction. |
| 6.2.3 | Designated staff | Destroy paper records containing PHI by cross-cut shredding. Destroy electronic records by secure wiping or physical destruction of media. | Per schedule. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a Record Destruction Log (Appendix A) documenting: record type, date range, destruction method, destruction date, and authorizer. | Updated at each destruction event; log retained permanently. |

### Appendix A — Record Destruction Log

| # | Record Type | Date Range of Records | Destruction Method | Destruction Date | Authorized By | Witness | Litigation Hold Verified Clear? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RD-2025-001 |  | From: ___ To: ___ | ☐ Cross-cut shred ☐ Secure wipe ☐ Physical destruction |  |  |  | ☐ Yes |

# CO-DC-001 — Assessment Audit Trail and Data Integrity
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Policy Title | Assessment Audit Trail and Data Integrity |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
Requires all assessment entries, modifications, and coding decisions to be captured in a timestamped, version-controlled audit trail to support data integrity, regulatory compliance, and fraud prevention.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All clinical assessment entries and OASIS coding decisions shall be captured in a system-generated, immutable audit trail.
4.2 Every modification to an assessment after initial entry shall be documented with: original value, modified value, modifying user, timestamp, and reason for change.
4.3 No assessment data shall be deleted from the audit trail. Corrections shall follow CO-DC-003 standards.
4.4 The Compliance Officer shall have access to all audit trails for compliance monitoring purposes.
## 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | IT Director | Configure EHR system to capture and retain a complete audit trail for all assessment data including: user ID, date/time of entry, date/time of modification, original values, modified values, and reason for change. | Before agency operation; maintained continuously. |
| 6.2 | IT Director | Ensure audit trail data is immutable — no user (including system administrators) may alter or delete audit trail entries. | Continuously. |
| 6.3 | Compliance Officer | Review audit trail data as part of documentation compliance audits per CO-DC-002. | Per audit schedule. |
| 6.4 | Compliance Officer | Investigate any audit trail anomalies (e.g., patterns of late modifications, unauthorized access, systematic coding changes) per CO-CP-007. | Within 7 calendar days of identification. |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes a systematic documentation audit program with defined sample sizes, audit frequency, scoring criteria, and corrective action triggers for identified deficiencies across all clinical and administrative documentation.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall maintain an active documentation audit program as a component of the internal compliance auditing program (CO-RA-002).
4.2 Documentation audits shall use standardized scoring criteria and defined deficiency thresholds.
4.3 Audit results shall be reported to the Compliance Committee and used to target training and corrective action.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Audit Schedule and Standards

| Clinical visit note completeness | Quarterly | 20 records, stratified by clinician | 12-point documentation checklist (Appendix A) | <90% compliance rate |
| Authentication and timeliness | Quarterly | 20 records | Timely completion per CL-CD-004 | <95% compliance rate |
| OASIS accuracy | Semi-annually | 20 records, stratified by assessor | Item-level accuracy per CMS guidance | <85% accuracy rate |
| Physician order documentation | Quarterly | 20 episodes | Order presence, signature, timeliness | <95% compliance rate |

### 6.2 Audit Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct documentation audits per the schedule above using standardized tools (Appendix A). | Per schedule. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Score each record and calculate compliance/accuracy rates. Document findings in the Documentation Audit Report (Appendix B). | Within 14 calendar days of audit. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | For deficiency rates below thresholds: develop targeted CAP per QA-AE-003. | Within 14 calendar days of report. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Report findings to Compliance Committee and include in quarterly Governing Body report. | Quarterly. |

# CO-DC-003 — Late Entry, Correction & Amendment Standards
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CO-DC-003 |
| Policy Title | Late Entry, Correction & Amendment Standards |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
Defines standards for late entries, error corrections, and amendments to clinical and administrative records to maintain documentation integrity and legal defensibility.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Original documentation shall never be deleted, obliterated, or rendered unreadable.
4.2 Late entries shall be clearly labeled as "LATE ENTRY" with the current date/time and the date of the event being documented.
4.3 Corrections shall use single-line strikethrough (for paper) or system correction function (for electronic), with the original entry preserved, the correction clearly marked, the correcting author identified, and the reason for correction documented.
4.4 Amendments shall be clearly labeled, reference the original entry, and include the amending author and date.
4.5 No correction or amendment shall be made under pressure from billing, coding, or administrative personnel to alter clinical findings.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Late Entries

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Documenting clinician | Enter the late entry using the current date and time. Label "LATE ENTRY — documenting events of [original date]." | As soon as practicable; no later than end of next business day. |
| 6.1.2 | Documenting clinician | Document the reason for the late entry. | With the late entry. |
| 6.1.3 | Supervisor | Review late entries during supervisory review. Excessive late entries by a clinician shall be addressed through counseling and, if persistent, progressive discipline per HR-ER-002. | During supervisory review. |

### 6.2 Corrections

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Correcting author | Electronic: use the EHR correction function. Original entry must remain visible. Paper: single-line strikethrough; write "error," initial, date. | As soon as error is identified. |
| 6.2.2 | Correcting author | Document the reason for correction. | With the correction. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Monitor correction patterns through audit trail review per CO-DC-001. Patterns of corrections that change clinical acuity, coding, or billing shall be investigated per CO-CP-007. | Per audit schedule. |

### 6.3 Amendments

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Amending author | Label amendment clearly: "AMENDMENT to entry dated [date]." Document the additional or clarifying information. Sign and date. | As needed. |
| 6.3.2 | Amending author | Never delete or overwrite the original entry. | N/A — prohibition. |

| Correction | "Error" or system correction flag | Yes — original visible | Current date | Yes |

# CO-DC-004 — Clinical, Documentation, and Billing Alignment Audit
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CO-DC-004 |
| Policy Title | Clinical, Documentation, and Billing Alignment Audit |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes a triangulation audit process verifying alignment between physician orders, visit delivery documentation, and billed claims. Misalignment among these three sources is a primary indicator of billing fraud, documentation falsification, or systemic operational failure.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall conduct quarterly triangulation audits comparing: (a) physician orders (services ordered); (b) clinical visit documentation (services documented as delivered); (c) billed claims (services billed to payer).
4.2 All three sources must be aligned. Any mismatch constitutes a deficiency requiring investigation.
4.3 Variance types include: (a) services billed but not documented; (b) services documented but not ordered; (c) services ordered but not delivered; (d) coding discrepancies between documentation and billing.
## 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct quarterly triangulation audits per CO-RA-002 standards. Minimum sample: 20 episodes per quarter. | Quarterly. |
| 6.2 | Auditor | For each episode, verify: (a) every billed service has corresponding visit documentation; (b) every documented visit has a corresponding physician order; (c) billed codes match documented services; (d) visit dates on claims match visit dates in documentation. | During audit. |
| 6.3 | Auditor | Document all variances using the Triangulation Audit Worksheet (Appendix A). Classify each variance by type and severity. | During audit. |
| 6.4 | Compliance Officer | For Critical variances (services billed but not documented — potential false claim): initiate investigation per CO-CP-007. For Major variances: develop CAP per QA-AE-003. For Minor variances: address through education. | Critical: 7 days. Major: 14 days. Minor: 30 days. |
| 6.5 | Compliance Officer | Report triangulation audit results to Compliance Committee and Governing Body. | Quarterly. |

### Appendix A — Triangulation Audit Worksheet

| Episode # | Patient MRN | Certification Period | Service Date | Service Type | Physician Order Present? | Visit Documentation Present? | Claim Submitted? | Codes Match? | Dates Match? | Variance Type | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 |  |  |  |  | ☐ Yes ☐ No | ☐ Yes ☐ No | ☐ Yes ☐ No | ☐ Yes ☐ No | ☐ Yes ☐ No | ☐ None ☐ Billed/Not Doc'd ☐ Doc'd/Not Ordered ☐ Ordered/Not Delivered ☐ Code Mismatch | ☐ Critical ☐ Major ☐ Minor |

Variance Type Definitions:

| Type | Definition | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billed but Not Documented | Claim submitted for service with no corresponding visit note | Critical |
| Documented but Not Ordered | Visit note exists but no physician order authorizes the service | Major |
| Ordered but Not Delivered | Physician order exists but no visit documentation or claim | Major |
| Code Mismatch | Documentation supports different code than billed | Major |
| Date Mismatch | Claim date differs from visit documentation date | Major |

# RM-ER-002 — Bag Technique (Corridor §6-013)

**Crosswalk:** ACHC HH7-1A, HH7-2A.01, HH7-2B.01 · CoP §484.70 · Title 22 §74723, §74725 · CDC Standard Precautions
**Evidence:** P, D, I, O

## PURPOSE
To prevent transmission of infectious agents into and out of the patient home via the nursing/clinician bag and its contents.

## POLICY
Every clinician who carries a bag into a patient home shall observe Bag Technique on every visit. Bag Technique is observable; competency is verified by direct field observation at hire and annually.

## PROCEDURE
1. **Surface preparation.** Place the bag on a clean, dry, hard surface — never on the floor, bed, or upholstered furniture. Place a barrier (paper towel/chux) under the bag.
2. **Pre-opening hand hygiene.** Perform hand hygiene (alcohol-based rub ≥20s or soap/water ≥20s) before opening the bag and before retrieving any item.
3. **Anticipate supplies.** Remove all anticipated supplies before patient contact; close the bag during patient care so the interior is not re-entered with contaminated hands.
4. **Item-return rule.** Disinfect any reusable item that contacted the patient with a hospital-grade EPA-registered disinfectant per manufacturer contact-time before returning it to the bag. Single-use items are **not** returned to the bag — they are bagged for disposal in the home.
5. **Pre-closure hand hygiene.** Perform hand hygiene before closing the bag.
6. **Bag exterior decontamination.** Decontaminate the bag exterior at least weekly and any time of visible soil. Log on `RM-OS-001.B`-equivalent *Bag Cleaning Log* (Addendum RM-ER-002.A).
7. **Shared instruments.** Stethoscope, BP cuff, pulse-ox, and thermometer disinfected between patients with alcohol-based wipe ≥30s contact.
8. **High-risk visits.** When entering an isolation/precaution home, leave the bag in the vehicle; carry only what is needed in a disposable plastic bag.
9. **Annual competency.** Direct field observation by Clinical Manager (or designee) recorded on Addendum RM-ER-002.B *Bag Technique Competency Checklist*. Failed observations trigger immediate retraining and re-observation within 7 days.

## ADDENDUMS
- RM-ER-002.A — Bag Cleaning Log
- RM-ER-002.B — Bag Technique Competency Checklist

## CROSS-REFERENCES
RM-ER-001 (IPC Plan) · RM-ER-003 (BBP) · RM-ER-004 (TB) · QA-PG-001 (QAPI surveillance) · HR-TD-001 (Annual Training).

# RM-OS-001 — Fire Safety & Extinguisher Inspection (Corridor §6-020/§6-024)

## PROCEDURE — Office Fire Safety (additive)
1. **Portable fire extinguisher monthly visual inspection** by the Safety Officer or designee:
   - Pressure gauge needle in the green operating range
   - Pull pin and tamper seal intact
   - Hose, nozzle, and discharge horn unobstructed and undamaged
   - Mounting bracket secure; signage visible from ≥30 ft
   - Service tag legible
   - Initialed on the back of the extinguisher tag **and** on Addendum RM-OS-001.B *Extinguisher Monthly Inspection Log* (form `RM-F-010`)
2. **Annual maintenance** by a state-licensed fire-protection servicer per **NFPA 10 §7.3** — service tag affixed.
3. **6-year internal maintenance** of stored-pressure dry chemical extinguishers (NFPA 10 §7.3.3).
4. **12-year hydrostatic test** of dry chemical extinguishers (NFPA 10 §8.3). Tracked on Addendum RM-OS-001.C *Extinguisher Lifecycle Log*.
5. **Egress.** Egress paths kept clear at all times; exit signs illuminated; emergency lighting tested **monthly (≥30 sec)** and **annually (≥90 min)** per NFPA 101 §7.9.
6. **Office fire drill** at least annually; after-action notes captured on Addendum RM-OS-001.D *Fire Drill After-Action Report* (form `RM-F-011`); deficiencies fed to QAPI (`QA-PG-001`).

## PROCEDURE — Patient-Home Fire Safety (additive)
At the initial environmental assessment (and on any change in equipment/layout), the clinician documents:
- Working smoke alarms on each level / outside each sleeping area
- Patient/caregiver knowledge of escape plan and meeting place
- Oxygen-in-use signage and "no smoking within 10 ft" reinforcement
- Extension cord / overload risks; absence of multi-tap power strips on heat sources
- Education delivered and documented on the visit note; deficiencies escalated to the Clinical Manager within 24 h.

## PROCEDURE — Equipment Management & SMDA (additive)
- Agency-owned equipment (BP cuff, glucometer, pulse-ox, scale): inventoried, calibrated per manufacturer, tagged with cycle date.
- DME from contracted vendor: vendor agreement (Addendum `.F`) defines delivery, set-up, patient training, 24/7 service. Clinician verifies safe operation at every visit.
- **Safe Medical Device Act** reportable events: device-related death, serious injury, or serious illness reported to the **manufacturer within 10 working days**, and to **FDA via MedWatch (Form 3500A)** when criteria are met. Logged on Addendum `.G` *SMDA Reportable Events Log*.

## ADDENDUMS (full set)
A: Office EOC Plan · B: Extinguisher Monthly Log (RM-F-010) · C: Extinguisher Lifecycle Log · D: Fire Drill AAR (RM-F-011) · E: Utilities Log · F: DME Vendor Agreement · G: SMDA Log · H: Vehicle Incident Report.

---

# RM-EP-001 — Emergency Preparedness Exercises & After-Action (Corridor §6-037)

## PROCEDURE — Exercises (additive, ACHC HH7-3D / CoP §484.102(d))
1. **Annual minimum:** two exercises per year.
   - **Exercise A:** one full-scale community-integrated exercise. If a community-integrated exercise is not accessible (documented in the AAR), the agency conducts an **individual facility-based functional exercise**.
   - **Exercise B:** one additional exercise: tabletop, drill, or another full-scale.
2. **HVA-driven scenarios:** scenarios drawn from the top-5 hazards on the current Hazard Vulnerability Analysis (Addendum A).
3. **Patient acuity tiers exercised:** every exercise must include a Tier-1 (life-sustaining) patient scenario.
4. **After-Action Report (AAR):** completed within **30 days** of the exercise on Addendum F. AAR captures:
   - Objectives, participants, scenario, timeline
   - Strengths
   - Areas for improvement
   - Corrective Action Items (each with owner, due date, success criteria)
5. **AAR routing:** to QAPI Committee (`QA-PG-001`), Governing Body (`GV-GB-001`), and into the IT DR/BCP review (`IT-DR-001`).
6. **Activation parity:** every actual EP activation also produces an AAR within 30 days.
7. **Tier-1 patient outreach:** during activation, Tier-1 patients are contacted within **4 h**, Tier-2 within **12 h**, Tier-3 within **24 h** — recorded on Addendum D.

## ADDENDUMS (full set)
A: HVA · B: Patient EP Tier Roster · C: Communication Cascade Test Log · D: Activation Cascade Worksheet · E: Patient EP Education Sheet · F: AAR Template · G: Cease-Operations Contingency Plan.

---

# QA-AE-001 — Incident Reporting → RCA → QAPI (Corridor §6-002)

## PROCEDURE — Sentinel-Event Loop (additive)
1. **Intake.** Any incident (patient harm, near-miss, complaint, equipment failure, exposure, vehicle accident, unsafe-visit) is logged within **24 h** of identification on the agency Incident Report (form referenced by `RM-OS-002`).
2. **Triage.** Compliance Officer or QAPI Coordinator categorizes:
   - **Sentinel** (death, permanent harm, major permanent loss of function unrelated to natural course of illness): RCA within 24 h.
   - **Serious adverse event:** RCA within 5 business days.
   - **Other:** trended, no individual RCA unless cluster identified.
3. **Root Cause Analysis.** RCA worksheet (Addendum QA-AE-001.A) documents: chronology, contributing factors, root cause(s), system vs. human factors, corrective actions with owner/due-date.
4. **30-day action plan** presented to QAPI Committee.
5. **90-day closure verification** by QAPI Coordinator with measurable evidence the corrective action was effective.
6. **Governing Body reporting** of all sentinel events at the next quarterly meeting (`GV-GB-001`).
7. **External reporting:** notify ACHC for sentinel events per accreditation manual; CDPH for any reportable event under Title 22 §74725.

## ADDENDUMS
A: RCA Worksheet · B: Sentinel Event Notification Template.

---

# CL-CP-001 — Plan of Care Verbal-Order Readback & 72-Hour Cosign (Corridor §4-002 / §4-003)

## PROCEDURE — Verbal Orders (additive)
1. **Receipt.** Only an RN may accept a verbal/telephone order from a certifying practitioner.
2. **Readback.** The RN repeats back the full order — drug, dose, route, frequency, duration, indication — and the practitioner confirms verbatim.
3. **Documentation.** RN dates, times, and signs the order in the EHR; logs it on Addendum B *Verbal Order Log*.
4. **Practitioner cosign.** The order is sent for practitioner signature and **counter-signed within 72 hours** (CoP §484.60(b)).
5. **Tracking.** Outstanding verbal orders >72 h appear on the Clinical Manager's daily exception report; trended in QAPI dashboard.

---

# OP-IM-002 — Grievance Process Timeliness (Corridor §2-008)

## PROCEDURE — Grievance Lifecycle (additive)
1. **Intake within 1 business day** of complaint receipt — verbal or written, from any source — logged on Addendum B *Grievance Log*.
2. **Patient acknowledgment within 5 business days** with: investigator name, expected timeline, escalation path (State Hotline 1-800-228-1363, ACHC complaint line 855-937-2242).
3. **Investigation** by Compliance Officer or designee independent of involved staff.
4. **Closure within 30 calendar days**; if delayed, written interim update with reason and revised closure date.
5. **Abuse / neglect / exploitation / misappropriation:** reported to **Adult Protective Services** and **CDPH** immediately; involved personnel removed from patient assignment pending investigation per `HR-ER-001` / `HR-ER-002`.
6. **QAPI trending:** monthly volume, type, time-to-close, substantiation rate.

---

# RM-ER-003 — Bloodborne Pathogens & Hep B Exposure Control (Corridor §6-029)

## PROCEDURE — Exposure & Hep B (additive)
1. **Exposure Control Plan** reviewed annually (29 CFR §1910.1030(c)).
2. **Hepatitis B vaccine** offered free to every at-risk employee within **10 working days of assignment**; declination signed and retained.
3. **Post-exposure response:** source patient and exposed worker tested within **2 hours**; PEP started per CDC guidance when indicated.
4. **Sharps log** maintained per OSHA Needlestick Safety Act; reviewed by IPC quarterly.
5. **Annual BBP training** documented on `HR-TD-001`.

---

# RM-ER-004 — TB Exposure Control (Corridor §6-028)

## PROCEDURE — TB (additive)
1. **Annual TB risk assessment** of patient population and personnel exposure.
2. **Baseline two-step TST or single IGRA** at hire for all clinical personnel (CDC 2019 update).
3. **Annual symptom screen** for all clinical personnel; serial testing only when annual risk assessment classifies the agency as medium/high risk.
4. **Conversion** triggers 30-day clinical evaluation, contact investigation, and reporting per CDPH.

---

# CO-HP-004 — HIPAA Breach Notification Timeline (Corridor §2-016)

## PROCEDURE — Breach Notification (additive, 45 CFR §164.404–§164.408)
1. **Discovery → risk assessment** completed within **5 business days**.
2. **Patient notification:** without unreasonable delay and **no later than 60 calendar days** from discovery; written, by first-class mail (or email if patient consented).
3. **HHS OCR notification:**
   - Breach affecting **≥500 individuals**: report **within 60 calendar days** of discovery and notify prominent local media.
   - Breach affecting **<500 individuals**: log internally and submit to OCR **within 60 days of the end of the calendar year**.
4. **Business Associate breach** triggers BA notice obligations within the BAA.
5. **Sanctions:** Disciplinary action per `HR-ER-001` policy; mandatory retraining.

## Policies/extracted_full/DOMAIN_ CL — Clinical Operations (6).md

# DOMAIN: CL — Clinical Operations
## CL-CP-001 — Plan of Care Development & Approval
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-001 |
| Policy Title | Plan of Care Development & Approval |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for developing, approving, implementing, and maintaining an individualized plan of care (POC) for every patient admitted to home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The plan of care is the foundational clinical document that authorizes, defines, and guides all services delivered to a patient during a certification period. It is simultaneously a clinical roadmap, a legal authorization for skilled services, and a billing instrument — any deficiency in its development, physician approval, or content directly compromises patient safety, regulatory compliance, and reimbursement integrity.
This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.60 — Condition of Participation: Care Planning, Coordination, and Quality of Care, which mandates that a plan of care be established and periodically reviewed by a physician for every patient receiving home health services. It also ensures compliance with CMS PDGM episode management requirements, OASIS data collection obligations, and the agency's documentation and billing alignment standards.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) responsible for completing the comprehensive assessment and establishing the plan of care
All clinical disciplines contributing to the plan of care (PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA)
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All intake and admissions staff who initiate the plan of care process
Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and approve plans of care
The Medical Records and Health Information staff
The Revenue Cycle team responsible for billing based on the approved plan of care
This policy applies at Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), and Recertification (RECERT) for every patient served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It does not govern individual visit notes, which are governed by CL-CD-001, or OASIS-specific data collection requirements, which are governed by CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall establish a written, individualized plan of care for every patient admitted to home health services prior to or at the initiation of services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a).
4.2 The plan of care shall be developed by the registered nurse responsible for the patient's care in collaboration with the patient, the patient's caregiver(s), the patient's attending physician or allowed practitioner, and all clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care.
4.3 No skilled home health services shall be provided to a patient without a physician-approved plan of care. Verbal orders for services may be initiated prior to written physician signature, provided the verbal order is received, documented, and authenticated in compliance with policy CL-CP-004 (Verbal Order Receipt & Authentication).
4.4 The plan of care shall be signed and dated by the physician or allowed practitioner before the agency submits a claim for Medicare home health services. For initial certification periods, the physician must sign the plan of care — which may be the OASIS-generated CMS-485 or equivalent — within the timeframe required by CMS.
4.5 The plan of care shall contain all elements required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a), as defined in Section 5 of this policy and detailed in Appendix A.
4.6 The plan of care shall be patient-centered, based on the findings of the comprehensive assessment (CL-CA-001), and shall reflect the patient's goals, functional limitations, and individual clinical needs.
4.7 No services shall be provided that are not authorized by the plan of care and a corresponding physician order. Any service not reflected in the current plan of care requires a new or amended physician order before the service is rendered, except in clinical emergencies where safety requires immediate action followed by immediate physician notification per CL-CP-003.
4.8 The plan of care shall be reviewed, revised, and recertified at least every 60 calendar days and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification, per policy CL-CP-002.
4.9 The physician-approved plan of care, the OASIS assessment, the physician orders, and all visit documentation must be internally consistent. Discrepancies between these documents constitute documentation integrity failures governed by policy CO-DC-004.
4.10 Only the most current physician-approved version of a patient's plan of care shall be operative. Superseded plan versions shall be retained in the clinical record but clearly marked as no longer active.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Plan of Care (POC) | The written document, established by the home health agency and approved by the physician, that specifies the patient's diagnosis, functional limitations, types and frequency of services to be furnished, medications, treatments, safety measures, and patient goals. Referred to in CMS documentation as the CMS-485 or Home Health Certification and Plan of Care. |
| Physician | A doctor of medicine (MD) or osteopathy (DO) legally authorized to practice medicine. For home health purposes, the physician responsible for signing the plan of care must not be employed by or have a financial relationship with the agency that would constitute a violation of the Stark Law, per 42 CFR § 424.22. |
| Allowed Practitioner | A nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) who is working in collaboration with a physician in accordance with state law, and who is authorized under 42 CFR § 424.22 to certify eligibility for home health services and approve the plan of care. |
| Certification Period | A period of not more than 60 calendar days during which the physician certifies that the patient is eligible for home health services. Each certification period requires a signed plan of care. |
| Start of Care (SOC) | The first billable visit made to a patient who has been admitted for a new episode of home health care. |
| Resumption of Care (ROC) | The first billable visit following a patient's return to the agency after an inpatient facility stay. |
| Recertification (RECERT) | The process of renewing a patient's plan of care for a subsequent 60-day certification period, based on a physician's determination that the patient continues to meet eligibility criteria and requires ongoing skilled services. |
| Verbal Order | An oral communication from a physician or allowed practitioner to a qualified clinician that authorizes a specific clinical action, governed by policy CL-CP-004. |
| CMS-485 | The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care form, or its electronic equivalent in the agency's EHR, that serves as the formal plan of care document for Medicare billing purposes. |
| PDGM | Patient-Driven Groupings Model — the Medicare home health prospective payment system that classifies patients into payment categories based on clinical grouping, functional level, comorbidity adjustments, and admission source, all of which are derived from the plan of care and OASIS assessment. |
| Homebound Status | The condition of a patient who has a condition due to an illness or injury that restricts their ability to leave home except with considerable effort, as defined in 42 CFR § 409.42(a). Homebound status must be certified by the physician and documented in the plan of care. |
| Individualized | Tailored to the specific needs, goals, diagnoses, functional limitations, and living situation of each patient, as opposed to a standardized or template-driven approach without patient-specific modifications. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Initiating the Plan of Care Process at Start of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Intake Staff / Administrator | Upon acceptance of a referral and determination that the patient meets admission criteria per OP-IM-002, assign the case to a qualified registered nurse for the comprehensive assessment and plan of care development. Ensure the patient's attending physician has been identified and contact information is documented in the intake record. | At the time of referral acceptance; assignment made no later than 1 business day before the scheduled SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Prior to the SOC visit, review all available referral documentation including hospital discharge summaries, physician orders, medication lists, recent laboratory results, and any therapy evaluations, to prepare for the comprehensive assessment. Do not pre-populate the plan of care with information that has not been verified through direct patient assessment. | Before the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Conduct the comprehensive assessment at the SOC visit in compliance with policy CL-CA-001, including completion of all required OASIS data elements per policies CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019. The SOC visit must occur within 48 hours of the referral or on the physician-ordered start date, whichever is earlier. | Within 48 hours of referral or on the physician-ordered start date. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | During or immediately following the SOC comprehensive assessment, develop the patient-specific plan of care incorporating: (a) all diagnoses, including the primary diagnosis and relevant secondary diagnoses supported by clinical documentation; (b) patient-specific functional limitations; (c) all skilled services ordered including discipline type, frequency, and duration; (d) medications including a complete medication list with dosages; (e) treatments and procedures; (f) safety measures; (g) patient goals — short-term and long-term, stated in measurable and patient-centered terms; (h) physician-ordered equipment and supplies; (i) patient/caregiver education needs and plan; (j) homebound status narrative. | Developed during or immediately following the SOC visit; documented in the EHR within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Collaborate with the patient and caregiver(s) in developing the plan of care. Document the patient's participation in goal-setting and any patient preferences, cultural considerations, or language access needs that affect the plan. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Identify all clinical disciplines needed based on the assessment findings. If additional disciplines are indicated (PT, OT, SLP, MSW), place orders per the physician referral or secure a verbal order per CL-CP-004 and document the referral to those disciplines within the plan of care. | Within 24 hours of the SOC assessment. |

#### 6.2 Required Elements of the Plan of Care
The plan of care for each patient shall contain, at minimum, all of the following elements as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a) and CMS billing requirements. Absence of any required element constitutes a documentation deficiency subject to correction per CO-DC-003.

| Required Element | Content Standard | Policy Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient identifying information | Full legal name, date of birth, Medicare/Medicaid number, address, emergency contact | CL-CA-001 |
| Attending physician | Name, NPI, address, telephone | CL-CP-003 |
| Certification period | Start and end dates of the 60-day episode | CL-CP-008 |
| Diagnoses | Primary diagnosis (the condition chiefly responsible for the patient's need for home health) and all relevant secondary diagnoses, coded to the highest level of specificity per ICD-10-CM | FN-CM-002 |
| Homebound status | Narrative description of the patient's homebound status with specific functional limitations | CL-CA-005 |
| Types and frequency of services | Each discipline ordered (RN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA), visit frequency per week or month, and estimated duration | CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-008 |
| Medications | Complete medication list including drug name, dose, route, frequency, and purpose | CL-SD-012 |
| Treatments and procedures | All skilled clinical interventions ordered (wound care, IV therapy, etc.) | CL-SD-010, CL-SD-011 |
| Safety measures | Environmental safety, fall risk precautions, high-risk medication monitoring | CL-SD-015, RM-PS-001 |
| Patient goals | Measurable short-term and long-term goals, patient-centered and time-bound | CL-CA-001 |
| Equipment and supplies | DME and supply items ordered | OP-SL-004 |
| Patient/caregiver education | Topics to be addressed and teaching plan | CL-SD-017 |
| Physician signature and date | Must be signed and dated by the certifying physician or allowed practitioner | CL-CP-003 |
| Prognosis | Physician's prognosis for restoration of normal health | 42 CFR § 484.60(a) |

#### 6.3 Physician Approval Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Within 24 hours of finalizing the plan of care in the EHR, transmit the plan of care to the patient's certifying physician for review, approval, and signature. Transmission shall be via fax, secure electronic transmission, or physician portal. Document the date, method, and recipient of transmission in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of POC finalization; documented at time of transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Initiate tracking of the pending physician signature in the agency's physician order tracking system per policy CL-CP-009. Log the date transmitted, the physician's name and fax/contact number, and the expected return date. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.3.3 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 7 calendar days of transmission, initiate the first follow-up contact. Document the follow-up attempt including date, time, method, and person contacted. | 7 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.4 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 14 calendar days of transmission, escalate to the Director of Nursing for second-level follow-up. The Director of Nursing or designee shall contact the physician's office directly by telephone and document the conversation. | 14 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | If no signed plan of care is received within 21 calendar days of transmission despite documented follow-up, escalate to the Administrator. Assess whether continued services are appropriate pending physician signature. Document all escalation actions. | 21 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.6 | Revenue Cycle / Director of Nursing | The agency shall not submit a final claim for a Medicare home health episode until a signed plan of care is on file for that episode. Verbal orders initiating care are permissible, but billing requires a signed plan of care. If the physician signature is not obtained, the episode is not billable and the Director of Nursing and Revenue Cycle Director must determine whether services should be discontinued. | Before claim submission for each episode. |
| 6.3.7 | Medical Records | File the signed plan of care in the patient's clinical record within 3 calendar days of receipt. Verify that the physician signature is dated, legible or accompanied by printed name and NPI, and covers the full certification period. Flag any unsigned, undated, or electronically unsigned plans of care for Director of Nursing review before filing. | Within 3 calendar days of receipt. |

#### 6.4 Multidisciplinary Coordination in Plan of Care Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Ensure that all disciplines providing services to the patient have reviewed the plan of care and that their discipline-specific goals, interventions, and visit frequencies are accurately reflected. No discipline shall provide services that conflict with or exceed what is authorized in the plan of care without a new physician order. | Within 48 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Each Clinical Discipline Provider | Upon receiving a referral for a new patient, review the plan of care within 24 hours of assignment. Confirm that the ordered services are within the discipline's scope of practice, are clinically appropriate based on the OASIS assessment and available records, and are supported by a current physician order. If any ordered service appears clinically inappropriate or outside scope, immediately contact the Director of Nursing. | Within 24 hours of assignment. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Serve as the primary coordinator for the patient's plan of care. Document all clinical communications regarding the plan of care in the patient's clinical record. Any discipline-specific addition, modification, or concern regarding the plan of care shall be communicated to the assigned RN, who will coordinate with the physician per CL-CP-003. | Ongoing throughout the certification period. |
| 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing | Conduct or ensure that a care coordination communication occurs among all disciplines involved in the patient's care no later than 14 calendar days after SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. The communication may occur via telephone, secure messaging, or a documented care conference. Document the date, participants, topics discussed, and any plan of care modifications agreed upon. | Within 14 calendar days of SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. |

#### 6.5 Patient and Caregiver Engagement in Plan of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, review the plan of care with the patient and caregiver(s) in plain language, ensuring they understand: (a) the services that will be provided and their frequency; (b) the goals of care; (c) their rights related to care decisions, including the right to refuse services; (d) how to contact the agency with questions or concerns; (e) safety measures specific to their condition and home environment. Provide the patient with a written copy of the plan of care or a plain-language summary in the patient's primary language. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Document the patient's and caregiver's understanding of and participation in the plan of care, including any expressed disagreements with specific goals or services, any modifications made based on patient preference (within physician-ordered parameters), and any language access services provided per OP-PA-003. | In the SOC visit note within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | If the patient or caregiver declines a specific ordered service, document the refusal per the agency's informed refusal process, notify the physician, and assess whether the refusal affects the patient's eligibility for continued home health services. | Immediately upon refusal; physician notification within 24 hours. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care is incomplete or missing required elements at the time of the first billable visit | Assigned RN escalates to Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing reviews and requires completion before any claim is submitted. Services may continue if the verbal order is properly documented per CL-CP-004. | Completion required before claim submission. |
| Physician refuses to sign the plan of care as written | Assigned RN and Director of Nursing contact the physician | Director of Nursing engages the physician to resolve clinical disagreements. Modify the plan of care per the physician's direction if clinically appropriate. If the physician declines to certify the patient at all, initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006. | Resolution within 7 calendar days of refusal. |
| Patient refuses to participate in plan of care development | Assigned RN documents refusal and notifies Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses whether the patient's capacity to refuse is intact. Engage the patient's legal representative if capacity is in question. Document refusal, actions taken, and outcome. | Immediate documentation; assessment within 24 hours. |
| Services are being delivered that are not reflected in the plan of care | Director of Nursing identifies the discrepancy | Stop non-authorized services immediately. Obtain a verbal or written physician order for any service that should have been included. Review for billing compliance with Revenue Cycle Director per CO-DC-004. Report to Compliance Officer if billing has already occurred. | Stop services immediately; order obtained within 24 hours; compliance review within 5 business days. |
| Plan of care is submitted to the physician but cannot be located in the record | Clinical Coordinator escalates to Director of Nursing | Conduct a full audit trail review in the EHR. If the plan of care was transmitted but not returned, re-transmit. If there is a gap in the audit trail, assess for data integrity concerns per CO-DC-001 and report to Compliance Officer. | Audit trail review within 3 business days of identification. |

### 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Completed plan of care | Patient-specific plan of care including all required elements per Section 6.2 | Assigned RN | EHR — patient clinical record | Developed within 24 hours of SOC visit; retained for minimum 7 years per CO-HP-007 |
| Physician-signed plan of care | Signed and dated CMS-485 or EHR equivalent | Certifying physician / Medical Records | EHR — patient clinical record | Received and filed before claim submission; retained minimum 7 years |
| Plan of care transmission record | Documentation of date, method, and recipient of transmission to physician | Clinical Coordinator | EHR — orders tracking module | At time of transmission; retained minimum 7 years |
| Physician follow-up documentation | Records of all follow-up contacts for pending signatures | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | EHR — orders tracking module | At each follow-up attempt; retained minimum 7 years |
| Patient/caregiver education and participation | Documentation in the SOC visit note of plan of care review with patient, patient's understanding, and any modifications | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours of SOC visit |
| Multidisciplinary care coordination | Documentation of care coordination communications per Section 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing / Assigned RN | EHR — care coordination notes | Within 14 calendar days of SOC for qualifying patients |
| Plan of care modifications | All mid-episode plan modifications with supporting physician orders | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | EHR — orders and plan of care | Within 24 hours of modification; physician order obtained before service change |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment of this policy by all personnel within scope (Appendix B) | Each individual (completion); Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of policy effective date, revision, or new hire |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans of care contain all required elements per 42 CFR § 484.60(a) | Monthly audit of a random sample of SOC plans of care using the Documentation Audit Tool (Appendix C) | ≥95% of audited plans contain all required elements; 100% target |
| Plans of care are physician-signed before claim submission | Cross-reference of billing records with physician signature dates in the EHR | Zero claims submitted without a signed plan of care on file |
| Plans of care are developed within 24 hours of SOC visit | Audit of POC finalization dates against SOC visit dates | ≥95% of SOC plans finalized within 24 hours of the SOC visit |
| Physician follow-up is documented for all unsigned plans | Review of the orders tracking module for plans pending signature longer than 7 days | All plans pending signature longer than 7 days have documented follow-up attempts |
| Patient participation in plan of care is documented | Review of SOC visit notes for patient engagement documentation | ≥95% of SOC visit notes document patient/caregiver participation in plan of care review |
| Plan of care is consistent with OASIS assessment and physician orders | Triangulation audit per CO-DC-004 | Zero tolerance for material inconsistencies between POC, OASIS, and orders on audited records |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60):
Evidence that a plan of care exists for every patient. Surveyors will request clinical records and verify that a written, physician-approved plan of care exists for each active patient and for each certification period of sampled past patients. Missing plans of care or unsigned plans are Condition-level deficiency risks.
Evidence that the plan of care contains all required elements. Surveyors will review plans of care for completeness per 42 CFR § 484.60(a). Commonly cited deficiencies include: missing homebound status narrative, vague or unmeasurable goals, incomplete medication lists, and visit frequencies that do not match delivered services.
Evidence that the plan of care is patient-centered and individualized. Surveyors distinguish between plans that are genuinely tailored to the patient and plans that appear to be templated without individualization. Cookie-cutter goal language (e.g., "patient will improve") without patient-specific metrics is a common deficiency.
Evidence of physician approval. Surveyors will verify physician signatures on plans of care and cross-reference with service dates to confirm that signed plans of care predate or accompany the services billed. Surveys will also verify that the certifying physician is eligible (not employed by or financially related to the agency in a prohibited manner).
Evidence that the plan of care is consistent with services delivered. Surveyors will compare ordered visit frequencies against actual visit delivery records. Significant and unexplained variances are cited as documentation integrity failures and potential False Claims Act concerns.
Evidence of patient participation. Surveyors may interview patients and caregivers about their knowledge of their plan of care and whether they were involved in developing their goals.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care developed by non-RN staff or templated without individualization | CMS deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.60; potential False Claims Act risk | Require RN development of all SOC plans of care; Director of Nursing conducts quality review of new SOC plans |
| Goals stated in non-measurable terms ("patient will improve ADLs") | Survey citation for inadequate plan of care; inability to demonstrate outcome achievement | Train all RNs on SMART goal-writing; use goal templates with required metrics |
| Services delivered that are not on the plan of care | Billing compliance risk; potential False Claims Act; survey deficiency | Implement visit authorization checking in scheduling system; audit monthly per CO-DC-004 |
| Physician signature obtained but not retained in clinical record | Missing documentation during survey; inability to support billing | Implement document receipt verification workflow; Director of Nursing reviews all unsigned episode records weekly |
| Plan of care not updated following significant change in patient condition | Clinical risk; documentation integrity failure | Train all clinicians on significant change criteria; Director of Nursing reviews mid-episode plan changes quarterly |
| Visit frequency on the plan of care does not match OASIS functional level | PDGM classification error; potential overpayment or underpayment; billing compliance risk | Conduct OASIS-to-POC consistency check at each SOC before claim submission per CO-DC-004 |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All registered nurses responsible for conducting SOC assessments and developing plans of care shall receive competency-validated training on plan of care development requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall be conducted by the Director of Nursing or a qualified designee and shall include: (a) all required elements of the plan of care per 42 CFR § 484.60(a); (b) ICD-10 primary diagnosis selection for PDGM; (c) SMART goal-writing for home health; (d) physician order management and the verbal order process; (e) plan of care transmission and tracking; (f) common survey deficiencies and how to avoid them; (g) the agency's EHR plan of care workflow.
10.2 All other clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) shall receive orientation to plan of care processes relevant to their discipline-specific contributions within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) how to read and confirm the plan of care; (b) their obligation not to deliver services outside the plan of care; (c) how to initiate a discipline-specific order change request through the assigned RN.
10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.
10.4 The Director of Nursing shall verify training completion and competency for all RNs in plan of care development prior to their independently conducting SOC assessments. Competency shall be documented using the SOC Competency Assessment Tool (Appendix D).
### 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.
