## CL-CP-005 — Coordination of Care
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-005 |
| Policy Title | Coordination of Care |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy mandates the coordination of services among all disciplines involved in a patient's care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and with external providers — including physicians, hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, pharmacies, community agencies, and other healthcare entities — involved in the patient's overall care. Coordination of care is not merely a documentation requirement; it is a clinical and ethical imperative that directly affects patient outcomes, patient safety, and the efficiency of care delivery. Fragmented care — where disciplines operate in silos, where the attending physician is not kept current on the patient's status, or where the home health team is unaware of care provided by other providers — creates clinical risk, medication errors, unnecessary hospitalizations, and documentation inconsistencies that threaten billing integrity. This policy ensures that Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. operates as a fully integrated member of the patient's care team at all times.
This policy implements the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.60(c) — Standard: Coordination of Care, which requires that the agency coordinates services provided and makes referrals to appropriate community resources.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses managing patient care
All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) providing patient services
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Medical Social Worker (primary community resource coordination role)
Operations staff managing scheduling and visit logistics
The attending physician and referring providers
Intake and discharge planning staff
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall ensure that all services provided to each patient are coordinated among all disciplines involved in the patient's care and with all external providers who contribute to the patient's overall health management.
4.2 The assigned registered nurse shall serve as the primary care coordinator for each patient, responsible for ensuring that all disciplines contributing to the patient's care are aware of the current plan of care, recent clinical changes, and the patient's progress toward goals.
4.3 Care coordination shall be documented in the patient's clinical record and shall include: (a) interdisciplinary communications regarding clinical status, plan changes, and goal progress; (b) communications with the attending physician, including all notifications of significant changes; (c) communications with external providers including hospitals, SNFs, pharmacies, and community agencies; (d) referrals to community resources.
4.4 The agency shall maintain ongoing, proactive communication with the patient's attending physician throughout the episode. At minimum, the physician shall be notified of: (a) any significant change in the patient's condition; (b) any new diagnosis identified during home health; (c) any medication concern or adverse reaction; (d) any patient safety risk identified during home assessment; (e) the patient's progress at recertification; (f) the patient's discharge status and estimated discharge date.
4.5 When a patient is transitioning from an inpatient setting to home health, the agency shall obtain and review all available discharge documentation, including discharge summaries, medication reconciliation records, and follow-up physician appointment schedules, to ensure continuity of the care plan.
4.6 The Medical Social Worker (MSW), when involved in a patient's care, shall serve as the primary coordinator for community resource referrals, support service linkage, and psychosocial needs coordination.
4.7 A formal interdisciplinary care coordination communication shall occur no later than 14 calendar days after SOC for any patient receiving three or more disciplines, and at any point when a significant change in condition occurs.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Coordination of Care | The deliberate organization of patient care activities between two or more participants (including the patient) involved in a patient's care to facilitate the appropriate delivery of health care services, sharing information among participants concerning patient needs, and using that information to maximize the quality and effectiveness of delivered care. |
| Interdisciplinary Communication | Clinical communication among two or more members of the patient's care team that occurs with the explicit purpose of coordinating the patient's plan of care, sharing clinical findings, or addressing care concerns. |
| Care Conference | A structured, documented communication event involving two or more clinical disciplines and/or the patient and caregiver, organized around a specific clinical coordination purpose. |
| External Provider | Any healthcare entity or professional outside of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. that is involved in the patient's care, including the attending physician, specialists, hospitals, SNFs, pharmacies, community agencies, and home medical equipment suppliers. |
| Referral | A documented recommendation or request by the agency for the patient to receive services from an external provider or community resource. |
| Warm Handoff | A care transition in which a member of the sending care team directly communicates with a member of the receiving care team to transfer patient care information, as distinct from a written record transfer alone. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Internal Interdisciplinary Coordination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | At SOC, review the patient's plan of care with each clinical discipline involved in the patient's care within 48 hours of the SOC visit. The communication shall include: (a) the patient's primary diagnosis and relevant co-morbidities; (b) the current plan of care including all ordered services and frequencies for each discipline; (c) the patient's functional status and goals; (d) any known safety concerns; (e) the patient's caregiver situation and any limitations to care delivery. | Within 48 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Document the SOC interdisciplinary communication in the clinical record. For patients with three or more disciplines, convene a care conference within 14 calendar days of SOC and document the conference including: date, participants, topics discussed, and any plan modifications agreed upon. | SOC communication within 48 hours; care conference within 14 calendar days for patients with three or more disciplines. |
| 6.1.3 | Any Discipline Provider | When a clinician from any discipline identifies a clinical finding, change, or concern during a patient visit that is relevant to other disciplines or to the overall care plan, communicate the finding to the assigned RN within 24 hours. Document the communication in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of the visit at which the finding was made. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Following any mid-episode care conference or significant communication, update the patient's clinical record with a Care Coordination Note documenting: (a) the parties involved; (b) the clinical issues discussed; (c) any plan modifications; (d) any referrals made; (e) any follow-up actions with assigned responsible parties and timelines. | Within 24 hours of the communication. |
| 6.1.5 | Director of Nursing | Review care coordination documentation during the monthly supervisory review of all active patient records. Identify any patient where there is no documented interdisciplinary communication within the past 30 calendar days and direct the assigned RN to conduct and document care coordination. | Monthly. |

#### 6.2 Physician Communication

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | Notify the attending physician within 24 hours of identifying any of the following: (a) significant change in the patient's condition per CL-CP-002; (b) a new clinical diagnosis or finding; (c) a medication concern, adverse reaction, or potential interaction; (d) a patient safety risk identified during the home assessment per RM-PS-001; (e) a patient refusal of ordered services; (f) a missed visit that affects the patient's clinical care continuity. | Within 24 hours of the identified event. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | At a minimum of every 30 calendar days, provide the attending physician with a clinical status update including: (a) the patient's current functional status and progress toward goals; (b) any concerns about the patient's trajectory; (c) the estimated discharge timeline and criteria; (d) any community resources or referrals provided. The update may be transmitted via fax, secure messaging, or telephone with documentation. | Every 30 calendar days; documented in the clinical record. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | Document all physician communications in the clinical record, including: (a) the date and time of the communication; (b) the name of the physician or physician office contact; (c) the method of communication; (d) the information communicated; (e) the physician's response or any orders received; (f) any follow-up actions agreed upon. | Within 24 hours of each communication. |

#### 6.3 Transition from Inpatient Setting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | For all patients transitioning from a hospital or SNF to home health, obtain from the sending facility: (a) the discharge summary (or, if not yet available, a transfer summary or face sheet); (b) the current medication reconciliation list; (c) any pending laboratory or diagnostic test results; (d) follow-up physician appointments scheduled; (e) any pending specialist referrals; (f) a list of all care providers seen during the inpatient stay. If documentation is not available at the time of the SOC visit, contact the facility directly and document the request. | Obtained before or at the SOC visit; if unavailable, requested within 24 hours of SOC. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, compare the patient's current status, current medications, and current home environment against the discharge documentation. Document any discrepancies identified and notify the attending physician within 24 hours of any clinically significant discrepancies per CL-OA-013. | At the SOC visit; physician notification within 24 hours of clinically significant discrepancies. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Confirm that the patient has a scheduled follow-up appointment with the attending physician within 7–14 days of discharge (or within the timeframe recommended by the discharging facility or CMS). If no appointment is scheduled, assist the patient and caregiver in scheduling and document the appointment date. | At the SOC visit; documented in the clinical record. |

#### 6.4 External Provider Coordination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | MSW / Assigned RN | Identify all community resources, services, and external providers relevant to the patient's needs at SOC or as needs emerge during the episode. Community resources may include: senior transportation services, meal delivery programs, adult day health programs, support groups, financial assistance programs, community mental health services, and homemaker services. | At SOC; ongoing as needs are identified. |
| 6.4.2 | MSW / Assigned RN | Facilitate referrals to appropriate community resources and external providers. Document all referrals in the clinical record including: (a) the resource or provider; (b) the reason for referral; (c) the date the referral was made; (d) the method of referral; (e) the patient's response; (f) confirmation of referral acceptance where obtainable. | Within 48 hours of identifying the referral need; documented at the time of referral. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | When a patient is also receiving services from other home health disciplines not provided by the agency (e.g., a contracted therapy provider), ensure that those external providers receive the current plan of care and that the results of their services are communicated back to the assigned RN and incorporated into care coordination documentation. | At the time of external discipline engagement; ongoing communication throughout the episode. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN | When a patient is discharged to another setting (hospital, SNF, hospice, or another home health agency), provide a warm handoff by telephone or secure communication to the receiving provider, in addition to the written clinical summary required by CL-CP-006 and CL-CP-007. Document the warm handoff. | On or before the date of transfer or discharge. |

#### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Physician is non-responsive to care coordination communications | Director of Nursing escalates after two unanswered contacts | Director of Nursing contacts the physician's office administrator or practice manager directly. If patient safety is at risk, Director of Nursing may contact covering physician or on-call physician. Documents all attempts. | Director of Nursing escalation after second unanswered contact; immediately for patient safety concerns. |
| Two or more disciplines are providing conflicting care instructions to the patient | Director of Nursing convenes an urgent care conference | Director of Nursing facilitates an interdisciplinary care conference within 48 hours, identifies the source of the conflict, resolves the discrepancy with physician guidance, and ensures consistent updated instructions are communicated to the patient. Documents resolution. | Care conference within 48 hours. |
| Community resource referral is declined or unavailable | MSW / Assigned RN documents and identifies alternatives | Document the barrier and identify at least one alternative resource. If no suitable alternative is available, notify the Director of Nursing and attending physician. | Within 5 business days of the referral barrier identification. |

### 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SOC interdisciplinary communication | Care Coordination Note in clinical record | Assigned RN | EHR — coordination notes | Within 48 hours of SOC |
| Care conference documentation | Structured care conference note including participants and outcomes | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | EHR — coordination notes | Within 24 hours of conference |
| Physician communication notes | Documentation of all physician contacts per Section 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | Within 24 hours of each contact |
| Transition documentation receipt | Documentation of receipt of inpatient discharge documents | Assigned RN | EHR — transition notes | At SOC; request documented within 24 hours if unavailable |
| Community resource referrals | Referral documentation per Section 6.4.2 | MSW / Assigned RN | EHR — referral notes | Within 48 hours of referral |
| Warm handoff documentation | Documentation of verbal communication with receiving provider at transfer or discharge | Assigned RN | EHR — transition notes | On or before date of transfer |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix A) | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interdisciplinary care conference documented within 14 days for patients with 3+ disciplines | Audit of care coordination notes and conference dates | ≥95% of qualifying patients with documented care conference within 14 calendar days of SOC |
| All significant changes result in physician notification within 24 hours | Audit of physician communication notes against visit notes with documented clinical changes | ≥95% compliance |
| All community resource referrals documented | Audit of referral documentation in clinical records | ≥95% of referrals documented with required elements |
| Warm handoffs documented for all transfers and discharges | Audit of transition documentation | ≥95% of transfers and discharges with documented warm handoff |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will examine care coordination documentation under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60). They will interview patients and caregivers to assess whether the patient felt their care was coordinated and whether the patient knew who to contact with concerns. They will look for documented physician communications, care conferences, and community resource referrals. The absence of physician contact notes in a complex patient's clinical record is a commonly cited deficiency.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Care coordination occurs verbally but is not documented | Survey deficiency; no evidence of coordination | Train all clinicians: "If it isn't documented, it didn't happen"; Director of Nursing audits coordination notes monthly |
| Disciplines operate independently with no documented communication | Fragmented care; patient safety risk; survey citation | Director of Nursing enforces 14-day care conference requirement; supervisory review identifies silos |
| Physician not notified of significant changes in a timely manner | Clinical risk; documentation gap; potential harm | Train all clinicians on 24-hour notification requirement; Director of Nursing reviews significant change events monthly |

10.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on care coordination requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, covering: the 24-hour physician notification requirement; the care conference requirement; community resource referral documentation; and warm handoff procedures.
10.2 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the criteria, processes, and documentation requirements for discharging patients from home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Discharge planning is a clinical process, not an administrative event — it begins at the time of admission and evolves throughout the episode as the patient progresses toward or away from identified goals. A well-executed discharge process ensures that patients leave home health care with the knowledge, support, and community resources necessary to maintain their health independently, that the clinical record reflects a complete and justified basis for discharge, and that the transition to the next setting or self-management is coordinated with the patient, the attending physician, and all relevant external providers.
This policy governs all types of discharges, including: goal-achieved discharges, physician-ordered discharges, patient-initiated discharges (including against medical advice), safety-related discharges, and discharges due to non-compliance. It ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.60, which requires the agency to document the basis for discharge, and with OASIS discharge assessment requirements under CMS guidelines.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses managing active patient caseloads
All clinical disciplines providing services at discharge
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
Medical Social Workers coordinating community resources at discharge
Clinical Coordinators managing discharge scheduling and documentation
Medical Records and Revenue Cycle staff managing discharge OASIS and final billing
The attending physician who must be notified of and, where required, authorize discharge
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Discharge planning shall begin at the time of the Start of Care assessment and shall be an ongoing, documented component of every patient's plan of care throughout the episode.
4.2 Discharge criteria — the specific clinical, functional, and support-system milestones that must be achieved before a patient is safely discharged from home health — shall be identified and documented in the plan of care at SOC, reviewed at every 30-day review, and updated as the patient's condition evolves.
4.3 Discharge shall occur when one or more of the following criteria are met: (a) the patient has achieved the goals established in the plan of care; (b) the patient no longer meets the Medicare homebound status criteria; (c) the physician orders discharge; (d) the patient or legal representative requests discharge; (e) the patient's condition has stabilized to the extent that skilled services are no longer required; (f) the patient has transferred to another care setting (hospital, SNF, hospice, assisted living); (g) the patient has relocated outside the agency's service area; (h) the patient or household poses an unresolvable safety risk to agency staff; (i) the patient is non-compliant with the plan of care in a manner that renders the provision of skilled services clinically meaningless and all reasonable efforts to resolve non-compliance have been exhausted and documented.
4.4 Discharge shall not occur based on: (a) the patient's race, ethnicity, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or religion; (b) the patient's diagnosis alone, without clinical justification; (c) financial considerations, including the patient's inability to pay for non-covered services or the likelihood of a LUPA.
4.5 The attending physician shall be notified of all planned discharges and shall issue a discharge order before the discharge OASIS is completed, except in emergency situations where the patient is transferred to an acute care setting.
4.6 The discharge OASIS assessment shall be completed within the timeframes required by CMS and transmitted to the OASIS database per policy CL-OA-001.
4.7 The patient shall receive a written discharge summary and home safety education appropriate to their discharge status before or at the time of the final visit.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Discharge | The formal termination of a patient's enrollment in home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Discharge Criteria | The specific clinical, functional, and support-system conditions that must be met before a patient is determined to be appropriate for discharge from home health services. |
| Goal-Achieved Discharge | A discharge that occurs because the patient has met the clinical and functional goals established in the plan of care and no longer requires skilled home health services. |
| Physician-Ordered Discharge | A discharge that occurs at the direction of the attending physician, who has determined that home health services are no longer indicated. |
| Patient-Initiated Discharge | A discharge requested by the patient or their legal representative, which may occur at any time regardless of whether the patient has met discharge criteria. |
| Discharge Against Medical Advice (AMA) | A patient-initiated discharge that occurs when the patient chooses to stop home health services despite the clinical team's recommendation to continue. |
| Safety-Related Discharge | A discharge initiated by the agency due to threats, violence, or unresolvable safety hazards in the patient's home that make it unsafe for agency staff to provide care. |
| Discharge OASIS | The OASIS assessment completed at the time of discharge (other than transfer to inpatient facility), documenting the patient's clinical and functional status at the end of the episode. |
| Discharge Summary | A written document provided to the patient at discharge summarizing the patient's progress, final status, discharge instructions, and community resource referrals. |
| Transfer | A move from home health services to an inpatient setting (hospital, SNF, IRF) — governed by policy CL-CP-007. Transfer is distinct from discharge for OASIS and billing purposes. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Discharge Planning Throughout the Episode

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | At SOC, identify and document in the plan of care: (a) the patient's anticipated discharge date (a realistic target based on clinical trajectory, visit frequency, and functional goals); (b) the specific discharge criteria — what the patient must achieve or demonstrate to be safely discharged; (c) the patient's and caregiver's discharge goals and preferences; (d) any anticipated barriers to discharge (caregiver limitations, community resource gaps, chronic conditions requiring ongoing management). | During the SOC visit; documented in the plan of care within 24 hours. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | At every 30-day plan of care review, reassess and update: (a) the estimated discharge date based on the patient's current progress; (b) the status of each discharge criterion — met, partially met, or not yet met; (c) barriers to discharge and the plan to address them; (d) referrals needed for community services post-discharge. | At each 30-day review; documented in the Plan of Care Review Note. |
| 6.1.3 | MSW | When community resources are needed to support discharge, initiate referrals no later than 14 calendar days before the anticipated discharge date, to allow sufficient time for services to be established before the patient is discharged. Document all referrals per CL-CP-005. | At least 14 calendar days before the anticipated discharge. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Begin formal discharge education with the patient and caregiver at least 7 calendar days before the anticipated discharge date, covering: (a) management of the patient's primary condition(s) after discharge; (b) medication management — including all medications, doses, schedules, and adverse effects to report; (c) diet and activity restrictions; (d) signs and symptoms that require physician contact or emergency services; (e) scheduled follow-up physician appointments; (f) community resources established; (g) how to access care if needed after discharge. | At least 7 calendar days before anticipated discharge; final reinforcement at the last visit. |

#### 6.2 Discharge Criteria Assessment and Physician Notification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | When the patient is assessed as meeting discharge criteria, document a Discharge Readiness Assessment in the clinical record, including: (a) specific evidence that each discharge criterion has been met; (b) the patient's final functional status; (c) the patient's and caregiver's readiness and confidence to manage independently; (d) community resources and follow-up appointments confirmed; (e) the clinical rationale supporting discharge. | Within 24 hours of the determination that discharge criteria are met. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | Contact the attending physician within 24 hours of the Discharge Readiness Assessment to report the patient's discharge status and obtain a discharge order. Provide the physician with: (a) a summary of the patient's progress and final status; (b) the basis for the discharge determination; (c) the proposed discharge date; (d) community resources and follow-up arrangements. | Within 24 hours of the discharge readiness determination. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | Obtain a written or verbal physician discharge order. Document the order per CL-CP-003 and CL-CP-004. The physician order shall specify the discharge date and confirm the discharge determination. | Before the discharge OASIS is initiated. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | If the physician disagrees with the discharge determination and does not issue a discharge order, continue services per the physician's direction. Document the physician's clinical rationale in the clinical record. Reassess in no later than 7 calendar days or at the next scheduled visit. | Continue services pending physician resolution; reassess within 7 calendar days. |

#### 6.3 Patient-Initiated Discharge and Discharge Against Medical Advice

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Any Clinician | When a patient or legal representative requests discharge, regardless of whether the patient has met clinical discharge criteria, acknowledge the request and contact the Director of Nursing within 4 hours. | Within 4 hours of the patient's request. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing / Assigned RN | Within 24 hours of the discharge request, the Director of Nursing or assigned RN shall: (a) assess the patient's understanding of the risks of discharge if criteria have not been met; (b) educate the patient on the clinical implications of early discharge; (c) offer alternatives such as a reduced visit schedule, if clinically appropriate; (d) document the patient's informed decision. | Within 24 hours of the discharge request. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | If the patient proceeds with discharge against medical advice, document in the clinical record: (a) that the patient was informed of the clinical risks; (b) the patient's expressed reason for early discharge; (c) the patient's or representative's signature on the AMA form (Appendix A) if obtainable; (d) if the patient declines to sign, a notation that the refusal to sign was documented in the presence of a witness. | Documented at the time of or immediately following the final visit. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | Notify the attending physician of the patient-initiated discharge within 24 hours. Provide the physician with the patient's clinical status at discharge and any ongoing clinical concerns. | Within 24 hours of the discharge. |
| 6.3.5 | Assigned RN | Even for a patient discharged against medical advice, provide the patient with the best possible discharge education and written instructions given the circumstances, and ensure any immediate safety concerns are addressed, including referral to emergency services if indicated. | At or before the final visit. |

#### 6.4 Safety-Related Discharge

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Clinician at the Patient's Home | If a clinician encounters an unsafe situation in the patient's home — including threats, violence, aggressive behavior, criminal activity, or unresolvable environmental hazards — the clinician shall: (a) exit the situation immediately if there is an imminent threat to safety; (b) call 911 if there is an imminent physical threat to anyone; (c) notify the Director of Nursing within 2 hours of the safety event. | Exit immediately if safety is at risk; Director of Nursing notification within 2 hours. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a Safety Risk Assessment within 48 hours of the reported safety event. Assess whether: (a) the safety concern can be resolved through education, alternative scheduling, or care plan modification; (b) staff safety cannot be assured and continuation of visits is not appropriate. | Within 48 hours of the reported event. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing / Administrator | If the Director of Nursing determines that the safety risk is unresolvable, initiate the discharge process. Notify the attending physician within 24 hours. Provide the patient with at least 7 calendar days' advance written notice of discharge (when it is safe to do so), along with information about alternative home health agencies and community resources, to allow the patient sufficient time to arrange alternative care. | Physician notification within 24 hours; patient notification as soon as it is safe to do so; minimum 7 calendar days advance written notice. |
| 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing | Document the full safety event, the safety risk assessment, the physician notification, the patient notification, and all actions taken in the patient's clinical record and in the agency's incident reporting system per RM-ER-002. | Within 24 hours of each event and action. |

#### 6.5 Non-Compliance Discharge

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | When a patient is repeatedly non-compliant with the plan of care (e.g., refusing skilled visits without clinical justification, not following prescribed treatments, refusing medication management) in a manner that renders continued skilled services clinically meaningless, document each instance of non-compliance in the visit note, including: (a) the specific non-compliant behavior; (b) the patient's stated reason; (c) the education and counseling provided; (d) the clinical assessment of the patient's capacity and |  |

# CL-SD-001 — Skilled Nursing Assessment & Services
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-001 |
| Policy Title | Skilled Nursing Assessment & Services |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the scope, frequency, clinical standards, and documentation requirements for skilled nursing assessment and services delivered by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Skilled nursing is the cornerstone of the Medicare home health benefit — it is the discipline most frequently ordered, most frequently surveyed, and most frequently the basis for the patient's initial and continued eligibility for home health services. The skilled nurse's clinical judgment, assessment competency, documentation accuracy, and care coordination are the primary determinants of clinical quality, regulatory compliance, and billing integrity across every episode.
This policy ensures that every skilled nursing visit is conducted with a clear clinical purpose, is documented with the specificity and timeliness required by CMS, and is aligned with the physician-approved plan of care. It implements the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.75 — Condition of Participation: Skilled Professional Services, and the skilled nursing coverage requirements defined in the CMS Home Health Benefit Manual, Chapter 7, § 40.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) providing direct patient care
All licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) providing skilled nursing services under RN supervision and within their California BPC § 2859 scope
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for nursing service oversight
Clinical Coordinators managing nursing visit scheduling
Revenue Cycle staff verifying nursing visit documentation supports billed claims
This policy governs all skilled nursing visits — assessment visits, routine skilled visits, supervisory visits, recertification visits, resumption of care visits, and discharge visits. It does not govern OASIS-specific data collection requirements (CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019), plan of care development (CL-CP-001), or discipline-specific services of other professions (CL-SD-002 through CL-SD-008).
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All skilled nursing services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall be provided by registered nurses (RNs) or licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) who are currently licensed by the California Board of Registered Nursing or the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians, whose licensure status has been verified per HR-TA-004, and who have demonstrated clinical competency per HR-TD-003.
4.2 Every skilled nursing visit shall have a documented clinical purpose that is directly tied to the physician-approved plan of care. No skilled nursing visit shall be conducted without a current, active physician order authorizing the visit per CL-CP-003. Visits without a clinical purpose tied to the plan of care are not billable under Medicare and expose the agency to False Claims Act liability.
4.3 At each skilled nursing visit, the RN or LVN shall perform and document, at minimum: (a) a focused clinical assessment relevant to the patient's diagnoses and plan of care goals; (b) skilled interventions as ordered in the plan of care; (c) an assessment of the patient's response to the interventions provided; (d) patient and caregiver education as indicated; (e) evaluation of progress toward the plan of care goals; (f) communication with the physician or other care team members as clinically warranted.
4.4 The scope of LVN practice at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall be limited to the services permitted under California BPC § 2859, provided under the direction of a registered nurse. LVNs shall not independently perform comprehensive assessments, develop or modify the plan of care, receive verbal orders outside the scope defined in CL-CP-004, complete OASIS assessments, or make clinical judgments that are within the exclusive scope of RN practice.
4.5 The Director of Nursing shall ensure that RN clinical supervision of LVN practice is documented per CL-SD-008 and that LVN caseloads are reviewed at minimum every 14 calendar days.
4.6 All skilled nursing visit documentation shall be completed and locked in the EHR within 24 hours of the visit per CL-CD-004. Documentation shall meet the minimum content standards defined in CL-CD-001 and shall include sufficient clinical detail to support the medical necessity of the visit and the skilled nature of the services provided.
4.7 Skilled nursing services shall be provided at the frequency and duration specified in the physician-approved plan of care. Any deviation from the ordered frequency — whether a missed visit, an additional visit, or a frequency change — shall be managed per CL-SD-024 (missed visits) and CL-SD-025 (ordered visit frequency compliance) and shall require a physician order for any change.
4.8 All skilled nursing visits shall include an assessment of medication management per CL-SD-012, safety hazards per RM-PS-001, and fall risk per CL-SD-015 as part of the standard nursing assessment protocol.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Skilled Nursing Service | A service that requires the skills of a registered nurse or licensed vocational nurse and is reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the patient's illness or injury, as defined in the CMS Home Health Benefit Manual, Chapter 7, § 40. |
| Clinical Purpose | The specific, documented clinical reason for a skilled nursing visit, directly tied to a physician order and the plan of care. |
| Focused Assessment | A clinical assessment targeted to the patient's active diagnoses, current symptoms, and plan of care goals, as distinguished from a comprehensive assessment (which is governed by CL-CA-001). |
| Skilled Intervention | A clinical action that requires the training, skill, and judgment of a licensed nurse — including but not limited to wound care, medication administration, injection administration, IV therapy, catheter management, clinical teaching, assessment and monitoring of unstable conditions, and management of a complex medication regimen. |
| Medical Necessity | The determination that a service is reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of the patient's illness or injury and is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice. |
| Visit Note | The clinical documentation entry created for each skilled nursing visit, meeting the content and timeliness requirements of CL-CD-001 and CL-CD-004. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Pre-Visit Preparation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | Before each visit, review the patient's current plan of care, active physician orders, medication list, recent visit notes from all disciplines, and any outstanding clinical alerts or coordination notes in the EHR. Identify the clinical purpose of the visit and the specific assessments and interventions to be completed. | Before departure for the visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Verify that all supplies, equipment, and educational materials needed for the visit are available and in working condition. If the visit requires specialized supplies (wound care supplies, IV supplies, injection supplies), confirm availability before the visit. | Before departure. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | Verify the patient's address, contact information, and any known access or safety concerns documented in the clinical record per RM-SS-001. | Before departure. |

### 6.2 Skilled Nursing Visit Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | Upon arrival, verify patient identity using two patient identifiers per OP-PA-002. Perform hand hygiene per CL-SD-016. | At the start of each visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Conduct a focused clinical assessment appropriate to the patient's diagnoses and current status, including at minimum: (a) vital signs — blood pressure, pulse, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation (as indicated); (b) pain assessment per CL-SD-014; (c) cardiopulmonary assessment for patients with cardiac or respiratory diagnoses; (d) wound assessment for patients with active wounds per CL-SD-011; (e) neurological assessment for patients with neurological conditions; (f) medication review — compare the patient's actual medication-taking behavior against the prescribed regimen per CL-SD-012; (g) fall risk evaluation per CL-SD-015; (h) home safety assessment per RM-PS-001; (i) psychosocial and behavioral health screening as indicated per CL-SD-022. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | Provide skilled interventions as ordered in the plan of care, including but not limited to: wound care, medication administration, injection administration, IV therapy management, catheter care, ostomy care, diabetic management, cardiac monitoring, respiratory care, and clinical teaching. All interventions shall be performed according to current evidence-based clinical standards and the agency's clinical practice standards. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN / LVN | Assess and document the patient's response to all interventions provided — the patient's tolerance, clinical outcome, and any adverse reactions. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN / LVN | Provide individualized patient and caregiver education as indicated by the plan of care and as warranted by the visit findings. Education topics shall include disease process management, medication management, dietary modifications, activity modifications, self-monitoring techniques, and when to contact the physician or call 911. Document the education provided, the teaching method used, and the patient's/caregiver's level of understanding per CL-SD-017. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.6 | Assigned RN / LVN | Evaluate the patient's progress toward each active goal in the plan of care. Note measurable progress, plateau, or regression for each goal. If the patient is not progressing as anticipated, assess the barriers and determine whether a plan of care modification is needed per CL-CP-002. | During the visit. |
| 6.2.7 | Assigned RN / LVN | If the assessment reveals a significant change in the patient's condition, a new clinical finding, a medication concern, or a safety risk, notify the attending physician within 24 hours per CL-CP-005 and initiate a plan of care modification as warranted per CL-CP-002. If the finding is urgent or emergent, follow the emergency procedures in CL-CP-003, Section 6.4. | During or immediately following the visit. |

### 6.3 Visit Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | Document the visit note in the EHR within 24 hours of the visit per CL-CD-004. The visit note shall include, at minimum: (a) date and time of the visit; (b) the clinical purpose of the visit; (c) subjective data — patient and caregiver reports; (d) objective data — all assessment findings including vital signs, physical findings, and clinical observations; (e) assessment — the nurse's clinical assessment and professional judgment regarding the patient's current status and response to care; (f) plan — actions taken, interventions provided, education given, physician notifications made, referrals initiated, and the plan for the next visit; (g) goal progress documentation; (h) the next scheduled visit date and clinical purpose. | Within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Ensure that the documentation supports the medical necessity and skilled nature of the visit. CMS requires that each visit note demonstrate why the service required the skills of a licensed nurse and could not have been safely and effectively performed by the patient, caregiver, or unlicensed personnel. Documentation that reads as routine, non-skilled, or maintenance-level does not support billing under Medicare. | At the time of documentation. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | If the visit results in a change to the plan of care, a new physician order, or a referral to another discipline, document the action in the visit note and initiate the appropriate follow-up per CL-CP-002 and CL-CP-003. | Within 24 hours. |

### 6.4 LVN Practice Oversight

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Assign LVN caseloads with a designated supervising RN for each LVN. The supervising RN shall review the LVN's visit notes and clinical findings at minimum every 14 calendar days. | At caseload assignment; review every 14 calendar days. |
| 6.4.2 | Supervising RN | Review LVN visit notes for clinical accuracy, documentation adequacy, and scope-of-practice compliance. If any LVN visit note reflects activity outside the LVN scope, immediately notify the Director of Nursing. | Every 14 calendar days. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a direct supervisory visit (on-site observation of LVN patient care) at minimum annually for each LVN, or more frequently as indicated by competency evaluation or patient complaints. Document the supervisory visit findings per CL-SD-008. | At minimum annually; more frequently as indicated. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visit documentation does not support the skilled nature of the service | Director of Nursing identifies during chart review | Director of Nursing provides individual coaching and documentation remediation training. If the visit is not supported as skilled, assess billing impact with Revenue Cycle and Compliance Officer. | Coaching within 7 calendar days; billing review within 14 calendar days. |
| LVN performs services outside their scope | Supervising RN or Director of Nursing identifies | Director of Nursing immediately reassigns the patient to an RN. Provides scope-of-practice remediation training to the LVN. Documents corrective action per HR-ER-002. | RN reassignment within 24 hours; corrective action within 7 calendar days. |
| Skilled visit provided without a supporting physician order | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing retroactively obtains a physician order if clinically justified. Notifies Compliance Officer if the visit was billed without an order. | Physician order within 24 hours; Compliance Officer notification within 48 hours. |
| Nurse identifies a clinical situation requiring immediate intervention beyond the scope of current orders | Nurse contacts physician per CL-CP-003, Section 6.4 | Follow emergency order procedure. Document all actions. Notify Director of Nursing within 2 hours. | Immediate action; Director of Nursing notification within 2 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visit note for each skilled nursing visit | Complete visit note per Section 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours of visit; retained minimum 7 years |
| LVN supervisory review documentation | RN review of LVN visit notes | Supervising RN | EHR — supervisory notes | Every 14 calendar days; retained minimum 7 years |
| Direct supervisory visit documentation | On-site supervisory visit findings | Director of Nursing | EHR — supervisory notes | At minimum annually; retained minimum 7 years |
| Physician notifications | Documentation of all physician contacts triggered by visit findings | Assigned RN / LVN | EHR — communication notes | Within 24 hours of notification; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix A) | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All skilled nursing visits have a documented clinical purpose tied to the plan of care | Monthly chart audit of random sample | ≥95% of audited visit notes document a clinical purpose |
| Visit notes completed within 24 hours | EHR timestamp audit | ≥95% of visit notes locked within 24 hours of the visit |
| Visit notes support the skilled nature of the service | Monthly chart audit using the skilled documentation criteria tool | ≥95% of audited notes clearly demonstrate skilled service |
| All visits supported by a current active physician order | Monthly cross-reference of visit log and active orders | Zero visits without a supporting order on audited records |
| LVN supervisory reviews completed every 14 days | Supervisory review log audit | 100% of LVNs with documented RN review every 14 calendar days |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors under Tag G184 (42 CFR § 484.75) will verify that: skilled nursing services are provided by qualified nurses with current licensure; each visit has a documented clinical purpose; visit documentation supports the skilled nature of the service; and LVN practice is appropriately supervised. ADR (Additional Documentation Request) auditors from the MAC will focus on whether each visit note demonstrates medical necessity and skilled care — they are trained to identify "maintenance-level" documentation that does not support Medicare coverage.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visit notes that read as routine vital-sign checks without skilled assessment or intervention | Medicare coverage denial; ADR denial; False Claims Act risk | Train all nurses on skilled documentation standards; Director of Nursing audits monthly |
| LVN performing OASIS assessments or comprehensive assessments | Scope of practice violation; CMS deficiency; OASIS data invalidation | Restrict OASIS and comprehensive assessment access in EHR to RN credentials only |
| Visit conducted without reviewing current plan of care | Services may not align with physician orders | EHR workflow requires plan of care acknowledgment before visit note entry |
| Medication review not documented at each visit | Missed drug interactions; survey deficiency | Include medication review as mandatory visit note field |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs and LVNs shall receive competency-validated training on skilled nursing visit requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: visit documentation standards demonstrating medical necessity and skilled care; focused assessment techniques; scope of practice boundaries (especially LVN limitations); medication review protocol; and fall risk and safety assessment integration.
10.2 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the clinical standards, documentation requirements, competency expectations, and discharge criteria for physical therapy (PT) services provided by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Physical therapy is one of the qualifying skilled services under the Medicare home health benefit and may serve as the sole qualifying service for a patient's admission to home health. PT services in the home setting address functional mobility limitations, balance and gait deficits, pain management through therapeutic exercise, strength and endurance training, transfer training, assistive device training, and fall prevention interventions. This policy ensures that all PT services are delivered by qualified physical therapists and physical therapist assistants (PTAs) in accordance with the physician-approved plan of care, California Physical Therapy Practice Act, and the CMS Home Health Benefit Manual coverage requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All physical therapists (PTs) providing direct patient care
All physical therapist assistants (PTAs) providing services under PT supervision
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for clinical service oversight
Clinical Coordinators managing PT visit scheduling
Revenue Cycle staff verifying PT documentation supports billed claims
This policy governs all physical therapy evaluations, re-evaluations, treatment visits, and discharge visits.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Physical therapy services shall be provided only by physical therapists licensed by the Physical Therapy Board of California, or by physical therapist assistants working under the supervision of a licensed physical therapist in accordance with California Business and Professions Code § 2630 et seq. and 16 CCR § 1398 et seq.
4.2 All PT services shall be authorized by a physician order and reflected in the physician-approved plan of care per CL-CP-001 and CL-CP-003. No PT service shall be rendered without a current, active physician order specifying the discipline, frequency, and duration of services.
4.3 The physical therapist shall conduct an initial evaluation within 48 hours of receiving the patient referral (or within the timeframe specified in the physician order), which shall include at minimum: (a) a review of the patient's medical history, current diagnoses, and surgical history relevant to PT; (b) a standardized functional mobility assessment including gait, balance, transfer ability, strength, range of motion, and endurance; (c) a pain assessment per CL-SD-014; (d) a fall risk assessment per CL-SD-015; (e) an assessment of the home environment for PT-relevant safety hazards and accessibility; (f) identification of patient-specific, measurable, time-bound goals; (g) a recommended treatment plan including visit frequency, duration, and anticipated discharge criteria.
4.4 PTAs shall not independently conduct initial evaluations, establish goals, develop or modify the plan of care, or determine discharge. PTAs shall deliver treatment interventions under the direction and supervision of the licensed physical therapist, with documented supervisory review at minimum every 30 calendar days or every 6th visit, whichever occurs first, or per California Physical Therapy Practice Act requirements if more stringent.
4.5 All PT visit documentation shall be completed within 24 hours of the visit per CL-CD-004 and shall demonstrate the skilled nature of the service, patient response to treatment, and measurable progress toward goals.
4.6 The physical therapist shall conduct a re-evaluation at each recertification period, or more frequently when warranted by a significant change in the patient's condition, and shall update goals, the treatment plan, and the recommended visit frequency.
4.7 Discharge from PT services shall occur when: (a) the patient has met all PT-specific goals; (b) the patient has plateaued and further skilled PT services will not result in meaningful functional improvement; (c) the physician orders discontinuation of PT; (d) the patient declines further PT services. The discharging PT shall document a discharge summary including final functional status, goals achieved, and home exercise program provided.
4.8 When PT is the sole qualifying skilled service for a patient's home health admission, the physical therapist shall collaborate with the assigned RN to ensure that the patient's overall eligibility for home health is maintained, including homebound status documentation per CL-CA-005.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Physical Therapy Evaluation | The initial comprehensive assessment performed by a licensed physical therapist that establishes the patient's baseline functional status, identifies treatment goals, and develops the PT treatment plan. |
| Re-evaluation | A focused assessment conducted by the physical therapist at defined intervals to measure progress, adjust goals, and modify the treatment plan. |
| Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) | A licensed health care professional who provides physical therapy services under the direction and supervision of a licensed physical therapist. |
| Maintenance Therapy | Therapy services that do not require the skills of a therapist and are designed to maintain the patient's current functional level rather than achieve improvement. Maintenance therapy is generally not covered under Medicare. |
| Home Exercise Program (HEP) | An individualized set of exercises prescribed by the physical therapist for the patient and/or caregiver to perform independently between therapy visits and after discharge. |
| Functional Mobility | The ability to move safely and effectively within the home and community, including bed mobility, transfers, ambulation, stair negotiation, and wheelchair management. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial PT Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Physical Therapist | Upon receiving the patient assignment, review the plan of care, physician orders, OASIS assessment, and all available clinical documentation including referral information. | Before the initial evaluation visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Physical Therapist | Conduct the initial evaluation in the patient's home, completing all elements defined in Section 4.3. Use standardized assessment tools appropriate to the patient's diagnoses (e.g., Timed Up and Go, Berg Balance Scale, 30-Second Sit to Stand, 6-Minute Walk Test, or equivalent validated tools). | Within 48 hours of referral or per physician order. |
| 6.1.3 | Physical Therapist | Establish measurable, time-bound goals in collaboration with the patient and caregiver. Goals shall address functional deficits identified during the evaluation and shall specify: the target functional outcome, the measurement method, and the anticipated achievement timeframe. | During the evaluation visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Physical Therapist | Develop a treatment plan that includes: specific interventions (therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, transfer training, modality use, manual therapy, patient education); recommended visit frequency and duration; estimated total number of visits; and discharge criteria. | During or within 24 hours of the evaluation visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Physical Therapist | If the evaluation reveals that the patient does not require skilled PT services, or that the patient's condition is not amenable to PT intervention, document the finding and notify the physician and assigned RN within 24 hours. Do not initiate a treatment plan for a patient who does not meet skilled PT coverage criteria. | Within 24 hours of the evaluation. |
| 6.1.6 | Physical Therapist | Communicate evaluation findings, goals, and the treatment plan to the assigned RN and all other disciplines involved in the patient's care per CL-CP-005. | Within 48 hours of the evaluation. |

### 6.2 PT Treatment Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Physical Therapist / PTA | At each treatment visit, document: (a) the specific interventions performed; (b) the patient's response to each intervention including tolerance, exertion level, and pain response; (c) objective measurements (e.g., distance walked, repetitions completed, balance scores) that demonstrate progress toward goals; (d) patient and caregiver education provided; (e) any barriers to progress; (f) the plan for the next visit. | During the visit; documented within 24 hours. |
| 6.2.2 | Physical Therapist / PTA | Assess and document progress toward goals at each visit using measurable, objective criteria. Avoid subjective or vague progress notations such as "patient is doing better" — use quantifiable data. | During each visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Physical Therapist / PTA | If the patient is not progressing toward goals after a reasonable treatment period (typically 4–6 visits or 2 weeks of treatment), conduct a re-evaluation to determine whether continued PT is appropriate, whether goals should be modified, or whether a different treatment approach is warranted. Notify the physician and assigned RN of the re-evaluation findings. | Re-evaluation within 2 weeks of identified non-progression. |
| 6.2.4 | Physical Therapist / PTA | Integrate fall prevention education and home exercise program instruction into every treatment visit. Update the HEP as the patient progresses. Document the HEP provided and the patient's demonstrated understanding. | At each visit. |

### 6.3 PTA Supervision

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Physical Therapist | Develop the PTA's treatment instructions at the time of the initial evaluation. The instructions shall specify the interventions the PTA is authorized to perform, parameters for progression, and criteria that require immediate PT notification. | At the time of evaluation. |
| 6.3.2 | Physical Therapist | Conduct a supervisory review of the PTA's treatment notes and patient progress at minimum every 30 calendar days or every 6th PTA visit, whichever occurs first. Document the supervisory review. | Every 30 days or every 6th visit. |
| 6.3.3 | Physical Therapist | Conduct a direct supervisory visit (on-site joint visit with the PTA and patient) at minimum every 60 calendar days or as required by the California Physical Therapy Practice Act if more frequent. | Every 60 calendar days minimum. |
| 6.3.4 | PTA | Immediately notify the supervising PT if: (a) the patient's condition changes significantly; (b) the patient is not responding to treatment; (c) the patient reports new pain or symptoms; (d) any clinical situation arises that requires PT-level clinical judgment. | Immediately upon identification. |

### 6.4 PT Discharge

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Physical Therapist | Conduct a final evaluation at or near the time of discharge from PT services. Document: (a) the patient's final functional status using the same standardized assessment tools used at evaluation; (b) a comparison of initial and final functional status demonstrating the outcomes of treatment; (c) goals achieved and any goals not achieved with explanation; (d) the final home exercise program provided to the patient in writing; (e) recommendations for the patient, caregiver, and physician regarding ongoing functional maintenance; (f) recommendations for follow-up if indicated. | At the last PT visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Physical Therapist | Notify the physician, assigned RN, and all other disciplines of PT discharge, the patient's final status, and any clinical recommendations. | Within 24 hours of the final PT visit. |
| 6.4.3 | Physical Therapist | If PT is the sole qualifying skilled service and the patient has met PT discharge criteria, coordinate with the assigned RN and Director of Nursing to determine whether the patient should be discharged from home health entirely or whether other skilled needs have been identified. | Before the final PT visit. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PTA provides services without current PT supervisory review | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing halts PTA visits until a supervisory review is completed. PT must review all unsupervised visit notes within 48 hours. Document corrective action. | PTA visits suspended until supervisory review; review within 48 hours. |
| PT documentation does not support skilled nature of service | Director of Nursing identifies during chart review | Director of Nursing provides documentation coaching. Reassess billing compliance for affected visits with Revenue Cycle. | Coaching within 7 calendar days; billing review within 14 days. |
| Patient is not progressing but PT has not re-evaluated | Director of Nursing identifies during supervisory review | Director of Nursing directs the PT to conduct an immediate re-evaluation. If services are no longer skilled, discontinue and notify the physician. | Re-evaluation within 5 calendar days of identification. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial PT evaluation | Comprehensive evaluation note per Section 6.1 | Physical Therapist | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours of evaluation; retained minimum 7 years |
| Treatment visit notes | Visit note per Section 6.2.1 | PT / PTA | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours of each visit |
| PTA supervisory review | Documented supervisory review per Section 6.3.2 | Physical Therapist | EHR — supervisory notes | Every 30 days or every 6th visit |
| Re-evaluation notes | Re-evaluation documentation | Physical Therapist | EHR — clinical notes | At recertification or as clinically indicated |
| Discharge summary | Final evaluation per Section 6.4.1 | Physical Therapist | EHR — clinical notes | At the final PT visit |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix A) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial PT evaluation completed within 48 hours of referral | EHR audit of evaluation dates vs. referral dates | ≥95% compliance |
| PT visit notes document measurable progress toward goals | Monthly chart audit | ≥95% of audited notes include measurable progress data |
| PTA supervisory reviews completed timely | Supervisory review log audit | 100% of PTAs with documented review per schedule |
| PT discharge summary completed with final functional comparison | Discharge documentation audit | ≥95% of PT discharges with complete discharge summary |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will verify that PT evaluations are comprehensive, goals are measurable, visit notes demonstrate skilled intervention and progression, and PTA supervision is appropriately documented. MAC auditors will specifically examine whether PT documentation supports medical necessity and skilled care versus maintenance-level services — maintenance therapy documentation is the leading cause of PT claim denials.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goals stated as "improve balance" without measurable criteria | Survey deficiency; claim denial | Train PTs on SMART goal-writing; Director of Nursing audits monthly |
| Visit notes that describe only exercises without documenting patient response and progress | Claim denial for non-skilled documentation | Standardized visit note template requiring response and progress fields |
| PTA supervision lapses | State practice act violation; CMS deficiency | Automated EHR alerts for supervision due dates |
| Patient on PT for extended period without documented progress | Maintenance therapy billing risk; False Claims Act | Director of Nursing reviews all PT patients >60 days for progression evidence |
