# CL-SD-025 — Ordered Visit Frequency Compliance & Monitoring
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-025 |
| Policy Title | Ordered Visit Frequency Compliance & Monitoring |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires systematic monitoring of actual visit delivery against physician-ordered frequency and disciplines, with defined variance thresholds, documentation requirements, and corrective action triggers at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy exists because there is an inherent tension in home health between the ideal (every ordered visit delivered exactly as ordered) and the reality (patient refusals, missed visits, scheduling constraints, clinician availability, and patient clinical variability). If the tension is left unmanaged, the result is a systematic pattern of under-delivery of ordered services that simultaneously constitutes a patient safety failure (the patient receives less care than the physician determined was clinically necessary), a documentation compliance failure (the clinical record does not reflect a defensible explanation for the variance), a billing compliance failure (a full PDGM episode payment is collected for a certification period in which the ordered services were not delivered), and a False Claims Act risk. The PDGM Low Utilization Payment Adjustment (LUPA) exists precisely because CMS recognizes that low-visit episodes should be paid differently — when a patient is billed at the full PDGM rate for an episode but receives fewer visits than the physician ordered without clinical justification, the agency has potentially submitted a false claim. This policy ensures that visit delivery is monitored in real time, that variances between ordered and delivered frequency are identified immediately, that every variance is documented with a clinical explanation, that physician-ordered frequency is the floor — not the ceiling — of what the patient should receive, and that systemic under-delivery is detected and corrected before it becomes a financial and legal compliance failure.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) managing active patient caseloads
All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA) delivering patient visits
Clinical Coordinators managing visit scheduling and monitoring
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for visit delivery oversight
Revenue Cycle staff monitoring LUPA risk and episode billing
The QAPI Coordinator tracking visit utilization as a quality indicator
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The physician-ordered visit frequency, specified in the physician-approved plan of care, represents the minimum standard of service delivery for each patient during each certification period. Every ordered visit shall be delivered unless a specific, documented clinical or patient-initiated reason justifies a variance, and that reason shall be communicated to the physician when it creates a clinically significant deviation from the ordered plan.
4.2 The agency shall maintain a centralized Visit Frequency Monitoring System that tracks, for each active patient and each discipline, the ordered visit frequency, the delivered visit count, and the variance — updated daily and reviewed by Clinical Coordinators at minimum daily and by the Director of Nursing at minimum weekly.
4.3 Variance thresholds shall be defined as follows: (a) Tier 1 Variance — 1 visit below the ordered frequency within a 2-week period: Clinical Coordinator documents the reason and schedules a makeup visit. Director of Nursing notified if the reason is patient refusal or clinician unavailability. (b) Tier 2 Variance — 2 or more visits below the ordered frequency within a 2-week period, OR any variance that creates LUPA risk: Director of Nursing review required within 24 hours. Physician notification within 24 hours. Plan of care modification assessment per CL-CP-002. (c) Tier 3 Variance — Pattern of under-delivery across 2 or more consecutive 2-week periods, OR variance creating a LUPA for the episode: Director of Nursing and Administrator review. Physician notification and plan of care modification required. Compliance Officer notification if billing has been submitted. QAPI Performance Improvement Project initiated per QA-PI-001.
4.4 Every variance between ordered and delivered visit frequency shall be documented with a clinical explanation that addresses: (a) why the visit was not delivered; (b) the clinical impact of the variance on the patient; (c) what actions were taken to minimize the impact; (d) the physician notification status.
4.5 If the physician-ordered visit frequency is consistently undeliverable because the patient refuses the number of visits ordered, the appropriate clinical action is a plan of care modification to reflect the frequency the patient will actually accept — not continued ordering of visits that are never delivered. Ordering visits that the patient consistently refuses and never delivers, while collecting full episode payment, constitutes billing for services not rendered.
4.6 The agency shall never provide more visits than ordered without a physician order authorizing additional visits. Providing unordered visits is also a compliance violation — both under-delivery and over-delivery of ordered services without physician authorization are non-compliant.
4.7 Visit frequency compliance shall be a standing agenda item at each QAPI Committee meeting per QA-PG-003, with discipline-specific delivery rates, LUPA rates, and corrective actions reported.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Ordered Visit Frequency | The number of visits per week or per certification period for each discipline, as specified in the physician-approved plan of care. |
| Delivered Visit | A visit that occurred as documented in a completed, authenticated visit note in the patient's EHR. |
| Variance | The difference between the ordered and delivered visit count for a specific discipline within a defined time period. A negative variance means fewer visits were delivered than ordered; a positive variance means more visits were delivered than ordered. |
| LUPA (Low Utilization Payment Adjustment) | A reduced Medicare payment applied when a patient receives fewer than the minimum number of visits required for their PDGM payment category during a certification period. The LUPA threshold varies by PDGM payment group. |
| LUPA Risk | A state in which the current episode's delivered visit count is below or at risk of falling below the LUPA threshold, given the number of days remaining in the certification period. |
| Visit Frequency Monitoring System | The agency's centralized tracking tool (within the EHR or a dedicated scheduling and monitoring system) that tracks ordered vs. delivered visits in real time for every active patient in every discipline. |
| Makeup Visit | A rescheduled delivery of a visit that was missed, provided as soon as clinically appropriate to minimize the gap in care. |
| Plan of Care Modification | A physician-authorized change to the ordered visit frequency, discipline, or services to better reflect the patient's current clinical needs or realistic delivery expectations. |
| Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 Variance | The agency's three-tier variance classification system based on severity of deviation from the ordered frequency — defined in Section 4.3. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Visit Frequency Monitoring System — Daily Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Generate a daily Visit Frequency Compliance Report from the Visit Frequency Monitoring System for all active patients. The report shall display: (a) patient name and MR#; (b) each active discipline; (c) the ordered visit frequency for the current certification period; (d) the delivered visit count to date in the current certification period; (e) the remaining ordered visits in the current certification period; (f) the current variance (ordered minus delivered); (g) LUPA risk status — flagged if the episode is at risk of not meeting the LUPA threshold. | Daily; by 9:00 AM. |
| 6.1.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Review the daily report for any new variances and classify each using the tier system per Section 4.3. For Tier 1 variances, take immediate rescheduling action and document in the patient's record. For Tier 2 or Tier 3 variances, notify the Director of Nursing immediately. | Immediately upon generating the daily report. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Coordinator | Update the Visit Frequency Monitoring System as visits are completed, missed, or rescheduled throughout each day. The system shall reflect the current delivery status in real time. | Continuously throughout each business day. |

### 6.2 Tier 1 Variance Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Upon identifying a Tier 1 variance (1 visit below ordered frequency within a 2-week period): (a) determine the reason for the missed visit; (b) schedule a makeup visit at the earliest clinically appropriate opportunity per CL-SD-024 rescheduling timelines; (c) document the reason and the rescheduling action in the patient's Missed Visit Record per CL-SD-024. | Same day as identification. |
| 6.2.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Notify the Director of Nursing of Tier 1 variances resulting from patient refusal or clinician unavailability, as these may indicate systemic issues requiring clinical or operational intervention. | Within 4 hours of identification. |
| 6.2.3 | Clinical Coordinator | Monitor the Tier 1 patient's delivery status daily until the makeup visit is confirmed as delivered. If the makeup visit is also missed, reclassify as a Tier 2 variance. | Daily. |

### 6.3 Tier 2 Variance Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Upon notification of a Tier 2 variance, conduct a clinical review within 24 hours: (a) review the patient's clinical record, missed visit documentation, and delivery history; (b) assess the clinical impact of the under-delivery — is the patient experiencing any clinical deterioration attributable to the missed visits? (c) assess the reason for the variance — patient refusal, scheduling failure, clinician availability, or other; (d) assess whether the plan of care visit frequency is realistic and achievable for this patient; (e) assess the LUPA risk for the episode. | Within 24 hours of identification. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Notify the attending physician within 24 hours of a Tier 2 variance: (a) report the specific variance (ordered vs. delivered); (b) report the reason for the variance; (c) report the patient's current clinical status; (d) assess with the physician whether the ordered frequency should be maintained and makeup visits pursued, or whether the plan of care should be modified to reflect a frequency the patient will accept; (e) obtain physician orders for any plan modification per CL-CP-002 and CL-CP-003. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Document the clinical review findings and actions in the patient's clinical record and in the supervisory review log. | Within 24 hours of the review. |
| 6.3.4 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Implement a clinical monitoring plan for the patient, including: (a) daily review of visit delivery; (b) proactive scheduling to ensure remaining ordered visits are delivered before the certification period ends; (c) LUPA risk tracking with Revenue Cycle. | Immediately following the Tier 2 review. |

### 6.4 Tier 3 Variance Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Upon identification of a Tier 3 variance (pattern of under-delivery across 2+ consecutive 2-week periods or LUPA confirmed for the episode), notify the Administrator within 24 hours. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Conduct a comprehensive case and systemic review: (a) identify all clinical reasons for the sustained under-delivery; (b) assess whether the plan of care requires modification to a realistic and deliverable visit frequency; (c) assess whether the patient should be considered for non-compliance discharge per CL-CP-006 Section 6.5; (d) assess whether the variance reflects a systemic scheduling or staffing issue requiring operational correction; (e) notify the Compliance Officer if billing has been submitted for a certification period with a LUPA, to assess whether the billing was accurate or constitutes a compliance concern. | Within 5 business days of identification. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Initiate a Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001 if the Tier 3 variance is identified as part of a systemic pattern affecting multiple patients. Report to the QAPI Committee at the next scheduled meeting. | PIP initiation within 14 calendar days; QAPI report at the next scheduled meeting. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | Assess the billing compliance implications of any confirmed LUPA episode, including whether the claim was submitted at the correct payment level and whether any corrective action (repayment) is warranted per FN-BC-004. | Assessment within 14 calendar days of notification. |

### 6.5 Plan of Care Frequency Modification Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | When a patient's consistent refusal or clinical status makes the ordered visit frequency unrealistic: (a) assess whether the patient has the capacity and right to refuse the number of ordered visits; (b) discuss with the patient and caregiver whether there is a frequency the patient would accept and find beneficial; (c) contact the physician with a clinical summary and a recommendation for plan of care modification to a deliverable frequency. | Within 7 calendar days of identifying an unrealistic ordered frequency. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Obtain a physician order for the modified visit frequency per CL-CP-003. Update the plan of care per CL-CP-002. | Within 24 hours of physician agreement to modify. |
| 6.5.3 | Revenue Cycle | Update the billing record to reflect the modified plan of care frequency. Assess whether the modification affects PDGM payment classification per FN-CM-001. | Within 5 business days of plan modification. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visit Frequency Monitoring System shows outdated or inaccurate data | Clinical Coordinator notifies Director of Nursing | Audit the system data against the EHR visit delivery records. Correct any data entry errors. Identify the source of the discrepancy and implement a process correction. | Correction within 24 hours; process correction within 5 business days. |
| Tier 2 variance identified but physician notification not completed within 24 hours | Director of Nursing identified during weekly review | Director of Nursing completes the notification immediately and provides corrective guidance to the responsible clinician. | Notification completed within 24 hours of identification. |
| Revenue Cycle submits a full episode claim for an episode with a LUPA | Compliance Officer and Revenue Cycle Director | Assess whether the claim was submitted at the correct LUPA payment level. If the claim was submitted at the wrong rate, assess for overpayment per FN-BC-004 and correct. | Assessment within 5 business days; correction within the CMS 60-day repayment timeline if overpayment is confirmed. |
| A discipline is consistently under-delivering ordered visits across multiple patients | Director of Nursing identifies pattern in QAPI review | QAPI PIP initiated. Operational analysis of scheduling, staffing, and clinical causes. Administrator notified. | PIP within 14 calendar days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Daily Visit Frequency Compliance Report generated every business day | Report generation log | 100% of business days |
| All variances documented with clinical explanation same day | EHR variance documentation audit | ≥95% |
| Tier 2 variances result in physician notification within 24 hours | Communication note audit | ≥95% |
| LUPA rate per discipline | QAPI dashboard | Agency target: at or below the national average per CMS Home Health Compare data |
| Episodes billed at correct payment level (LUPA vs. full) | Revenue Cycle audit | 100% — zero episodes billed at wrong payment level |
| QAPI visit utilization report presented quarterly | QAPI Committee meeting minutes | 100% — quarterly presentation |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will compare ordered visit frequencies in the plan of care against delivered visit counts in the clinical record. Surveyors will flag episodes where fewer visits were delivered than ordered without documented clinical justification. ADR auditors and MAC reviewers will specifically target episodes where the delivered visit count is below the LUPA threshold for the patient's payment group — these are treated as potential billing errors or False Claims Act concerns. OIG audits of home health agencies routinely identify patterns of claiming full PDGM payment for episodes in which ordered visits were systematically not delivered.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No centralized monitoring system — visit delivery tracked informally | Variances undetected until billing; LUPA missed | Mandatory daily Visit Frequency Compliance Report; Director of Nursing weekly review |
| Variances documented as "patient refused" without physician notification | Unresolved plan of care misalignment; billing risk | Physician notification protocol triggers at Tier 2; Director of Nursing monitors compliance |
| Plan of care continues to order visits the patient consistently refuses | Billing for services not rendered; False Claims Act risk | Plan of care modification process initiated at 3 consecutive refusals in the same discipline |
| LUPA episodes billed at full PDGM rate | Overpayment; billing compliance failure | Revenue Cycle pre-bill LUPA check; Compliance Officer notification for confirmed LUPA episodes |
| Visit frequency monitoring data not updated in real time | Variances identified too late for makeup visit scheduling | EHR workflow requiring missed visit or visit completion entry same day |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All Clinical Coordinators shall receive training on the Visit Frequency Monitoring System at hire and whenever the system is updated, covering: daily report generation; variance classification using the three-tier system; rescheduling timelines; LUPA risk identification; and escalation protocol.
10.2 All RNs and clinical discipline leads shall receive training on ordered visit frequency compliance within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, covering: the clinical and billing implications of under-delivery; the physician notification requirement for Tier 2 variances; the plan of care modification process; and the documentation requirements for variances.
10.3 Revenue Cycle staff shall receive training on LUPA threshold identification and billing level compliance at hire and annually.
10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001. 11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions shall be archived as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE." 11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001. 11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with Governing Body notification at the next regular meeting.

## 2. Purpose
This policy mandates completion of a comprehensive patient assessment — including all required OASIS data elements at applicable time points — for every patient admitted to home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The comprehensive assessment is the clinical foundation upon which every other clinical activity in the home health episode depends. It is simultaneously: the clinical document that establishes the patient's eligibility for the Medicare home health benefit (homebound status, need for skilled services); the data source for all OASIS items that drive PDGM payment classification; the basis for the individualized plan of care; the baseline against which all clinical progress is measured; and the primary document that CMS surveyors and ADR auditors examine when evaluating whether the patient legitimately required — and received — skilled home health services. An inadequate, incomplete, or inaccurate comprehensive assessment cascades failure across the entire episode: an inaccurate OASIS produces the wrong PDGM payment group; an incomplete clinical picture produces a plan of care that does not reflect the patient's actual needs; missing homebound status documentation creates billing vulnerability; and inadequate assessment documentation fails to justify the skilled services billed. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.55 — Condition of Participation: Comprehensive Assessment of Patients — which requires that a registered nurse complete a comprehensive assessment for each patient admitted to home health care that accurately reflects the patient's current health status and includes information that may be used to inform the individualized plan of care.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) authorized to conduct comprehensive assessments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. — only RNs may conduct comprehensive assessments; LVNs, therapists, and other disciplines may not independently conduct the comprehensive assessment or complete OASIS assessments
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for assessment quality oversight
All clinical disciplines whose initial discipline-specific evaluations contribute to but do not substitute for the comprehensive assessment
Medical Records and OASIS submission staff
Revenue Cycle staff relying on OASIS data for payment classification
This policy governs comprehensive assessments at all applicable time points: Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), Recertification (RECERT), Follow-Up (FU), Discharge (DC), and Transfer (TRN). Discipline-specific assessments (PT evaluation, OT evaluation, SLP evaluation, MSW psychosocial assessment) are supplemental to the comprehensive assessment and are governed by the respective discipline-specific policies (CL-SD-002 through CL-SD-005). OASIS-specific data collection requirements, accuracy standards, and submission requirements are governed by CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019, which cross-reference this policy as the clinical basis for OASIS data.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 A comprehensive patient assessment shall be completed by a qualified registered nurse at the Start of Care visit and at all subsequent applicable OASIS time points. The comprehensive assessment shall begin at the time of the first billable visit — the SOC visit — and shall be completed at the patient's home.
4.2 Only a registered nurse currently licensed by the California Board of Registered Nursing and meeting the assessment competency requirements of this policy may complete a comprehensive assessment for home health patients. Licensed vocational nurses, therapists, and other clinical disciplines shall not complete comprehensive assessments or OASIS assessments independently, regardless of the clinical services they provide.
4.3 The comprehensive assessment shall be completed within 5 calendar days following the start of the care episode — meaning the SOC assessment shall be completed at or within 5 calendar days of the first billable visit per 42 CFR § 484.55(a)(1). The 5-day window applies to the completion and locking of the assessment in the EHR, not merely to the collection of data during the visit.
4.4 The comprehensive assessment shall include all domains specified in Section 6.2 and shall incorporate all applicable OASIS data elements as defined in the current CMS OASIS-E2 guidance. The assessment shall be individualized and patient-specific — template-driven assessments that do not reflect the patient's actual clinical presentation at the time of the assessment are not compliant with 42 CFR § 484.55.
4.5 The comprehensive assessment shall include a determination of homebound status per CL-CA-005, clearly documented with patient-specific functional limitations that support the homebound determination.
4.6 The comprehensive assessment shall include a determination of the patient's need for skilled services — specifically identifying which skilled disciplines are required and why they are medically necessary for the treatment of this patient's conditions.
4.7 The comprehensive assessment findings shall form the direct basis of the plan of care. Every element of the plan of care — diagnoses, services, frequency, goals, medications, treatments, and safety measures — shall be traceable to findings documented in the comprehensive assessment.
4.8 The assigned RN shall incorporate or coordinate with the findings of all discipline-specific evaluations (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) conducted at or near the SOC into the unified plan of care, ensuring that the plan is a truly interdisciplinary document rather than a series of parallel, disconnected discipline plans.
4.9 All OASIS items shall be completed accurately, using the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for all response selection decisions. The RN completing the assessment is solely responsible for the accuracy of the OASIS coding — OASIS responses shall not be altered by non-clinical staff, revenue cycle personnel, or billing coders.
4.10 A comprehensive re-assessment shall be conducted at each OASIS time point (ROC, RECERT, FU as applicable, TRN, DC). The re-assessment shall reflect the patient's current status at the time of the re-assessment — not the status at the prior assessment or the status at an earlier time point. Each OASIS assessment is a contemporaneous point-in-time assessment of the patient's current condition per CL-OA-009.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Comprehensive Assessment | The full, multidimensional clinical assessment of a home health patient required by 42 CFR § 484.55, incorporating all required OASIS data elements and all clinical domains specified in this policy. Only a registered nurse may complete this assessment. |
| OASIS (Outcome and Assessment Information Set) | The standardized data collection instrument mandated by CMS for Medicare-certified home health agencies, used to measure patient outcomes and clinical characteristics and to inform PDGM payment classification. The current version is OASIS-E2. |
| OASIS Assessment Time Points | The specific clinical events that trigger a required OASIS assessment: Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), Recertification (RECERT), Follow-Up (FU), Transfer to Inpatient Facility (TRN), and Discharge from Agency (DC). |
| Start of Care (SOC) | The first billable visit to a patient for a new home health episode. The comprehensive assessment shall be initiated at this visit. |
| Resumption of Care (ROC) | The first billable visit following a patient's return to home health services after an inpatient facility stay of ≥24 hours. A new comprehensive assessment is required. |
| Recertification (RECERT) | The comprehensive assessment conducted between Day 56 and Day 60 of each certification period to evaluate continued eligibility and update the plan of care. |
| Follow-Up (FU) | An OASIS assessment conducted between the SOC and RECERT time points, triggered by a significant change in the patient's condition (SCIC assessment), as defined by CMS criteria. |
| Transfer (TRN) | An OASIS assessment completed at the time of transfer to an inpatient facility, documenting the patient's status at the point of transfer. |
| Discharge (DC) | An OASIS assessment completed at the time of discharge from the agency (other than transfer to an inpatient facility), documenting the patient's final status. |
| Assessment Accuracy | The degree to which each OASIS item response correctly reflects the patient's actual functional status, symptoms, and clinical characteristics at the time of the assessment, as determined by direct observation, clinical evaluation, patient and caregiver report, and review of available documentation. |
| Homebound Status | The condition in which the patient has a normal inability to leave home due to an illness or injury, and leaving home requires a considerable and taxing effort — as defined in 42 CFR § 409.42(a). |
| Skilled Services Need | The clinical requirement for services that require the training, skills, and judgment of a licensed nurse, physical therapist, occupational therapist, or speech-language pathologist — the qualifying condition for Medicare home health eligibility. |
| Point-in-Time Assessment | The assessment principle that each OASIS assessment reflects the patient's status at the time of the specific assessment encounter — not a historical average or a projection. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Pre-Assessment Preparation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Verify that the assigned RN has completed the agency's Comprehensive Assessment Competency Program (Appendix A) and is listed on the OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster before independently conducting assessments. A newly hired RN who has not completed the competency program shall conduct their first SOC assessment under direct supervision of the Director of Nursing or a preceptor RN. | Before the first independent assessment assignment. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Before the SOC visit, review all available referral documentation: hospital discharge summary (including hospital course, surgical reports, discharge diagnoses, discharge medications, follow-up instructions); physician referral and orders; insurance authorization; any prior home health records if available; specialty consultation notes; and most recent laboratory or diagnostic results. Prepare for the assessment by identifying the primary clinical focus areas based on the referral information. | Before the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Verify that the following assessment tools and supplies are available and ready for the SOC visit: stethoscope, blood pressure cuff, thermometer, pulse oximeter, measuring tape (for wound assessment, OASIS functional measurements), monofilament (for diabetic neuropathy assessment), appropriate language interpretation resources (per OP-PA-003 if the patient's primary language is not English), standardized assessment tools required for OASIS completion (PHQ-2/PHQ-9, BIMS, MAHC-10 if applicable). | Before the SOC visit. |

### 6.2 Comprehensive Assessment — Required Domains and Content

| Domain | Required Assessment Elements |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Sociodemographic | Living situation; household members; primary language; education level; health literacy; cultural background relevant to care; social support system. |
| 2. Medical History | Primary diagnosis (chief reason for home health); all secondary diagnoses relevant to the episode; surgical history; relevant hospitalization history (past 12 months); current physician(s) and specialists; allergies (drug, food, environmental); advance directive status per CL-PR-002 and CL-SD-023; immunization status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, other). |
| 3. Vital Signs and Physical Examination | Blood pressure; heart rate (rate, rhythm, regularity); respiratory rate; temperature; oxygen saturation (room air and on supplemental oxygen if applicable); weight; height (BMI calculated); complete head-to-toe physical examination appropriate to the patient's diagnoses, with organ-system specificity. |
| 4. Medication Review | Complete medication list per CL-SD-013 (three-source medication reconciliation at SOC/ROC); medication management capability assessment; adherence assessment; high-alert medication identification per RM-PS-005; OASIS medication management items. |
| 5. Functional Status | ADL performance (bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, eating, functional mobility); IADL performance (meal preparation, medication management, telephone use, transportation, managing finances, light housekeeping, laundry); bed mobility and transfer ability; ambulation; upper extremity function; assistive device use; prosthetic or orthotic use. All OASIS functional items (M-series). |
| 6. Cognitive Status | Orientation (person, place, time, situation); short-term and long-term memory; attention; executive function; BIMS administration per CL-SD-022; decision-making capacity assessment; OASIS cognitive function items. |
| 7. Behavioral Health | PHQ-2 (and PHQ-9 if positive) per CL-SD-022; anxiety assessment; behavioral symptoms (agitation, combativeness, elopement risk); substance use screening per clinical indication; OASIS behavioral health items. |
| 8. Wound and Skin Status | Complete skin assessment (all body surfaces); wound assessment per CL-SD-011 for all identified wounds (location, etiology, stage, measurements, wound bed, drainage, periwound skin, signs of infection); OASIS wound items (M1311–M1350); pressure injury risk assessment. |
| 9. Pain Assessment | Comprehensive pain assessment per CL-SD-014 (location, intensity, quality, pattern, impact on function, management); OASIS pain items. |
| 10. Respiratory Status | Respiratory assessment per CL-SD-020 (if respiratory diagnosis present); oxygen therapy status; dyspnea assessment; OASIS respiratory items. |
| 11. Cardiac and Circulatory Status | Cardiac assessment per CL-SD-019 (if cardiac diagnosis present); edema; peripheral vascular assessment; orthostatic blood pressure. |
| 12. Endocrine/Metabolic | Diabetic assessment per CL-SD-018 (if diabetic diagnosis present); blood glucose; nutritional status. |
| 13. Nutrition | Nutritional intake assessment; weight change in the past 3 months; swallowing function; feeding method (oral, tube); body weight trend; nutrition risk indicators; OASIS nutritional items. |
| 14. Bowel and Bladder Function | Continence status (bowel and bladder); incontinence type and frequency; urinary catheter status; ostomy status; OASIS incontinence items. |
| 15. Neuromusculoskeletal | Strength assessment (by major muscle group); range of motion (major joints); coordination; balance (clinical observation; standardized tool such as Timed Up and Go if applicable); sensation (including monofilament for diabetic patients). |
| 16. Fall Risk | Comprehensive fall risk assessment per CL-SD-015 (validated tool, FRID review, environmental hazard assessment, prior fall history). |
| 17. Homebound Status | Documented clinical basis for homebound determination per CL-CA-005 — patient-specific functional limitations and the clinical reason they make leaving home require considerable and taxing effort. |
| 18. Skilled Services Need | Clinical justification for each skilled discipline ordered — why does this patient require the skills of a licensed nurse, PT, OT, or SLP? Not merely that the services are ordered, but why they are medically necessary. |
| 19. Home Environment | Environmental safety assessment per RM-PS-001 — walkways, lighting, stairs, grab bars, rugs, oxygen safety, medication storage, emergency access. |
| 20. Caregiver Status | Caregiver availability, willingness, and capability; caregiver training needs; caregiver stress assessment per CL-SD-021 (if pediatric) and CL-SD-023 (if palliative); OASIS caregiver items. |
| 21. Patient Goals | Patient's and caregiver's priorities and goals for the home health episode — what does the patient want to achieve? What is most important to them? These shall be incorporated directly into the plan of care goals. |
| 22. Discharge Potential | Estimated episode length; anticipated discharge date; discharge criteria; potential discharge setting and resource needs; barriers to discharge. |

### 6.3 OASIS Data Collection and Completion

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | Collect all OASIS data elements during the comprehensive assessment visit using direct observation, physical examination, patient and caregiver report, and review of all available documentation. Adhere to the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for all response selection decisions. For every OASIS item, select the response that most accurately describes the patient's status at the time of the assessment — not the best possible performance, not the worst-case performance, but the actual current status. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Administer all required standardized assessment tools — PHQ-2/PHQ-9 per CL-SD-022, BIMS per CL-SD-022, MAHC-10 (if applicable), and any other CMS-mandated standardized tool for the applicable OASIS version — exactly as specified in the validated administration protocols. Do not abbreviate or modify the administration of standardized tools. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Document the clinical basis for every OASIS item response in the narrative visit note — the OASIS response and the narrative documentation must be consistent per CL-OA-007. The narrative shall describe the specific observation, test result, or patient report that supports the OASIS response. Do not complete OASIS items that are not supported by documented clinical evidence. | During and immediately following the SOC visit. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | Complete and lock the comprehensive assessment in the EHR within 5 calendar days of the SOC visit, including all OASIS items. Prior to locking, conduct a self-review using the pre-submission quality review checklist per CL-OA-019 to identify internal inconsistencies, missing items, and items that conflict with narrative documentation. | Within 5 calendar days of the SOC visit. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a supervisory OASIS quality review of a random sample of ≥5% of all SOC assessments per month. The review shall verify OASIS accuracy per CL-OA-002, narrative-OASIS consistency per CL-OA-007, homebound status documentation adequacy, and skilled service justification adequacy. | Monthly. |

### 6.4 Assessment-to-Plan of Care Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | Following completion of the comprehensive assessment, develop the plan of care per CL-CP-001, ensuring direct traceability from every plan of care element to a specific finding in the comprehensive assessment. Every diagnosis in the plan of care shall correspond to a documented clinical finding. Every service and discipline ordered shall be justified by an assessed need. Every goal shall address a specific functional deficit or clinical problem identified in the assessment. | Within 24 hours of the SOC assessment. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | Obtain discipline-specific evaluations from PT, OT, SLP, and MSW within the timeframes specified in the respective discipline policies, and integrate their findings into the unified plan of care. | Per the respective discipline evaluation timelines; integration within 48 hours of each discipline evaluation. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Review the plan of care with the patient and caregiver at or before the second visit, incorporating their goals and preferences as documented in the assessment. | At or before the second visit. |

### 6.5 Recertification and Subsequent Assessments

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | Conduct each subsequent OASIS assessment (ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, DC) as a complete, contemporaneous assessment of the patient's current status — not an update of the prior assessment. Each assessment independently reflects what the patient's status is at the moment of that specific assessment. | At each applicable OASIS time point. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | At RECERT, evaluate all assessment domains per Section 6.2, identifying changes from the SOC baseline. Document the patient's progress, any new or worsened conditions, and the clinical basis for continued eligibility (continued homebound status, continued need for skilled services). | Between Day 56 and Day 60 of each certification period. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | At DISCHARGE, document the patient's final status in all applicable OASIS domains, enabling CMS to calculate outcome measures comparing the patient's status at SOC to their status at discharge — the basis for all publicly reported home health quality measures. | At the final visit or within 2 calendar days of discharge. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assigned RN cannot complete the comprehensive assessment within 5 calendar days of SOC due to patient illness, hospitalization, or unavailability | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses clinical appropriateness of delaying the assessment. If the patient is hospitalized, initiate transfer OASIS. If the patient is unavailable but returning, reschedule for the earliest available date and document the reason for the delay. | Assessment completed as soon as clinically possible; delay documented with clinical rationale. |
| Comprehensive assessment reveals the patient does not meet Medicare home health eligibility criteria (not homebound, no skilled need) | Assigned RN and Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing reviews the clinical findings and consults with the Compliance Officer. If the patient does not meet eligibility criteria, the agency shall not bill the visit as a Medicare-covered visit. Discuss findings with the physician and develop a non-Medicare service plan or discharge the patient appropriately. | Assessment findings reviewed within 24 hours; physician consultation within 48 hours. |
| OASIS assessment data is locked and submitted but contains an error | Director of Nursing and OASIS submission coordinator | Correct the OASIS assessment per CL-OA-002 and resubmit. Document the correction and the reason for it per CO-DC-003. | Correction within the timeframe specified in CL-OA-002. |
| Assessment conducted by a clinician who is not an authorized OASIS assessor | Director of Nursing identifies during review | OASIS invalidation assessment — the unauthorized assessment must be voided and re-completed by a qualified RN. Director of Nursing reviews all visits conducted under the unauthorized assessment for billing implications. Compliance Officer notified. | Re-assessment within 5 business days; compliance review within 14 calendar days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Comprehensive assessments completed within 5 calendar days of SOC | OASIS lock date audit vs. SOC date | ≥98% completed within 5 calendar days |
| All OASIS assessments conducted by authorized RN assessors | Authorized Assessor Roster cross-reference | 100% — zero assessments by unauthorized assessors |
| OASIS narrative-to-item consistency | Director of Nursing monthly OASIS quality review | ≥95% of audited assessments with consistent narrative and OASIS responses |
| Homebound status documented with patient-specific functional limitations | Chart audit | ≥95% of SOC assessments with adequate homebound documentation |
| Skilled service need documented for each ordered discipline | Chart audit | ≥95% of SOC assessments with documented skilled need justification |
| Director of Nursing monthly OASIS quality review completed | Review log audit | 100% — monthly review documented |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G140 (42 CFR § 484.55):
1. Evidence that a registered nurse completed the comprehensive assessment. Surveyors will verify that the OASIS assessment was completed by an RN. Assessment by LVNs, therapists, or non-clinical staff is a Condition-level deficiency.
2. Evidence that the assessment was completed within 5 calendar days. Surveyors will compare the OASIS lock date to the SOC date. Late assessments are a documentation compliance deficiency.
3. Evidence that the assessment is comprehensive and individualized. Surveyors will review OASIS assessments for template-driven responses that do not reflect the specific patient's status. Cookie-cutter assessments are cited as failures to meet the comprehensive assessment standard.
4. Evidence that OASIS items are accurate. OASIS validation auditors will select specific items — particularly functional status items (GG section), wound items (M1311–M1350), behavioral health items (M1700–M1750), and medication management items — and compare the coded response to the narrative assessment documentation. Inconsistencies are cited as OASIS inaccuracy deficiencies.
5. Evidence that the assessment led to an individualized plan of care. Surveyors will compare the plan of care goals and services to the assessment findings. A plan of care that does not reflect the assessment is evidence that the assessment was not the basis for the plan.
6. Evidence of homebound status. Surveyors will specifically review the homebound documentation in the assessment for patient-specific, clinical language describing why the patient cannot leave home without considerable effort. Generic homebound language ("patient has difficulty ambulating") without patient-specific limitations is frequently cited.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment contains template-driven language not individualized to the patient | Survey deficiency; assessment not considered comprehensive | Director of Nursing monthly OASIS review with feedback on individualization; require specific clinical findings in all narrative fields |
| OASIS locked after the 5-calendar-day window | Documentation compliance deficiency; OASIS timing violation | EHR alert on Day 4 post-SOC for incomplete OASIS; Director of Nursing review of all late assessments |
| Homebound status documented generically | Billing vulnerability; survey citation | Train all RNs on patient-specific homebound documentation; Director of Nursing reviews all homebound documentation at monthly chart audit |
| OASIS completed by an LVN or therapist | Condition-level CMS deficiency | EHR system access control — OASIS module access restricted to RN credentials only; Authorized Assessor Roster enforced |
| OASIS items inconsistent with narrative documentation | OASIS accuracy deficiency; payment integrity risk | Pre-submission quality review per CL-OA-019 mandatory before every OASIS lock |
| Assessment findings not reflected in the plan of care | Fragmented care; survey citation | CL-CP-001 requires direct traceability from assessment to plan; Director of Nursing reviews POC development at monthly supervisory review |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs shall complete the Comprehensive Assessment Competency Program (Appendix A) before independently conducting comprehensive assessments. The program shall include: (a) didactic content covering all assessment domains in Section 6.2; (b) OASIS item-specific training per the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual; (c) standardized tool administration (PHQ-2/PHQ-9, BIMS, MAHC-10 as applicable) with validated competency demonstration; (d) homebound status documentation standards; (e) skilled service need documentation standards; (f) pre-submission quality review process; (g) assessment-to-plan of care integration; (h) documentation standards demonstrating individualized, patient-specific assessment content.
10.2 The Director of Nursing or a designated preceptor RN shall directly supervise and evaluate the first independent SOC assessment of every newly hired or newly authorized RN before adding the RN to the Authorized Assessor Roster.
10.3 Annual refresher competency for comprehensive assessment and OASIS accuracy shall be completed by all authorized RN assessors, incorporating any changes to the OASIS data set or CMS guidance issued since the prior annual training.
10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
10.5 The Director of Nursing shall maintain the Comprehensive Assessment Competency Program training records and the Authorized Assessor Roster for all RNs and shall report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of any training deadline.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001. 11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions shall be archived as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE." 11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001. 11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with Governing Body notification at the next regular meeting.

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standards for accurate, timely, and complete OASIS data collection in compliance with CMS requirements at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Outcome and Assessment Information Set (OASIS) is not merely a documentation instrument — it is the financial, clinical, and regulatory backbone of the Medicare home health benefit. Every OASIS data element directly affects one or more of the following: the patient's PDGM payment group assignment (which determines how much Medicare pays the agency for the episode); the agency's publicly reported quality measures on Home Health Compare (which affect the agency's star ratings, referral relationships, and competitive standing); CMS survey compliance (inaccurate OASIS data is a direct deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.55); and the clinical validity of the agency's patient population data (which underpins every quality improvement decision the QAPI program makes).
OASIS accuracy failures are among the most consequential and most commonly cited deficiencies in home health. They occur along a spectrum: individual item errors driven by misunderstanding of CMS guidance; systematic coding patterns driven by financial pressure (upcoding to maximize payment); systematic undercoding driven by unfamiliarity with the instrument; and documentation inconsistencies where OASIS responses are not supported by the clinical narrative. All of these failure modes have regulatory, financial, and legal consequences. The False Claims Act imposes liability not only for fraudulent claims but for claims submitted with reckless disregard for their accuracy — a pattern of OASIS inaccuracy without a robust accuracy program may meet that standard.
This policy establishes the complete framework for OASIS data collection accuracy at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., incorporating: the clinical decision rules that govern response selection; the documentation standards that must support every response; the quality review process that validates accuracy before submission; the training and authorization program that ensures only competent assessors collect OASIS data; and the audit and correction process that identifies and resolves errors after submission. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.55(b) — which requires that the comprehensive assessment accurately reflect the patient's current health status — and CMS Conditions of Participation requirements for OASIS data integrity under 42 CFR § 484.20.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) authorized to conduct comprehensive assessments and collect OASIS data
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for OASIS quality oversight
The OASIS Quality Reviewer (a designated RN with advanced OASIS training who conducts pre-submission and post-submission OASIS audits)
OASIS submission staff responsible for transmitting data to the CMS OASIS repository
The QAPI Coordinator who uses OASIS-derived quality measures for performance improvement
Revenue Cycle staff whose payment calculations depend on accurate OASIS data
This policy does not apply to non-RN clinical staff (LVNs, therapists, HHAs), who do not collect OASIS data. It governs all OASIS time points: SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU (SCIC), TRN, and DC.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All OASIS data elements shall be collected by a registered nurse who has completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program per CL-CA-001 and is listed on the current OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster. No OASIS data element shall be collected, modified, or finalized by any non-RN clinical staff member, administrative staff, revenue cycle personnel, or billing coder, regardless of the purpose of the modification.
4.2 Every OASIS response shall be selected using the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual as the definitive authority for all coding decisions. When agency-developed coding guidance conflicts with CMS guidance, CMS guidance governs. Agency-created coding rules, internal coding conventions, or OASIS "cheat sheets" that deviate from or contradict CMS guidance are prohibited.
4.3 Every OASIS response shall be supported by documented clinical evidence in the patient's clinical record. The evidentiary hierarchy for OASIS coding shall follow CL-OA-006 (Documentation Hierarchy and Evidence Source Prioritization). An OASIS response that is not supported by documented clinical evidence is an unsupported response and constitutes a data integrity failure, regardless of whether the response happens to be clinically plausible.
4.4 OASIS data shall reflect the patient's actual clinical status at the time of the specific assessment encounter — not the patient's best possible performance, not the patient's worst-case scenario, not an average of performances across recent visits, and not an extrapolation from prior assessments. Every OASIS assessment is a contemporaneous point-in-time assessment per CL-OA-009.
4.5 The agency shall implement a multi-level OASIS quality review process: (a) a self-review by the assessing RN using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019 before locking the assessment; (b) a designated OASIS Quality Reviewer review of all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking; (c) a monthly random sample OASIS audit by the Director of Nursing covering ≥5% of all submitted assessments per CL-OA-002; (d) quarterly OASIS accuracy trending analysis presented to the QAPI Committee.
4.6 The agency shall maintain an OASIS data accuracy rate — defined as the percentage of audited OASIS items where the agency's response matches the correct response as determined by the OASIS Quality Reviewer — of ≥95% as the minimum acceptable standard. An accuracy rate below 95% on any audited item category shall trigger a Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001.
4.7 Any OASIS response that is identified as inaccurate, whether before or after submission, shall be corrected per the procedures established in CL-CA-003 (OASIS Transmission & Correction). All corrections shall be documented with the reason for the change and the clinical evidence supporting the corrected response.
4.8 Financial pressure, revenue targets, payment optimization goals, or any external influence on OASIS response selection are explicitly prohibited. OASIS responses shall reflect the patient's actual clinical status — the payment consequence of an accurate response is never a justification for an inaccurate one.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS | Outcome and Assessment Information Set — the standardized data set mandated by CMS for all Medicare-certified home health agencies, currently in version OASIS-E2. |
| OASIS Item | A single data element within the OASIS data set, identified by an alphanumeric code (e.g., M1800, GG0130A). Each item has a specific definition, data collection instructions, and response options defined in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. |
| OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual | The CMS-published document that provides item-specific guidance for every OASIS data element, including definitions of response options, look-back periods, time points at which items are collected, and special circumstances. This is the definitive authority for all OASIS coding decisions. |
| Assessment Time Point | A specific clinical event that triggers an OASIS assessment requirement. The six time points are: SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU (Follow-Up/SCIC), TRN (Transfer), and DC (Discharge). |
| Look-Back Period | The CMS-defined timeframe prior to the assessment date during which clinical information is considered for coding a specific OASIS item. Look-back periods vary by item — some items require assessment of the past 24 hours, others 7 days, others 14 days, and some items are assessed at the moment of the visit (point-in-time). |
| OASIS Authorized Assessor | A registered nurse who has completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program and is authorized by the Director of Nursing to independently conduct comprehensive assessments and collect OASIS data. |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer | A designated RN with advanced OASIS expertise who conducts pre- and post-submission accuracy reviews of OASIS assessments. The Quality Reviewer is typically the Director of Nursing or a designee with OASIS specialist training. |
| Data Accuracy Rate | The percentage of audited OASIS item responses that match the correct response as determined by independent expert review, calculated per item category and overall. |
| Upcoding | The practice of selecting OASIS responses that reflect a higher level of functional impairment, disease severity, or resource need than the patient's actual clinical status in order to maximize payment — a False Claims Act violation. |
| Undercoding | The practice of selecting OASIS responses that reflect a lower level of functional impairment, disease severity, or clinical need than the patient's actual clinical status — a quality measure accuracy failure and a documentation integrity failure. |
| SCIC Assessment | Significant Change in Condition assessment — a Follow-Up (FU) OASIS assessment triggered when a patient experiences a major decline or improvement in health status that meets the CMS criteria for a significant change, requiring reassessment of applicable OASIS items. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 OASIS Data Collection — General Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Before conducting any OASIS assessment, verify that the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual is available (electronic access or printed current edition). Never rely on memory, informal summaries, or prior-version guidance for item-specific coding decisions. | Before each assessment. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Identify all OASIS items applicable to the specific assessment time point being conducted. The items collected vary by time point — not all items are collected at all time points. Use the time-point applicability table in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual to confirm item applicability. | Before each assessment. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | For each applicable OASIS item, identify the look-back period specified in the CMS guidance. Information collected outside the look-back period shall not be used to code the item, regardless of its clinical relevance. | During data collection. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Collect OASIS data through a combination of: (a) direct observation and physical examination of the patient during the visit; (b) structured clinical interview of the patient using validated tools where required (PHQ-2/PHQ-9, BIMS, MAHC-10); (c) structured interview of the caregiver regarding the patient's typical performance; (d) review of all available clinical documentation within the applicable look-back period. Do not select a response based on any single source alone when multiple sources are available and relevant. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | When the patient's performance or status varies across the look-back period (some days better, some days worse), select the OASIS response that reflects the patient's usual status — the level of performance or impairment that most consistently describes the patient across the look-back period. When CMS guidance specifies a different selection rule for a specific item (e.g., worst-case selection for certain safety items), follow that item-specific rule. | During data collection. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Document the clinical basis for every OASIS response in the assessment narrative at the time of the assessment — not after the fact. The narrative shall describe the specific observation, test result, or patient report that led to the selected response. The linkage between the narrative and the OASIS response must be traceable and unambiguous per CL-OA-007. | During and immediately after the assessment. |

### 6.2 Domain-Specific OASIS Accuracy Standards
The following domain-specific accuracy standards shall govern response selection for the highest-risk OASIS item categories. These standards supplement the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and do not supersede it.
#### 6.2.1 Functional Status — GG Items (GG0130, GG0170)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1.1 | Assigned RN | The GG functional items assess the patient's performance of specific activities — not their capacity. Observe the patient perform each activity during the visit whenever possible. Do not select a response based solely on the patient's or caregiver's report of what the patient can or cannot do. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.2.1.2 | Assigned RN | Use the activity-specific scoring guidance in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for each GG item. The response options follow a standardized functional independence scale — select the response that accurately reflects the level of assistance the patient requires, not the level the clinician believes the patient should require. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.1.3 | Assigned RN | Document the specific activity performed and observed, the level of assistance provided by the clinician or caregiver, the patient's performance quality, and any safety concerns identified. This documentation shall be specific enough that a second RN reviewing the record could independently arrive at the same GG response. | Within 24 hours of the assessment. |
| 6.2.1.4 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review all GG functional item responses at the SOC assessment against the narrative documentation. Flag any GG response that is not supported by a documented observation of the patient performing (or attempting to perform) the specific activity. | Within 5 business days of assessment lock. |

#### 6.2.2 Wound Assessment — M1311–M1350

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.2.1 | Assigned RN | At every applicable OASIS time point, undress all wound dressings and directly observe all wounds before coding any wound items. Do not code wound items based on prior documentation without direct observation. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.2.2.2 | Assigned RN | Apply the NPIAP staging system exclusively for pressure injuries. Do not use any other staging system. Do not reverse-stage a healing pressure injury — once staged at Stage 3 or Stage 4, the wound retains that stage designation for the life of the wound regardless of healing progress. Code the wound as "Stage 3, healing" or "Stage 4, healing" rather than downstaging. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.2.3 | Assigned RN | For M1340 (Does this patient have a Surgical Wound) and M1342 (Status of Most Problematic Surgical Wound), apply the CMS-defined response options precisely per the guidance manual. Do not conflate wound types (e.g., coding a dehisced surgical wound as a pressure injury). | During data collection. |
| 6.2.2.4 | Assigned RN | Document all wound assessment findings using the Wound Assessment Documentation Template per CL-SD-011, ensuring that the documented wound status directly supports the M1311–M1350 OASIS responses. Cross-reference all wound OASIS items with the wound narrative documentation before locking the assessment. | Within 24 hours of assessment. |

#### 6.2.3 Behavioral Health — M1700–M1750

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.3.1 | Assigned RN | Administer the BIMS for M1700 (Cognitive Function) using the validated CMS protocol — three-word repetition, temporal orientation, and word recall. Document the item-level scores and the total score. Code M1700 using the BIMS score ranges specified in the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. If the patient is unable to complete the BIMS, use the Staff Assessment for Mental Status (SAMS) and code M1700 accordingly. | During the assessment. |
| 6.2.3.2 | Assigned RN | Administer the PHQ-2 (and PHQ-9 if PHQ-2 ≥3) for M1730 (Depressive Feelings) per CL-SD-022. Code M1730 using the PHQ-9 score ranges specified in the guidance. Do not code M1730 based solely on clinical impression — the validated tool administration and score are required. | During the assessment. |
| 6.2.3.3 | Assigned RN | For M1740 (Behaviors Demonstrated at Least Once a Week) and M1745 (Frequency of Disruptive/Problematic Behaviors), apply the 7-day look-back period specified in the guidance. Base coding on caregiver report and clinical observation — not exclusively on what is observed during the visit itself. | During the assessment with caregiver interview. |

#### 6.2.4 Medication Management — M2001, M2003, M2010

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.4.1 | Assigned RN | Code M2001 (Drug Regimen Review) based on whether a drug regimen review was completed during the assessment and whether potential clinically significant medication issues were identified. Apply the CMS-defined criteria for "potential clinically significant medication issues" (drug interactions, allergies, duplication, wrong dose, wrong drug). | During data collection. |
| 6.2.4.2 | Assigned RN | Code M2003 (Medication Follow-Up) based on whether a physician was contacted within one calendar day of completing the drug regimen review when a potential clinically significant medication issue was identified. This is a process measure — it requires physician contact, not just documentation of the issue. | Based on actions taken following the review. |
| 6.2.4.3 | Assigned RN | Code M2010 (Patient/Caregiver High-Risk Drug Education) based on whether the patient/caregiver received education specific to high-risk medications per the CMS definition. Apply the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual's definition of "high-risk medications" — which differs from the agency's clinical high-alert medication list per RM-PS-005. | During data collection. |
| 6.2.4.4 | Assigned RN | Code medication management items per CL-OA-014 (Medication Reconciliation — Prescribed Regimen vs. Actual Patient Behavior) — distinguish between what is prescribed and what the patient is actually taking. Code the items based on the patient's actual medication-taking behavior, not the prescribed regimen alone. | During data collection. |

#### 6.2.5 Homebound Status and Eligibility

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.5.1 | Assigned RN | While homebound status is not a single OASIS item, it is assessed and documented as part of the comprehensive assessment and is a prerequisite for billing any Medicare home health visit. At each applicable time point, reassess and re-document homebound status with patient-specific clinical language per CL-CA-005. | At each OASIS time point. |
| 6.2.5.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | At each SOC review, verify that the homebound status narrative contains patient-specific functional limitations — not generic language. Flag any homebound documentation that uses template language without individualization. | Within 5 business days of assessment lock. |

### 6.3 Pre-Submission Self-Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN | Before locking any OASIS assessment, complete the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019. The checklist shall verify: (a) all applicable items are completed; (b) no items are left at default or blank without clinical justification; (c) functionally related item groups are internally consistent (e.g., ambulation and locomotion items are consistent with each other and with the physical examination narrative); (d) medication items are consistent with the medication list; (e) wound items are consistent with the wound assessment narrative; (f) behavioral health items are consistent with the standardized tool scores; (g) homebound status and skilled need are documented. | Before locking each assessment. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | If the self-review identifies any inconsistency, omission, or unsupported response, correct the assessment before locking. Document the correction and the basis for the corrected response. | Before locking. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Lock the assessment only after the self-review is complete and all identified issues are resolved. A locked assessment may not be modified without following the correction process per CL-CA-003. | After self-review completion. |

### 6.4 OASIS Quality Reviewer Review — Post-Lock, Pre-Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking, using the OASIS Quality Review Tool (Appendix A). The review shall assess: accuracy of GG functional items; accuracy of wound items (M1311–M1350); accuracy of behavioral health items (M1700–M1750); accuracy of medication management items (M2001–M2010); narrative-OASIS consistency for all reviewed items; homebound documentation adequacy; skilled need documentation adequacy. | Within 5 business days of locking. |
| 6.4.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Document the review findings in the OASIS Quality Review Log (Appendix B), including: the assessment date, the assessing RN, each item reviewed, the reviewer's determination (Accurate / Inaccurate — requires correction / Insufficient documentation), and any corrective action recommended. | At the time of the review. |
| 6.4.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If an inaccuracy is identified, communicate the finding to the assessing RN and the Director of Nursing within 24 hours, providing the item number, the assessing RN's response, the reviewer's determination of the correct response, and the clinical evidence supporting the correction. | Within 24 hours of finding. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | If the assessing RN agrees with the reviewer's finding, initiate the OASIS correction process per CL-CA-003. If the assessing RN disagrees with the reviewer's determination, escalate to the Director of Nursing for clinical adjudication within 24 hours of the disagreement. The Director of Nursing's determination is final. | Within 24 hours of disagreement notification. |
| 6.4.5 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Conduct quarterly ROC, RECERT, and DC assessment reviews at a minimum 10% sample rate, using the same review methodology as SOC reviews. | Quarterly. |

### 6.5 Monthly OASIS Accuracy Audit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct or commission a monthly OASIS accuracy audit covering ≥5% of all submitted assessments from the prior month, using the OASIS Quality Review Tool (Appendix A). The audit shall include all time points in the sample, not only SOC assessments. | Monthly. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | Calculate the data accuracy rate for the audited sample by item category: GG functional items, wound items, behavioral health items, medication items, and overall. Document the accuracy rate in the OASIS Accuracy Dashboard (Appendix C). | Within 5 business days of audit completion. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | Present OASIS accuracy results to the QAPI Committee quarterly. Identify any item category with an accuracy rate below 95% and initiate a Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001. | Quarterly QAPI meeting. |
| 6.5.4 | Director of Nursing | Provide individual clinician-level OASIS accuracy feedback to each RN assessor based on audit findings. For any RN with an accuracy rate below 85% on any item category, provide targeted retraining within 14 calendar days and schedule a follow-up audit within 30 calendar days. | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS item completed by a non-RN staff member | Director of Nursing identifies | All OASIS items completed by the non-authorized individual shall be voided and re-completed by a qualified RN. Director of Nursing assesses all visits affected for billing implications. Compliance Officer notified. | Re-assessment within 5 business days; compliance review within 14 calendar days. |
| Systematic OASIS accuracy pattern suggesting upcoding or undercoding across multiple patients | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer conduct a full-scope review of all assessments submitted by the identified assessor(s) within the prior 90 days. Corrective action, retraining, and self-disclosure assessment per CO-CP-007 and FN-BC-004. | Review initiated within 5 business days; corrective action within 30 calendar days. |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer and assessing RN disagree on a response and escalation to Director of Nursing does not resolve the disagreement | Administrator and Compliance Officer | The Compliance Officer reviews the clinical record and CMS guidance independently. The Compliance Officer's determination reflects the agency's official coding position. If the Compliance Officer determines the submitted response is inaccurate and was submitted as a paid claim, initiate correction and overpayment assessment per FN-BC-004. | Resolution within 7 calendar days. |
| OASIS accuracy rate falls below 90% agency-wide in any quarter | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Agency-wide OASIS retraining initiated. External OASIS consultant engaged for review if accuracy rate does not recover above 92% within 60 calendar days. Governing Body notified at next quarterly meeting. | Retraining within 14 calendar days; consultant within 30 calendar days if needed. |
