### 2. Purpose
This policy requires all OASIS responses to align with the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and prohibits agency-created coding interpretations that conflict with CMS guidance at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The OASIS Guidance Manual is the definitive authority for every coding decision — not the assessor's clinical intuition, not the agency's internally developed "cheat sheets," not the guidance from a prior version of OASIS, not the interpretation provided by a revenue cycle vendor, and not what the agency believes CMS "should" mean by a particular item definition.
The history of home health compliance enforcement is littered with agencies that developed their own internal OASIS coding conventions — often driven by payment optimization concerns — that deviated from or directly contradicted the CMS Guidance Manual. These deviations, when identified through OASIS validation surveys, MAC audits, or OIG investigations, produced findings of systematic upcoding or inaccurate data reporting that led to recoupments, corrective action plans, and in some cases False Claims Act settlements. The agency that codes the GG functional items by asking the patient what they can do, rather than by observing what they actually do during the visit, is not just making a clinical error — it is systematically overstating functional impairment in a way that increases PDGM payment. The agency that codes wound stages without applying the NPIAP staging system is not just making an assessment error — it is generating invalid quality measure data that misrepresents the agency's patient outcomes.
This policy establishes the absolute authority of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, the process for accessing and maintaining current guidance, the prohibition on agency-created alternative interpretations, the process for resolving item-level ambiguity through legitimate channels, and the governance of guidance updates when CMS revises the OASIS instrument or the Guidance Manual.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All authorized OASIS assessors who make item-level coding decisions
The Director of Nursing who oversees coding guidance compliance
The OASIS Quality Reviewer who validates item-level coding against the Guidance Manual
The Compliance Officer who oversees the prohibition on financially motivated coding deviations
Any educational materials, training programs, reference tools, or coding aids used by the agency in connection with OASIS assessment
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual — the most current version, as published by CMS — is the sole authoritative source for all OASIS item-level coding decisions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. No other source has equivalent authority.
4.2 When an assessor has a question about the correct coding of any OASIS item for a specific patient situation, the correct process is: first, consult the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for the specific item; second, review the item-specific FAQ or Q&A materials published by CMS or the relevant state OASIS contractor; third, consult the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer for clinical adjudication; fourth, if the guidance remains unclear, submit the question to the CMS OASIS contractor or the state OASIS coordinator through the official Q&A submission process. At no point in this process shall the assessor create an agency-specific interpretation that is not grounded in and consistent with CMS guidance.
4.3 The agency shall maintain a current, accessible copy of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual in the EHR reference library and shall update it within 30 calendar days of any CMS revision to the Guidance Manual. Assessors shall access the Guidance Manual from the agency's EHR reference library — not from memory, from prior-version documents, or from third-party materials that have not been verified for consistency with the current Guidance Manual.
4.4 The following practices are explicitly prohibited at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.:
(a) Using a prior version of the OASIS Guidance Manual as the basis for any coding decision after a new version has been published and adopted.
(b) Applying an internally developed "cheat sheet," "quick reference guide," or coding shortcut that selects OASIS response options through a decision pathway not grounded in the current CMS Guidance Manual. All quick reference materials used in OASIS coding must be verified against the current Guidance Manual and must explicitly note that they are supplements to — not replacements of — the Guidance Manual.
(c) Coding OASIS items in a systematic manner that departs from the Guidance Manual's response selection rules — including but not limited to: coding GG functional items based solely on patient or caregiver report without observing the patient perform the activity; coding wound items without undressing dressings and directly observing wounds; coding behavioral health items without administering the required standardized tools in validated protocols; or reverse-staging healing pressure injuries.
(d) Accepting OASIS coding instructions from revenue cycle staff, billing consultants, or management personnel that deviate from the CMS Guidance Manual's response selection rules, for any reason — including payment optimization.
(e) Retaining in the agency's reference library any OASIS coding guidance, training material, or reference tool that conflicts with the current version of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, without clearly marking the conflicting material as "SUPERSEDED — DO NOT USE."
4.5 When the CMS Guidance Manual provides an unclear or ambiguous response to a specific clinical scenario — a situation that genuinely exists for some items — the assessor shall use the clinical reasoning documentation process per CL-OA-012 to document the specific ambiguity, the interpretive approach applied, and the clinical basis for the selected response. This documentation does not authorize deviation from CMS guidance — it documents the assessor's good-faith application of judgment where the guidance itself is ambiguous.
4.6 The agency shall track CMS OASIS guidance updates through the CMS website, CMS OASIS listservs, and state OASIS contractor communications, and shall disseminate updates to all authorized assessors within 14 calendar days of any change to the Guidance Manual.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual | The current, definitive, CMS-published document providing item-specific guidance for all OASIS data collection decisions, including definitions of response options, look-back periods, time points at which items are collected, and special circumstances. The authoritative source for all coding decisions. |
| Item-Level Guidance | The specific instructions, definitions, response option descriptions, special circumstances guidance, and coding rules provided in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for a specific OASIS item. |
| Agency-Created Coding Interpretation | Any OASIS coding rule, convention, shortcut, or guidance document developed by the agency, its management, its revenue cycle team, or any third party that is not grounded in or consistent with the current CMS Guidance Manual. Prohibited by this policy. |
| Guidance Ambiguity | A situation where the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual does not clearly and unambiguously resolve the correct coding response for a specific clinical scenario. Requires clinical reasoning documentation per CL-OA-012. |
| CMS OASIS Guidance Update | A revision to the OASIS data set, the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, the OASIS Q&A database, or associated CMS guidance documents that changes item definitions, response options, collection rules, or coding instructions. |
| Quick Reference Material | Any abbreviated coding guide, summary document, or reference card used by assessors to support OASIS completion — permissible only if grounded in and consistent with the current CMS Guidance Manual and clearly labeled as a supplement to the Guidance Manual. |
| OASIS Contractor | The CMS-contracted organization responsible for providing training, technical assistance, and Q&A resolution for OASIS-related questions. The official channel for submitting questions about OASIS coding not resolved by the Guidance Manual itself. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Access to Current CMS OASIS Guidance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Maintain a current copy of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual in the agency's EHR reference library, accessible to all authorized assessors at any time from any device with EHR access. The EHR reference library copy shall be the current version — when CMS publishes a new version, the outdated version shall be replaced within 30 calendar days and marked "SUPERSEDED" if retained for reference. | Current version maintained continuously; update within 30 calendar days of CMS publication. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | Subscribe to the CMS OASIS listserv, state OASIS contractor notifications, and relevant CMS email updates to receive notification of Guidance Manual revisions, Q&A updates, and coding clarifications as soon as they are issued. | Subscriptions maintained continuously. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | When a CMS OASIS Guidance update is received, assess its impact: (a) identify which items have been changed; (b) identify how the changes affect current assessor practice; (c) determine whether immediate correction of any in-progress assessments is needed; (d) prepare a training update for all authorized assessors. | Within 5 business days of receiving the update. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Distribute the guidance update to all authorized assessors within 14 calendar days, with a written summary of: what changed; how it differs from the prior guidance; practical examples illustrating the new coding approach; and any assessments submitted under the prior guidance that may require correction. Obtain written acknowledgment from each assessor that they received and reviewed the update. | Within 14 calendar days of the update. |

#### 6.2 Item-Level Ambiguity Resolution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assessing RN | When encountering a clinical situation where the correct OASIS coding is unclear — because the patient's presentation does not map cleanly to the Guidance Manual's response option definitions — follow this sequential resolution process: Step 1: Review the complete item-specific guidance in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, including special circumstances, Q&A sections, and any relevant examples provided. Step 2: Search the CMS OASIS Q&A database (available on the CMS website) for existing Q&As addressing the specific scenario. Step 3: Consult the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer for clinical adjudication. Step 4: If the ambiguity cannot be resolved through Steps 1–3, the Director of Nursing may submit a formal question to the state OASIS contractor for official guidance. | Before finalizing the coding decision. |
| 6.2.2 | Assessing RN | Document the ambiguity resolution process per CL-OA-012: note the specific ambiguity, the steps taken to resolve it, the clinical reasoning applied, and the final coding decision with its basis. This documentation is both a clinical record entry and a compliance defense if the coding decision is later questioned. | In the assessment narrative; within 24 hours of the decision. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Compile a log of recurring item-level ambiguities encountered by the agency's assessors. Use the log to: identify training needs; prepare pre-emptive guidance for common ambiguous scenarios; and submit formal questions to the OASIS contractor to obtain official resolution. Share the log and any official Q&A responses with all authorized assessors. | Log reviewed quarterly; formal Q&A submissions as warranted. |

#### 6.3 Audit of Coding Materials for Guidance Compliance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct an annual audit of all OASIS coding materials in the agency's possession — including printed reference guides, digital reference cards, training slides, coding worksheets, and any third-party training materials — to verify that each material is: (a) consistent with the current version of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual; (b) clearly labeled as a supplement to — not replacement of — the Guidance Manual; (c) dated and identified as applicable to the current OASIS version. | Annually; concurrent with the annual OASIS re-competency cycle. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Remove or destroy any coding material that: contains instructions or response-selection shortcuts that are inconsistent with the current Guidance Manual; was prepared for a prior version of the OASIS without having been updated for the current version; or contains language suggesting that payment optimization should influence coding decisions. Document the removal and the reason in the materials audit log. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct a quarterly review of the Director of Nursing's OASIS coding materials audit log and assess whether any identified deviations suggest systemic compliance risk requiring investigation or corrective action. | Quarterly. |

#### 6.4 Governance of Third-Party OASIS Training and Reference Materials

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Before distributing any third-party OASIS training material — including materials from training vendors, professional associations, or peer agencies — verify its consistency with the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. If any third-party material conflicts with the Guidance Manual, the Guidance Manual governs. Annotate any conflicting third-party material with the correct guidance before distribution. | Before any distribution. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Assess all agency EHR-embedded OASIS coding guidance or drop-down prompts for consistency with the current CMS Guidance Manual annually and whenever the OASIS instrument is updated. Report any EHR-embedded guidance that is inconsistent with current CMS guidance to the IT Director and EHR vendor for correction. | Annually; within 30 calendar days of any OASIS update. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Do not accept OASIS coding instruction from revenue cycle consultants, coding vendors, or billing companies that selects response options on the basis of payment optimization rather than clinical accuracy. Report any such instruction to the Compliance Officer immediately. | Immediately upon identification. |

#### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An assessor is found to be using an outdated version of the Guidance Manual | Director of Nursing | Immediately provide the current Guidance Manual. Assess all assessments completed under the outdated guidance for potential coding errors. Initiate corrections for any identified errors per CL-OA-002. | Immediate guidance correction; assessment review within 14 calendar days. |
| Revenue cycle staff or management instructs assessors to code in a specific way to increase PDGM payment | Compliance Officer | The Compliance Officer initiates a compliance investigation per CO-CP-007. Immediate corrective communication to all parties. Assessment of all assessments coded under the instruction for potential corrections and overpayment. Governing Body notification. | Immediate Compliance Officer involvement; investigation within 24 hours. |
| A CMS OASIS Guidance update contradicts a prior training that assessors received | Director of Nursing | Issue an immediate update communication to all assessors. Schedule a focused training session on the changed item within 14 calendar days. Review recent assessments for items affected by the change. Initiate corrections per CL-OA-002 for assessments coded under the superseded guidance if the change affects clinical accuracy of submitted data. | Immediate communication; training within 14 calendar days; assessment review within 30 calendar days. |
| An assessor consistently selects the highest severity response option for GG functional items without documenting observation of the patient performing the activity | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Director of Nursing conducts targeted retraining on GG observation requirement. OASIS Quality Reviewer conducts a 100% review of the assessor's GG items from the past 90 days. Compliance Officer assesses whether the pattern constitutes systematic upcoding. | Retraining within 7 calendar days; comprehensive review within 30 calendar days. |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual accessible in EHR reference library | IT / Medical Records audit | 100% — current version confirmed at each quarterly review |
| All guidance updates distributed to assessors within 14 calendar days | Distribution log with dates | 100% |
| No coding materials in use that conflict with current Guidance Manual | Annual materials audit | 100% — no non-conforming materials in active use |
| Item-level ambiguity documentation present for all complex coding decisions | Monthly OASIS quality review per CL-OA-002 | ≥95% of audited ambiguous items with documented reasoning |
| No revenue-motivated coding instruction identified | Compliance Officer quarterly review | Zero violations |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will select specific OASIS items from a patient sample and will bring the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual to compare the agency's coding decisions against. They will verify that the assessor can articulate the CMS guidance basis for the selected response. They will also review the agency's coding reference materials and assess whether any of these materials contain response-selection shortcuts that bypass or misrepresent the Guidance Manual's rules.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessors coding from memory without consulting the Guidance Manual | Inaccurate responses based on clinical intuition rather than CMS rules | EHR reference library Guidance Manual accessible at every visit via mobile; training emphasizes "when in doubt, look it up" |
| Agency-developed quick reference guides that simplify response selection in ways that deviate from the Guidance Manual | Systematic coding inaccuracy; potential upcoding | Annual materials audit; all quick reference materials must cite specific Guidance Manual page references |
| Guidance Manual update not distributed — assessors still coding under prior version | Coding errors for changed items | CMS subscription; Director of Nursing update protocol within 14 calendar days |
| Revenue cycle pressure on assessors to code toward higher payment groups | False Claims Act exposure | Zero-tolerance policy in this policy statement; Compliance hotline for reporting; Compliance Officer quarterly review |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes controls to ensure OASIS data is accurate, complete, securely transmitted, and protected from unauthorized access or modification at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. OASIS data occupies a unique position at the intersection of clinical accuracy, financial integrity, and data security. It is simultaneously: (a) protected health information (PHI) under HIPAA — subject to all access control, transmission security, and breach notification requirements; (b) a clinical quality record — the accuracy of which determines the validity of every quality measure the agency reports publicly; (c) a financial record — the content of which drives Medicare payment classification and creates billing compliance obligations; and (d) a regulatory submission — transmitted to a federal database and subject to the full enforcement authority of CMS, OIG, and the Department of Justice.
The security and integrity dimensions of OASIS data are frequently underemphasized in home health agency governance. Agencies focus intensely on coding accuracy — and rightly so — but the controls that ensure data integrity (is this actually what the assessor coded?) and security (who can access, modify, or transmit this data?) are equally essential and equally subject to regulatory scrutiny. An OASIS database that allows non-clinical staff to modify assessment responses, that transmits data over unencrypted channels, that lacks an audit trail of every modification, or that cannot demonstrate the chain of custody from the assessor's clinical evaluation to the transmitted CMS record has failed the data integrity and security obligations that underpin the validity of the entire OASIS program.
This policy establishes the complete data integrity and security framework for OASIS data at this agency — the access controls, the transmission security standards, the audit trail requirements, the data retention protocols, and the breach and unauthorized modification response process.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All authorized OASIS assessors who create, access, and authenticate OASIS data
The Director of Nursing who oversees OASIS data governance
IT Director / CISO who configures and maintains EHR security controls for OASIS data
OASIS Transmission Coordinator who manages data transmission to CMS
Medical Records staff who manage completed OASIS data within the clinical record
The Compliance Officer who oversees HIPAA compliance and data breach response
Revenue Cycle staff who access OASIS data for payment classification purposes
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 OASIS data — including all draft and completed OASIS assessments, all transmission records, all quality review records, and all correction documentation — is protected health information (PHI) under HIPAA and shall be protected in accordance with all HIPAA Privacy and Security Rule requirements per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002.
4.2 Access to OASIS assessment data within the EHR shall be restricted through role-based access controls per IT-SC-002. Only the following roles may access OASIS data: authorized RN assessors (for assessments in their assigned caseload); the OASIS Quality Reviewer; the Director of Nursing; Revenue Cycle staff (read-only access for payment classification verification); the Compliance Officer; and Medical Records staff. No other role — including non-clinical administrative staff, HHAs, LVNs, and therapy staff — shall have access to the OASIS assessment module.
4.3 OASIS data shall not be modified by any person other than the original assessing RN or the Director of Nursing / OASIS Quality Reviewer conducting a legitimate error correction per CL-OA-002. Any modification to a locked OASIS assessment shall be captured in an auditable amendment record per CO-DC-001, identifying the person who made the modification, the date and time, the original content, and the modified content.
4.4 OASIS data shall be transmitted to the CMS national repository using only CMS-approved, encrypted transmission channels through the agency's certified OASIS submission software. Transmission over unsecured networks, unencrypted channels, or through unauthorized software is prohibited.
4.5 The EHR shall maintain a complete, unalterable audit trail of all access to and all modifications of OASIS assessment data, per CO-DC-001. The audit trail shall record: the user identity; the date and time of access or modification; the specific data accessed or modified; and the type of action (view, create, modify, delete). The audit trail itself shall be protected from modification and shall be retained for a minimum of 7 years.
4.6 Any suspected unauthorized access to, unauthorized modification of, or breach of OASIS data shall be reported to the IT Director and Compliance Officer within 2 hours of identification, and shall be investigated and addressed per the HIPAA Breach Notification requirements of CO-HP-003.
4.7 OASIS data shall be retained in the EHR for a minimum of 7 years from the date of submission to the CMS repository, consistent with the retention requirements of CO-HP-007 and CMS record retention standards.
4.8 OASIS data shall not be stored, processed, or transmitted outside the agency's HIPAA-compliant systems and networks. OASIS data shall not be stored on personal devices, personal cloud storage, unencrypted USB drives, or any other storage medium that is not managed and secured under the agency's IT security program per IT-SC-002 through IT-SC-006.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS Data | All information contained in or derived from OASIS assessments — including raw assessment data, locked assessment records, transmission records, quality review records, correction records, and derived measures such as PDGM payment groups and quality measure indicators. |
| Data Integrity | The property of OASIS data that ensures it accurately represents what the assessing RN recorded at the time of assessment, has not been modified without authorization, and can be traced from the original assessment to the CMS repository without unexplained alteration. |
| Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) | An EHR security configuration that grants each user access only to the data and functions necessary for their specific job role — preventing access by individuals whose roles do not require OASIS data access. |
| Audit Trail | The EHR-generated, unalterable electronic log that permanently records every access to and modification of OASIS assessment data, including the user identity, the date and time, and the specific action performed. |
| Encrypted Transmission | The use of cryptographic protocols (e.g., TLS/SSL) that protect data during transmission by converting it into a form that cannot be read without the correct decryption key — required for all OASIS data transmissions to the CMS repository. |
| Unauthorized Access | Any access to OASIS data by a person whose role does not include authorized access, or any access by an authorized person to data not within their legitimate clinical or administrative scope. |
| Unauthorized Modification | Any change to OASIS assessment data made without following the authorized correction process defined in CL-OA-002, or made by a person not authorized to make corrections. |
| Data Breach | An unauthorized acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of OASIS data that compromises the security or privacy of the PHI contained in the data, triggering HIPAA Breach Notification obligations per CO-HP-003. |
| Data Retention | The practice of maintaining OASIS assessment records for the required minimum period before authorizing destruction, ensuring availability for audit, litigation, and quality review purposes. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Access Control Configuration and Maintenance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | IT Director | Configure role-based access controls in the EHR to restrict the OASIS assessment module to the authorized roles specified in Section 4.2. The configuration shall prevent: (a) read access to OASIS assessment data by any role not listed in Section 4.2; (b) write access (creating or modifying OASIS data) by any user not on the current OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster per CL-OA-003; (c) deletion of any OASIS assessment or audit trail record by any user. | EHR configuration established at implementation; verified at each annual security review per IT-SC-002. |
| 6.1.2 | IT Director | Generate a monthly OASIS access control report showing: all users who have OASIS module access by role; any access granted in the prior month; any access revoked in the prior month. Distribute to the Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer. | Monthly. |
| 6.1.3 | IT Director | When an individual leaves the agency or changes roles, revoke or modify their OASIS access within 4 hours of notification of the separation or role change. This is a HIPAA-mandated security control — delayed revocation creates unauthorized access liability. | Within 4 hours of notification. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Verify the accuracy of the OASIS access control list monthly, by comparing the IT access control report against the current OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster per CL-OA-003. Notify IT Director of any discrepancy for immediate correction. | Monthly; correction within 24 hours of identification. |
| 6.1.5 | IT Director | Conduct a formal OASIS access control audit annually, reviewing all user access permissions against current authorized roles and identifying any excessive permissions, stale accounts, or access granted to non-authorized users. Present findings to the Compliance Officer. | Annually. |

#### 6.2 Audit Trail Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | IT Director | Ensure the EHR generates a complete, automatic, unalterable audit trail for all OASIS assessment data access and modification events, capturing: user ID; date and time; IP address or device identifier; action type (view, create, lock, modify, attempt to delete); specific assessment record accessed; and any data changed (before and after values for modifications). | Audit trail generation: continuous. Configuration verified quarterly. |
| 6.2.2 | IT Director | Protect the OASIS audit trail from modification or deletion by any user — including administrative users. The audit trail shall be stored in a write-once format or equivalent protection, and shall be accessible to the Compliance Officer and Director of Nursing but not modifiable by any user. | Audit trail protection: continuous. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing / Compliance Officer | Review the OASIS audit trail monthly for: (a) access by unauthorized users; (b) access by authorized users outside their normal clinical scope; (c) modifications to locked assessments without documented correction authorization per CL-OA-002; (d) access at unusual times (e.g., late night access from unusual locations). | Monthly. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Any audit trail anomaly that suggests unauthorized access or unauthorized modification shall be treated as a potential HIPAA security incident and investigated per CO-HP-003 within 24 hours of identification. | Within 24 hours of identification. |
| 6.2.5 | IT Director | Retain all OASIS audit trail records for a minimum of 7 years from the date of the access event, consistent with HIPAA Security Rule record retention requirements and CO-HP-007. | Continuous; reviewed annually. |

#### 6.3 Secure Transmission — OASIS Data to CMS Repository

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Transmit all OASIS data using only the agency's certified OASIS submission software, connected to the CMS OASIS repository through the approved encrypted transmission pathway. The agency shall maintain a current, licensed, CMS-certified version of the OASIS submission software. | At each transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | IT Director | Verify annually that the OASIS submission software and its data transmission pathway use current encryption standards meeting or exceeding HIPAA Security Rule requirements (minimum TLS 1.2 or equivalent). Update the software if encryption standards are found to be below current requirements. | Annually; immediately upon identifying a below-standard encryption configuration. |
| 6.3.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Never transmit OASIS data using: email (even encrypted email); file transfer protocol (FTP) without SFTP/FTPS encryption; USB drives or portable storage; personal email accounts; or any channel other than the approved CMS transmission pathway. | At all times. |
| 6.3.4 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Verify successful CMS receipt confirmation for every transmission per CL-CA-003. If a transmission fails or is rejected by CMS, notify the IT Director immediately to investigate whether the failure involved a security issue (vs. a data format or software issue). | Immediately upon transmission failure or rejection. |

#### 6.4 Data Storage Security

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | IT Director | Ensure that all OASIS data stored within the EHR is encrypted at rest using current encryption standards meeting or exceeding HIPAA Security Rule requirements. Verify encryption configuration annually. | Annual verification; updates as needed. |
| 6.4.2 | IT Director | Ensure that the EHR backup system includes OASIS data in all backup cycles, that backups are encrypted, and that backup restoration is tested annually per IT-DR-001. | Annual backup testing; continuous backup cycling. |
| 6.4.3 | All Personnel | Never export, save, or store OASIS data outside the agency's HIPAA-compliant EHR — including to personal computers, personal cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, personal OneDrive), or unmanaged USB drives. If OASIS data must be accessed for a specific legitimate purpose outside the EHR (e.g., for an audit response), use the agency's managed, encrypted file transfer system with Compliance Officer authorization. | At all times. |
| 6.4.4 | IT Director | Implement endpoint protection on all devices used to access the EHR, preventing unauthorized data export from the OASIS module through endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) controls per IT-SC-005. | Endpoint protection maintained continuously. |

#### 6.5 Unauthorized Access and Modification Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Any Agency Personnel | If any person observes or has reason to believe that OASIS data has been accessed by an unauthorized individual, modified without following the authorized correction process, transmitted through an unauthorized channel, or exposed through a security breach: report to the IT Director and Compliance Officer within 2 hours. | Within 2 hours of identification. |
| 6.5.2 | IT Director | Upon notification of a potential unauthorized access or modification: (a) immediately assess the scope of the incident using the EHR audit trail; (b) if unauthorized access is confirmed, contain the breach by revoking the involved user's access; (c) notify the Compliance Officer with full details within 4 hours. | Within 4 hours; audit trail review begins immediately. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Assess the incident under HIPAA Breach Notification standards per CO-HP-003: (a) does the incident constitute a breach of unsecured PHI? (b) if yes, are any of the four exceptions to breach notification applicable? (c) if the incident is a reportable breach, initiate the notification process — patient notification within 60 calendar days, HHS OCR notification within 60 calendar days, and media notification if more than 500 individuals in a single state are affected. | Per CO-HP-003 timelines. |
| 6.5.4 | Director of Nursing | Assess the clinical impact of any unauthorized OASIS modification: (a) was any OASIS assessment data changed? (b) did any change affect a claim that was submitted or will be submitted? (c) does the modification suggest an attempt to systematically alter OASIS data for financial benefit? | Within 24 hours of the security incident assessment. |
| 6.5.5 | Director of Nursing | If any OASIS assessment was modified without authorization: (a) review the audit trail to identify the original and modified data; (b) correct the assessment to reflect the original, accurate data through the authorized correction process per CL-OA-002; (c) assess whether the modification affected any submitted claims and initiate billing review with Revenue Cycle and the Compliance Officer. | Within 5 business days of incident identification. |

#### 6.6 Data Retention and Secure Destruction

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Medical Records | Retain all OASIS assessment data — including completed assessments, transmission records, quality review records, and correction records — for a minimum of 7 years from the date of the assessment submission to the CMS repository, per CO-HP-007 and CMS retention requirements. | Ongoing; reviewed annually. |
| 6.6.2 | Medical Records / IT Director | When OASIS data reaches the end of its retention period and is authorized for destruction: destroy electronic OASIS data using a HIPAA-compliant secure deletion method that renders the data irrecoverable (DoD 5220.22-M standard or equivalent). Document the destruction with the date, the data destroyed, the method of destruction, and the authorizing signature of the Compliance Officer. | At retention expiration with Compliance Officer authorization. |
| 6.6.3 | Compliance Officer | Authorize all OASIS data destruction in writing before destruction occurs. Verify that no legal hold, open audit, pending litigation, or government investigation prohibits destruction of the specific data before authorizing. | Before each destruction authorization. |

#### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EHR audit trail reveals OASIS modification by Revenue Cycle staff | Compliance Officer | Revenue Cycle staff access to OASIS write functions is immediately revoked. Compliance Officer investigates the modification for financial motivation per CO-CP-007. Assess for False Claims Act implications. | Immediate access revocation; investigation within 24 hours. |
| OASIS data is transmitted through an unencrypted channel (e.g., emailed to a payer in error) | IT Director and Compliance Officer | Treat as a potential HIPAA breach per CO-HP-003. Assess whether the data was actually received by the unauthorized recipient. Notify affected individuals if required. | HIPAA breach assessment within 24 hours. |
| EHR backup failure results in potential loss of OASIS assessment data | IT Director and Director of Nursing | IT Director initiates emergency backup recovery per IT-DR-001. Assess which OASIS records are at risk. If records cannot be recovered, assess whether the CMS repository retains a copy and whether the records can be reconstructed from the CMS data. | Recovery initiated within 4 hours; Compliance Officer notification within 24 hours. |
| A staff member exports OASIS data to a personal device in violation of this policy | IT Director and Compliance Officer | Assess the scope of the export. Contain the data by remotely wiping the personal device (if MDM capability exists) or demanding immediate deletion. Assess for HIPAA breach. Initiate HR disciplinary action per HR-ER-002. | Immediate containment; HIPAA assessment within 24 hours; HR action within 5 business days. |

### 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EHR OASIS access control configuration | Current configuration documentation and access control list | IT Director | IT security file | Maintained continuously; annual verification documented |
| Monthly OASIS access control report | Report of all users with OASIS access and any changes | IT Director | IT security file; Compliance Officer | Monthly; retained 7 years |
| EHR audit trail — OASIS data | Unalterable log of all OASIS access and modification events | EHR system (automatic) | EHR audit trail repository | Maintained continuously; retained 7 years |
| Monthly audit trail review | Documentation of Director of Nursing / Compliance Officer review findings | Director of Nursing / Compliance Officer | Director of Nursing supervisory file; Compliance file | Monthly; retained 7 years |
| Annual OASIS access control audit | Formal annual review of all OASIS access permissions | IT Director | IT security file | Annually; retained 7 years |
| Transmission security verification | Annual confirmation of encryption standards for CMS transmission pathway | IT Director | IT security file | Annually; retained 7 years |
| Data breach / unauthorized access investigation | HIPAA breach assessment and notification documentation | Compliance Officer | Compliance file | Per CO-HP-003 timelines; retained 7 years |
| Data destruction authorization | Written Compliance Officer authorization and destruction documentation | Compliance Officer / Medical Records | Compliance file | At each destruction event; retained 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS module EHR access restricted to authorized roles only | Monthly access control report | 100% consistent with authorized roles |
| All OASIS modifications captured in auditable audit trail | EHR audit trail completeness audit | 100% — no modifications without audit trail entry |
| All CMS OASIS transmissions use encrypted, approved transmission pathway | Transmission log and IT security verification | 100% |
| Monthly audit trail review completed | Review documentation audit | 100% of months |
| No unauthorized OASIS access incidents | Audit trail review and breach investigation log | Zero unremediated unauthorized access incidents |
| OASIS data retained for minimum 7 years | Medical Records retention audit | 100% |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting HIPAA security compliance reviews and OASIS validation surveys will:
Verify that only authorized personnel can access OASIS data — surveyors will request the EHR access configuration and verify it restricts access to appropriate roles.
Verify that an audit trail exists for OASIS data — surveyors will request the audit trail for selected assessment records and verify that all accesses and modifications are documented.
Verify secure transmission — surveyors will request the transmission software documentation and may ask about the encryption standards used.
Assess the agency's response to any identified security incidents — surveyors will request documentation of any unauthorized access incidents and the agency's breach assessment and response.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS module access granted to billing staff with write permissions | Unauthorized modification; False Claims Act risk | RBAC configuration limits Revenue Cycle to read-only access; annual access audit |
| EHR audit trail not reviewed regularly — anomalies detected only at survey | Unauthorized modifications undetected; HIPAA breach unreported | Monthly mandatory audit trail review by Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer |
| OASIS data exported to personal device for "convenience" during off-site work | HIPAA breach; data exposure; regulatory violation | Annual security awareness training; endpoint DLP controls; immediate disciplinary action |
| EHR backup does not include OASIS data in its scope | Risk of irreversible OASIS data loss | Annual backup verification includes confirmation that OASIS module data is included |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All authorized OASIS assessors shall receive training on OASIS data security requirements within 14 calendar days of initial authorization and annually thereafter, including: the prohibition on storing OASIS data outside the HIPAA-compliant EHR; the prohibition on transmitting OASIS data through unapproved channels; the audit trail and its implications for data integrity; and the reporting requirement for suspected unauthorized access.
10.2 IT staff responsible for EHR OASIS access controls shall receive training on the access control configuration requirements of this policy and on the audit trail review obligation at implementation and annually.
10.3 The Compliance Officer shall ensure that OASIS data security is incorporated into the agency's annual HIPAA security risk analysis per CO-HP-002.
10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
### 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy is valid. Superseded versions shall be archived as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval, re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days, and policy index update per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with Governing Body notification at the next regular meeting.

## CL-CD-002 — Clinical Record Content & Organization
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CD-002 |
| Policy Title | Clinical Record Content & Organization |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CD — Clinical Documentation |

| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 6.0 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the required content elements and organizational structure of every patient clinical record maintained by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A complete, well-organized clinical record is the legal and clinical foundation of patient care, serves as the primary basis for reimbursement, supports continuity among care providers, and demonstrates compliance with Medicare Conditions of Participation under 42 CFR § 484.110 and California licensing requirements under Title 22 CCR § 74751. Incomplete or disorganized records constitute a major survey deficiency and expose the agency to payment denial, civil monetary penalties, and program exclusion.

### 3. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff responsible for creating or maintaining patient documentation, including Registered Nurses, Licensed Vocational Nurses, Physical Therapists, Occupational Therapists, Speech-Language Pathologists, Medical Social Workers, and Home Health Aides. It applies to all patient records whether maintained in the agency's Electronic Health Record (EHR) system or in paper format.

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a complete clinical record for every patient receiving home health services. The record shall be initiated at the time of referral and remain active throughout the episode of care and for the retention period defined in CO-HP-007.

4.2 Every patient clinical record shall contain at minimum the following required content elements:
(a) Referral source documentation and intake assessment;
(b) Physician orders — initial, verbal, written, and change orders — authenticated per CL-CD-003;
(c) Completed and certified OASIS assessment(s) per CL-OA-001;
(d) Current, physician-approved Plan of Care (CMS-485 or equivalent) per CL-CP-001;
(e) Individualized care plan with measurable goals, disciplines, frequencies, and functional objectives per CL-CP-001;
(f) All visit notes (skilled nursing, therapy, social work, HHA supervisory, and HHA activity notes) per CL-CD-001;
(g) Medication profile with current medications, dosages, routes, and frequencies;
(h) Physician communication records including verbal order logs and telephone encounter notes;
(i) Diagnostic test results, laboratory reports, and imaging studies relevant to the home health episode;
(j) Patient/caregiver education documentation including topics taught, methods used, and learner response;
(k) Advance Directive documentation per CL-PR-002 — inquiry, copy if provided, and notation of patient decision;
(l) Consent documents per CL-PR-003;
(m) Patient Rights acknowledgment per CL-PR-001;
(n) Coordination of care notes including referrals to other disciplines, hospital communications, and specialist consultations;
(o) Discharge summary or transfer documentation for every episode closure;
(p) Supervisory visit documentation for Home Health Aide cases per CL-SD-006;
(q) All QAPI-related incident reports referencing the patient per QA-AE-004.

4.3 Clinical records shall be organized in a consistent, standardized manner as defined in the agency's EHR configuration or paper record structure. The sequence of documents shall allow any authorized reviewer to quickly locate the Plan of Care, most recent visit note, physician orders, and medication profile within 60 seconds of accessing the record.

4.4 No clinical record shall be altered, backdated, or falsified. Corrections shall be made by drawing a single line through the incorrect entry, entering the correction, and initialing and dating the correction. In electronic records, audit trail/version history shall be maintained by the EHR system.

4.5 The Director of Nursing or designee shall conduct quarterly audits of a random sample of 10% of active patient records to verify completeness and organization per QA-PG-001.

### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Record | The complete collection of documents related to a patient's care, whether electronic or paper, created and maintained by the agency during and after service provision. |
| Episode of Care | A 60-day period of Medicare home health services beginning with the first billable skilled visit and ending on day 60 or at discharge, whichever occurs first. |
| OASIS | Outcome and Assessment Information Set — the standardized patient assessment instrument required for Medicare home health. |
| Plan of Care (POC) | The physician-approved document that authorizes and defines all home health services for a patient during a certification period. |

### 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Intake Coordinator | Create patient record in EHR upon referral acceptance | Same business day as referral |
| 6.2 | Admitting RN | Complete all required SOC documentation including OASIS and initial POC | Within 5 business days of SOC |
| 6.3 | All Clinicians | Submit visit notes for each patient encounter | Within 24 hours of visit per CL-CD-004 |
| 6.4 | Physician Liaison | Obtain and file physician order signatures | Per CL-CP-002 timeframes |
| 6.5 | Medical Records | Audit record completeness at 30-day intervals | Ongoing |
| 6.6 | DON / Designee | Quarterly record content audit (10% sample) | Quarterly |
| 6.7 | Medical Records | Close and archive record within 30 days of discharge | Within 30 days of discharge |

| 42 CFR § 484.110 | Clinical record content, maintenance, and retention | CL-CD-002 |

## CL-CD-003 — Clinical Record Authentication & Signature Requirements
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Policy ID | CL-CD-003 |
| Policy Title | Clinical Record Authentication & Signature Requirements |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CD — Clinical Documentation |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 6.0 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes requirements for the authentication, co-signature, and countersignature of all entries in the patient clinical record at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Authentication requirements ensure that all clinical documentation is traceable to a specific, identifiable, and authorized author, thereby protecting patient safety, legal accountability, and Medicare reimbursement. Unauthenticated clinical entries are not legally valid, may not support claims adjudication, and constitute a survey-level deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.110(b).

### 3. Scope
All employees and contractors who create or co-sign entries in patient clinical records, including all clinical disciplines, supervising clinicians, and agency administrators who countersign documentation.

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Every entry in a patient clinical record — including visit notes, assessments, care plan updates, physician orders, verbal order transcriptions, education notes, and supervisory notes — shall be authenticated (signed and dated) by the author at the time the entry is completed.

4.2 Authentication shall include: (a) the author's full name; (b) professional credentials/licensure (e.g., RN, LVN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA); (c) date and time of the entry; (d) handwritten signature (for paper records) or electronic signature with audit trail (for EHR).

4.3 Electronic signatures shall be unique to each individual user, not shared, and shall be protected by secure password per IT-AS-001. Electronic signatures carry the same legal weight as handwritten signatures.

4.4 Home Health Aide (HHA) visit notes shall be cosigned by the supervising Registered Nurse within 14 days of the visit, per 42 CFR § 484.80(d).

4.5 Verbal orders transcribed by a licensed nurse or therapist shall include: (a) the transcriber's name and credentials; (b) the prescribing physician's name; (c) date and time of the verbal order; (d) statement "V.O. received per telephone from Dr. [Name]." Verbal orders shall be authenticated by the ordering physician within 30 days per CL-OA-003.

4.6 Late entries shall be labeled as "Late Entry" with the current date and time. No entry shall be backdated.

4.7 Corrections to signed entries shall comply with CL-CD-002 § 4.4. Obliteration, use of correction fluid, or erasure of any signed entry is prohibited.

4.8 Students and volunteers shall not authenticate clinical documentation. All documentation by students shall be reviewed and countersigned by a licensed supervising clinician.

4.9 The Director of Nursing shall audit authentication compliance as part of the quarterly record review per QA-PG-001, reporting results to the QAPI committee.

### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | The process of confirming the authorship of a clinical record entry by means of a dated signature (handwritten or electronic). |
| Countersignature | A second signature by a supervising clinician that acknowledges review of documentation authored by another staff member. |
| Verbal Order | A physician order communicated orally (in person or by telephone) and transcribed by an authorized clinical staff member. |

### 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | All Clinicians | Sign and date all entries at time of completion | Immediately upon entry |
| 6.2 | HHA | Complete HHA activity notes for every visit | Within 24 hours |
| 6.3 | Supervising RN | Countersign HHA visit notes | Within 14 days of visit |
| 6.4 | Transcribing Clinician | Document and sign verbal orders per protocol | At time of order receipt |
| 6.5 | Physician Liaison | Route verbal orders to physician for co-signature | Within 5 business days |
| 6.6 | DON / Medical Records | Audit authentication compliance | Quarterly |

### 7. Compliance & Regulatory References

| Regulation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| 42 CFR § 484.110(b) | Record authentication requirements |
| 42 CFR § 484.80(d) | HHA documentation cosignature by supervising RN |
| Title 22 CCR § 74751 | California signature requirements |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory timeframes for completion and locking of clinical documentation at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Timely documentation ensures continuity of care between providers, supports accurate and timely claims submission, facilitates agency quality assurance, and demonstrates compliance with 42 CFR § 484.110(c) and CMS operational standards. Late or unlocked documentation creates both clinical risk (gaps in care coordination) and billing risk (rejected claims).

### 3. Scope
All clinicians and clinical staff documenting patient care, including RNs, LVNs, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, and HHA. Also applies to supervisory and administrative staff with documentation responsibilities.

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All visit notes shall be completed and authenticated in the agency's EHR system within 24 hours of the patient visit. This includes skilled nursing notes, therapy notes, social work notes, and HHA activity notes.

4.2 OASIS assessments shall be completed within the following timeframes:
(a) Start of Care (SOC): within 5 calendar days of the SOC visit;
(b) Resumption of Care (ROC): within 2 calendar days of the ROC visit;
(c) Recertification (RECERT): at the RECERT assessment visit, prior to end of certification period;
(d) Transfer to Inpatient Facility: within 2 calendar days of transfer;
(e) Discharge: on the date of discharge or within 2 calendar days.

4.3 Care plan updates and physician order changes shall be documented and authenticated within 24 hours of the clinical decision or verbal order receipt.

4.4 Discharge summaries shall be completed within 5 business days of patient discharge from care.

4.5 Once a visit note is completed and authenticated, it shall be locked in the EHR system per the agency's IT policy (IT-DM-003). Locked records may not be edited; corrections shall be made via addendum with date, time, author, and reason for correction.

4.6 Supervisors shall review documentation compliance weekly. Clinicians with chronic late documentation (>20% of visits late in any 30-day period) shall receive progressive counseling per HR-ER-003.

4.7 Claims shall not be submitted for any episode or visit that has not been documented, authenticated, and locked in the EHR system per CL-OA-006.

4.8 The Director of Nursing shall report documentation timeliness metrics to the QAPI committee monthly and to the Governing Body quarterly.

### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Document Lock | A system function that prevents further editing of a finalized and authenticated clinical record entry. |
| Late Documentation | Any clinical record entry not completed and authenticated within the timeframe specified in this policy. |
| Addendum | A supplemental entry added to a locked clinical record to provide additional information, corrections, or clarification, without altering the original entry. |

### 6. Documentation Timeliness Standards

| Document Type | Completion Deadline | Lock Deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skilled Visit Note (RN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW) | 24 hours post-visit | 48 hours post-visit |
| HHA Activity Note | 24 hours post-visit | 48 hours post-visit |
| OASIS — SOC | 5 calendar days | 7 calendar days |
| OASIS — ROC | 2 calendar days | 3 calendar days |
| OASIS — Discharge | Day of discharge + 2 days | +3 days |
| Care Plan Update | 24 hours | 48 hours |
| Verbal Order Transcription | At time of receipt | Same day |
| Discharge Summary | 5 business days | 7 business days |

| 42 CFR § 484.110(c) | Timely clinical record completion |
| 42 CFR § 484.55 | OASIS assessment timeframe requirements |

## CL-PR-001 — Patient Rights & Responsibilities
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-PR-001 |
| Policy Title | Patient Rights & Responsibilities |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | PR — Patient Rights & Clinical Procedures |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Administrator |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes and protects the rights of every patient receiving home health services from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and defines the corresponding responsibilities of patients and their designated representatives. Patient rights are not aspirational — they are legally enforceable entitlements under 42 CFR § 484.50 (Condition of Participation: Patient Rights), the California Home Health Agency Licensing Law (Health & Safety Code §§ 1726–1727), and the Patient Self-Determination Act (42 U.S.C. § 1395cc(f)). Failure to provide, document, and honor patient rights constitutes a Condition-level deficiency that may result in immediate jeopardy findings, civil monetary penalties, and program termination.

### 3. Scope
This policy applies to all patients and their designated representatives, all clinical and administrative staff, all contracted providers, and anyone acting on behalf of the agency in patient interactions.

### 4. Patient Rights
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide every patient, at or before the initiation of care, with a written notice of the following rights, in a language and manner the patient understands:

4.1.1 Right to be informed of rights: Every patient has the right to receive written notice of their rights and to have those rights explained verbally in understandable terms before care begins.

4.1.2 Right to exercise rights: Every patient has the right to exercise their rights as a patient of the agency and as a citizen of the United States without interference, coercion, discrimination, or reprisal.

4.1.3 Right to be informed of charges: Patients have the right to be informed of the services covered under their specific payer source, any limitations on coverage, and any services for which they will be personally responsible for payment, in advance of receiving those services.

4.1.4 Right to participate in care planning: Patients have the right to participate in the development and revision of their plan of care. This includes the right to request changes to the care plan, refuse specific treatments, and have their preferences documented.

4.1.5 Right to refuse care: Patients have the right to refuse all or any part of their care plan. When a patient refuses care, the clinician shall document the refusal, the information provided to the patient about the potential consequences of refusal, and the patient's decision per CL-CD-001.

4.1.6 Right to confidentiality: Patients have the right to have their clinical records and personal information kept confidential per HIPAA (CO-HP-001) and California law.

4.1.7 Right to access records: Patients have the right to access their clinical records per CO-HP-002 and 45 CFR § 164.524.

4.1.8 Right to be treated with dignity and respect: Patients have the right to be treated courteously, fairly, and without discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by federal or California law.

4.1.9 Right to voice grievances: Patients have the right to voice grievances about care or services without fear of discrimination or reprisal. Grievances shall be investigated and resolved per OP-PA-001.

4.1.10 Right to be informed of investigation outcomes: Patients have the right to be informed of the outcome of any investigation of a grievance filed per OP-PA-001.

4.1.11 Right to advance directives: Patients have the right to formulate an advance directive and to have the agency honor the directive to the extent permitted by law per CL-PR-002.

4.1.12 Right to be free from abuse and neglect: Patients have the right to be free from verbal, mental, sexual, and physical abuse, neglect, and exploitation by agency personnel, per HR-ER-009 and California Welfare and Institutions Code.

4.1.13 Right to have property respected: Patients have the right to have their property treated with respect. Agency staff shall not use patient property, borrow money, or accept gifts of more than nominal value from patients.

4.1.14 Right to know staff identity: Patients have the right to know the name and function of any person providing care to them, and to know the identity of the agency supervising their care.

4.2 The agency shall maintain documentation that the Patient Rights and Responsibilities notice was provided, explained, and acknowledged by the patient or representative at admission. A signed copy shall be filed in the patient clinical record per CL-CD-002.

4.3 If a patient lacks decision-making capacity, the rights specified in this policy extend to the patient's legally authorized representative (legal guardian, healthcare agent, or next of kin per California law).

### 5. Patient Responsibilities
5.1 Patients are expected to: (a) provide accurate and complete health information; (b) follow the agreed-upon plan of care to the best of their ability and notify the agency when they cannot; (c) treat agency staff with courtesy and respect; (d) keep scheduled appointments or notify the agency in advance of cancellations; (e) notify the agency of changes in their condition, payer status, or living situation; (f) inform the agency of any other healthcare services they are receiving; (g) accept responsibility for refusing care or for failing to follow their care plan.

### 6. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1 | Admitting Clinician | Provide written Patient Rights notice to patient/representative | At or before SOC |
| 6.2 | Admitting Clinician | Review rights verbally with patient/representative | At SOC visit |
| 6.3 | Patient/Representative | Sign acknowledgment of receipt | At SOC visit |
| 6.4 | Admitting Clinician | File signed acknowledgment in EHR clinical record | Same day as SOC |
| 6.5 | Administrator / DON | Investigate any reported rights violations | Within 72 hours of report |
| 6.6 | Administrator | Notify patient of investigation outcome | Within 30 days per OP-PA-001 |

### 7. Compliance & Regulatory References

| Regulation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| 42 CFR § 484.50 | Home Health CoP: Patient Rights |
| California HSC §§ 1726–1727 | California Home Health Patient Rights |
| Patient Self-Determination Act (1990) | Advance Directive rights |
| 42 U.S.C. § 1395cc(f) | Medicare provider patient rights obligations |

## CL-PR-002 — Advance Directive Compliance
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-PR-002 |
| Policy Title | Advance Directive Compliance |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | PR — Patient Rights & Clinical Procedures |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Administrator / Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes requirements for identifying, documenting, honoring, and maintaining advance directives for all patients receiving home health services from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Compliance with the Patient Self-Determination Act (PSDA, 42 U.S.C. § 1395cc(f)) is a condition of participation in the Medicare and Medicaid programs. Every Medicare-participating home health agency must: (a) provide written information to patients about their rights under state law to make decisions about medical care including the right to accept or refuse treatment; (b) maintain written policies and procedures regarding advance directives; (c) document in the patient's record whether the patient has an advance directive; and (d) not discriminate against individuals based on whether they have an advance directive.

### 3. Scope
All patients admitted to home health services and all clinical and administrative staff involved in patient intake, admission, and ongoing care.

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 At or before the initiation of home health services, Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide every adult patient (or the patient's authorized representative) with written information about the patient's rights under California law to make decisions about medical care, including the right to execute an Advance Directive.

4.2 The admitting clinician shall ask every patient at admission whether they have an existing Advance Directive. The patient's answer shall be documented in the clinical record per CL-CD-002. If the patient has an Advance Directive, a copy shall be requested for the clinical record.

4.3 If the patient has an Advance Directive, the agency shall: (a) place a copy or summary of the directive in the patient's clinical record; (b) flag the directive for visibility to all treating clinicians; (c) honor the directive to the extent permitted by law and consistent with the patient's wishes; (d) communicate the existence and content of the directive to treating clinicians and, as appropriate, to emergency services.

4.4 The agency shall NOT condition the provision of care, discriminate, or create barriers based on whether a patient has or does not have an Advance Directive.

4.5 If the agency's professional or religious convictions create a conflict with honoring a specific provision of an Advance Directive, the agency shall promptly notify the patient and, if necessary, assist in transferring the patient to another care provider that can honor the directive.

4.6 If a patient wishes to create, modify, or revoke an Advance Directive and requests assistance, the agency shall provide the patient with general information about California Advance Directives and refer the patient to appropriate resources (primary care provider, social worker, or a California Probate Code attorney). Agency staff shall not participate in drafting a patient's legal documents.

4.7 Types of Advance Directives recognized under California law and relevant to home health include:
(a) Healthcare Power of Attorney / AHCD (Prob. Code § 4600 et seq.);
(b) POLST (Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment) — a physician order, not just a directive;
(c) Natural Death Act Declaration (Living Will);
(d) Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) Order, if signed by a physician.

4.8 Home Health Aides and non-licensed staff shall NOT make clinical decisions regarding Advance Directives. Any question about a patient's wishes or an AD's applicability shall be escalated to the supervising RN immediately.

4.9 The agency shall provide annual staff education on Advance Directive requirements and patient rights per HR-TD-001.

### 5. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1 | Admitting Clinician | Provide written Advance Directive information to patient | At or before SOC |
| 5.2 | Admitting Clinician | Inquire about existing Advance Directive; document answer | At SOC |
| 5.3 | Admitting Clinician | Request copy of AD if patient has one; file in record | At SOC |
| 5.4 | DON | Ensure AD is flagged in EHR for all treating clinicians | Within 24 hours of SOC |
| 5.5 | All Clinicians | Review AD at each visit if patient condition changes | Ongoing |
| 5.6 | Clinician | Escalate any AD conflict or uncertainty to DON/Administrator | Immediately |

### 6. Compliance & Regulatory References

| Regulation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| 42 U.S.C. § 1395cc(f) | Patient Self-Determination Act |
| 42 CFR § 484.50(d) | Home Health CoP: Patient Rights — Advance Directives |
| California Probate Code § 4600 et seq. | Advance Healthcare Directive |
| California Health & Safety Code § 443 et seq. | End of Life Option Act |

## CL-PR-003 — Informed Consent
### 1. Policy Header

| Subdomain | PR — Patient Rights & Clinical Procedures |

| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for obtaining, documenting, and maintaining valid informed consent from patients or their authorized representatives prior to initiating home health services and prior to specific procedures or treatments. Informed consent is a fundamental legal and ethical obligation grounded in the patient's right to self-determination (California Health & Safety Code § 1599.80) and the agency's duty to ensure patients understand the care being proposed before agreeing to receive it. Lack of proper informed consent exposes the agency to legal liability and constitutes a violation of patient rights under 42 CFR § 484.50.

### 3. Scope
All patients, their authorized representatives, and all clinical and administrative staff involved in obtaining and documenting consent.

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall obtain written, informed consent from every patient or authorized representative prior to initiating home health services. Consent shall be documented on the agency's standard Consent for Home Health Services form.

4.2 Informed consent requires that the patient be provided with: (a) a description of the proposed services, including disciplines involved, visit frequency, and anticipated duration; (b) the potential benefits of the services; (c) potential risks or burdens, if applicable; (d) available alternatives to the proposed services; (e) the consequences of refusing services; (f) the right to withdraw consent at any time without affecting other rights or access to care.

4.3 Consent shall be obtained in a language and manner the patient understands. If the patient requires language interpretation, a qualified interpreter (not a family member unless in emergency) shall be provided per CO-HP-003.

4.4 Consent shall be obtained by an authorized staff member (RN, Administrator, or trained intake coordinator). Home Health Aides shall not obtain informed consent.

4.5 For patients who lack decision-making capacity, consent shall be obtained from: (a) the legal guardian; (b) the agent named in a healthcare power of attorney (AHCD); (c) next of kin per California Probate Code § 4711, in the order specified by law.

4.6 Verbal consent in urgent or emergency situations is permitted provided it is: (a) witnessed by a second staff member; (b) documented immediately with the witness's name; (c) followed up with written consent at the earliest opportunity.

4.7 Consent shall be obtained separately for: (a) general home health services (signed at admission); (b) HIV/AIDS testing, if applicable (California HSC § 120990); (c) recording of communications, if applicable.

4.8 Consent forms shall be retained in the patient clinical record per CO-HP-007 and CL-CD-002.

### 5. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1 | Admitting Clinician / Intake | Present consent form and explain in patient's language | At SOC or intake |
| 5.2 | Clinician | Allow patient time to ask questions; answer questions honestly | Before signing |
| 5.3 | Patient / Representative | Sign consent form | At SOC |
| 5.4 | Clinician | File signed consent in EHR record | Same day |
| 5.5 | DON | Audit consent completion as part of quarterly record review | Quarterly |

### 6. Compliance & Regulatory References

| Regulation | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| 42 CFR § 484.50 | Patient Rights — right to participate in care decisions |
| California HSC § 1599.80 | Informed consent requirements |
| California Probate Code § 4711 | Surrogate decision-making hierarchy |

### 7. Cross-Referenced Policies
CL-PR-001, CL-PR-002, CL-CD-002, CO-HP-001, CO-HP-003, CO-HP-007.
