# FN-CM-005 — LUPA Prevention & Monitoring
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | FN-CM-005 |
| Title | LUPA Prevention & Monitoring |
| Domain | FN — Finance & Revenue Cycle |
| Subdomain | CM — Coding & Classification |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Policy Owner/Steward | CFO / Revenue Cycle Director |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Alignment | 42 CFR § 484.205, 42 CFR § 484.60, CMS IOM Pub. 100-04 Ch. 10, CMS PDGM Final Rules |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the agency's program for monitoring visit utilization within each 30-day payment period to identify episodes at risk of Low Utilization Payment Adjustment (LUPA) and to ensure that all physician-ordered visits are delivered in accordance with the Plan of Care. Under PDGM, when the number of visits in a 30-day period falls below the CMS-established LUPA threshold for the assigned payment group, the agency receives a significantly reduced per-visit payment instead of the full PDGM case-mix adjusted payment. LUPA episodes typically reimburse at approximately 15–30% of the full payment amount, resulting in substantial revenue loss. While the agency must never add visits solely to avoid LUPA (which would constitute fraud), the agency has a clinical and operational obligation to ensure that all physician-ordered visits are actually delivered as ordered. This policy integrates clinical visit compliance (CL-SD-025), scheduling operations (OP-SL-001), and revenue cycle monitoring (FN-FP-003) into a unified LUPA prevention program managed through QAPI (QA-PI-006).
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
CFO / Revenue Cycle Director
Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All clinical scheduling coordinators
All billing coordinators
QAPI Coordinator
Compliance Officer
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall monitor visit utilization for every open 30-day payment period against the applicable PDGM LUPA threshold.
4.2 The LUPA threshold for each 30-day period is determined by the PDGM payment group assigned to that period. The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain the current CMS LUPA threshold table and update it annually when CMS publishes updated thresholds.
4.3 Episodes identified as at risk of LUPA (projected visits below threshold) shall be reviewed by the Director of Nursing within 48 hours to determine: (a) whether all physician-ordered visits have been scheduled and delivered; (b) whether any missed, cancelled, or rescheduled visits have reduced the count below threshold; (c) whether the patient's clinical condition supports the ordered visit frequency.
4.4 The agency shall NEVER add visits that are not clinically necessary or not physician-ordered solely to exceed the LUPA threshold. Adding visits solely for payment purposes constitutes fraud. Any LUPA prevention intervention must be grounded in the physician-ordered Plan of Care and clinical need.
4.5 Legitimate LUPA prevention actions include: (a) ensuring all physician-ordered visits are scheduled and delivered; (b) resolving scheduling barriers (patient cancellations, staff availability); (c) communicating with the physician regarding appropriate visit frequency; (d) identifying missed visits and rescheduling per CL-SD-024.
4.6 LUPA rate shall be monitored as a Key Performance Indicator (KPI) and reported monthly to the CFO, quarterly to the QAPI Committee, and quarterly to the Governing Body.
4.7 A LUPA rate exceeding 10% of total 30-day periods in any calendar month shall trigger a root cause analysis per QA-AE-002.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| LUPA | Low Utilization Payment Adjustment — a payment reduction applied by CMS when the total number of visits in a 30-day payment period falls below the PDGM LUPA threshold for the assigned payment group. The agency receives a per-visit payment instead of the full PDGM case-mix adjusted payment. |
| LUPA Threshold | The minimum number of visits (by all disciplines combined) required in a 30-day period to receive the full PDGM payment. Thresholds vary by payment group and are published annually by CMS. Typically range from 2 to 6 visits. |
| At-Risk Episode | A 30-day period where projected or actual visit count is at or below the LUPA threshold with calendar days remaining in the period. |
| Visit Count | The total number of billable visits by all disciplines (SN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA) within a 30-day payment period. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 LUPA Threshold Monitoring

| Step | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain the current CMS LUPA threshold table within the billing system, updated annually upon CMS publication. | Revenue Cycle Director | Annually (by January 1) |
| 6.1.2 | For every open 30-day payment period, the billing system (or manual tracking) shall compare actual visit count against the LUPA threshold at the midpoint (day 15) and at day 25 of each 30-day period. | Revenue Cycle Director / Billing Coordinator | Day 15 and Day 25 |
| 6.1.3 | Any 30-day period where the visit count at day 15 is below 50% of the LUPA threshold shall be flagged as "LUPA Watch." | Revenue Cycle Director | Day 15 |
| 6.1.4 | Any 30-day period where the visit count at day 25 is at or below the LUPA threshold shall be flagged as "LUPA Alert." | Revenue Cycle Director | Day 25 |
| 6.1.5 | LUPA Watch and LUPA Alert flags shall be communicated to the Director of Nursing within 24 hours of identification. | Revenue Cycle Director | Within 24 hours |

### 6.2 Clinical Review of At-Risk Episodes

| Step | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Upon receipt of a LUPA Watch or Alert, the Director of Nursing shall review the episode within 48 hours. The review shall determine: (a) total visits ordered on the Plan of Care for this 30-day period; (b) total visits actually delivered; (c) reason for any shortfall (missed visits, cancellations, scheduling gaps, patient refusal, hospitalization); (d) whether clinical need supports the ordered frequency; (e) whether any visits can be legitimately rescheduled within the remaining days. | Director of Nursing | Within 48 hours |
| 6.2.2 | If visits were missed due to scheduling error, staff availability, or patient cancellation (not patient refusal or clinical reason): (a) reschedule missed visits within the remaining days of the 30-day period if clinically appropriate and consistent with the Plan of Care; (b) document the rescheduling and the clinical rationale per CL-SD-024 and CL-SD-025. | Director of Nursing / Scheduling Coordinator | Immediately |
| 6.2.3 | If the visit shortfall is due to the physician ordering fewer visits than the LUPA threshold and clinical need supports additional visits: the DON may contact the physician to discuss whether the visit frequency should be adjusted. Any change must be physician-ordered and documented. | Director of Nursing | Within 48 hours |
| 6.2.4 | If the visit count is below LUPA threshold due to legitimate clinical reasons (patient improved rapidly, patient refused visits, patient hospitalized during the period): document the clinical rationale, accept the LUPA payment, and close the review. No visits shall be added. | Director of Nursing | Document immediately |
| 6.2.5 | Document the LUPA review decision on the LUPA Review Worksheet (Appendix A). | Director of Nursing | Same day as decision |

### 6.3 Monthly LUPA Rate Monitoring

| Step | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | The Revenue Cycle Director shall calculate the monthly LUPA rate: (LUPA 30-day periods ÷ total 30-day periods billed) × 100. | Revenue Cycle Director | Monthly — by 15th of following month |
| 6.3.2 | Report LUPA rate to CFO monthly and include in the revenue cycle performance dashboard per FN-FP-003. | Revenue Cycle Director | Monthly |
| 6.3.3 | Report LUPA rate to QAPI Committee quarterly per QA-PI-006. | QAPI Coordinator | Quarterly |
| 6.3.4 | Report LUPA rate to Governing Body quarterly in the financial report per GV-GB-001 §6.2.5. | CFO | Quarterly |
| 6.3.5 | If LUPA rate exceeds 10% for any calendar month, initiate root cause analysis per QA-AE-002 within 30 calendar days. | Revenue Cycle Director + Compliance Officer | Within 30 calendar days |

### 6.4 Escalation Matrix

| Condition | Escalation Path | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Episode at LUPA Watch (day 15) | DON review within 48 hours | Day 15 |
| Episode at LUPA Alert (day 25) | DON urgent review and action | Day 25 — immediate |
| Monthly LUPA rate >10% | CFO and Compliance Officer; RCA per QA-AE-002 | Within 30 calendar days |
| Monthly LUPA rate >15% | Administrator and Governing Body notified | Within 5 business days |
| Pattern of visits added without clinical basis | Compliance Officer investigation per CO-CP-007 | Within 24 hours |
| Scheduling barriers causing chronic LUPA | Operations Director; staffing and scheduling review | Within 14 calendar days |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LUPA threshold table | Current CMS LUPA thresholds | Revenue Cycle Director | Billing system | Current year + 7 years |
| LUPA review | LUPA Review Worksheet (Appendix A) | Director of Nursing | Clinical/billing file | 7 years |
| Monthly LUPA rate | Revenue cycle dashboard per FN-FP-003 | Revenue Cycle Director | Financial records | 7 years |
| RCA (if triggered) | RCA report per QA-AE-002 | Compliance Officer | QAPI/compliance file | 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgments | Signed Appendix B | Revenue Cycle Director | Policy acknowledgment file | 7 years |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LUPA rate | Monthly calculation | ≤ 10% |
| LUPA Watch/Alert reviewed by DON within 48 hours | Appendix A timestamp | 100% |
| Zero visits added solely for LUPA avoidance | Compliance audit/investigation | Zero findings |
| Monthly LUPA reporting completed | Dashboard report | 100% |
| RCA triggered for LUPA rate >10__ | RCA documentation | 100% |

42 CFR § 484.205, 42 CFR § 484.60, CMS PDGM Final Rules, CMS IOM Pub. 100-04 Ch. 10.

## 1. Policy Header

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for negotiating, executing, monitoring, and managing contracts with Medicare Advantage plans, Medi-Cal managed care plans, and commercial insurance payers for home health services provided by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Payer contracts define reimbursement rates, authorization requirements, billing procedures, and performance expectations that directly affect agency revenue and operations. Effective contract management ensures the agency: (a) maintains financially viable reimbursement rates; (b) complies with all contractual obligations; (c) tracks and enforces payer payment obligations; (d) evaluates contract performance annually; (e) makes informed decisions about contract renewals, renegotiations, and terminations.
## 3. Scope
CFO / Revenue Cycle Director, Administrator, Compliance Officer, Director of Nursing (clinical requirements), billing coordinators, legal counsel (as needed).
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All payer contracts shall be reviewed and approved by the CFO before execution. Contracts with annualized revenue impact exceeding $50,000 shall also be approved by the Administrator. Contracts exceeding $250,000 shall be reported to the Governing Body.
4.2 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain a centralized Payer Contract Registry (Appendix A) documenting all active contracts with key terms, rates, expiration dates, and renewal deadlines.
4.3 Each payer contract shall be reviewed for financial performance annually, including: reimbursement adequacy (comparison to Medicare FFS rates and cost of care delivery), payment timeliness, denial rates, and administrative burden.
4.4 Contract renewal decisions shall be based on documented financial analysis. No contract shall be auto-renewed without annual performance review.
4.5 The agency shall not accept reimbursement rates below the cost of service delivery without documented business justification approved by the CFO and Administrator.
4.6 All contracts shall be reviewed by the Compliance Officer for regulatory compliance and by legal counsel for contracts exceeding $100,000 or containing unusual terms.
## 5–11. Procedures, Documentation, Compliance, References, Training, Version Control
(Full procedures covering: contract negotiation, execution, registry maintenance, annual performance review, renewal/termination decisions, rate analysis methodology, escalation matrix. Documentation: Appendix A — Contract Registry; Appendix B — Annual Contract Performance Review; Appendix C — Contract Negotiation Checklist; Appendix D — Policy Acknowledgment. Compliance monitoring: 100% contracts in registry, annual reviews completed, no auto-renewals without review. References: 42 CFR § 484.100, state insurance law, cross-referenced FN-BC-007, FN-FP-003, GV-EA-001, CO-HP-005, GV-GB-001, EN-TG-001. Training and version control per standard format.)

## 2–4. Purpose, Scope, Policy Statements
Establishes standards for accurate charge capture for all services and maintenance of the agency fee schedule. Ensures: (a) all billable services are captured with correct charge codes, amounts, and dates; (b) the agency fee schedule is reviewed and updated annually; (c) charges are reconciled against services delivered; (d) charge capture errors are identified and corrected. Applies to all billing coordinators, Revenue Cycle Director, CFO, clinical scheduling coordinators.
## 5–11. Full Policy Content
(Procedures covering: charge capture workflow from visit delivery through billing; fee schedule annual update process aligned with CMS rate changes; charge reconciliation against visit logs; charge correction process; charge capture audit quarterly. ## 1. Policy Header

| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
Establishes a comprehensive revenue cycle performance monitoring program with defined KPIs, monitoring frequency, dashboard reporting, and escalation thresholds. Revenue cycle performance is a critical indicator of agency financial health and billing compliance.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain a Revenue Cycle Performance Dashboard (Appendix A) tracking the following KPIs monthly:

| KPI | Target | Escalation Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Days in A/R (average) | ≤ 45 days | > 60 days |
| Clean Claim Rate | ≥ 95% | < 90% |
| Denial Rate | ≤ 5% | > 7% |
| LUPA Rate | ≤ 10% | > 15% |
| NOA Timeliness (≤5 days) | 100% | < 95% |
| Claims Submission Timeliness (≤14 days from period end) | ≥ 95% | < 90% |
| Payment Variance Rate | < 3% | > 5% |
| Cash Collection Rate | ≥ 95% of expected | < 90% |
| Timely Filing Violations | Zero | Any |
| Overpayments Identified/Returned in 60 Days | 100% | Any violation |

4.2 Dashboard reviewed by CFO monthly, presented to Administrator monthly, reported to Governing Body quarterly.
4.3 Any KPI exceeding escalation threshold for 2 consecutive months triggers formal RCA per QA-AE-002.
## 6. Procedures
Monthly dashboard production by 20th of following month. CFO review within 5 business days. Quarterly integration with QAPI per QA-PI-002. Governing Body reporting per GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.

## 2–11. Full Policy Content
Establishes criteria for classifying and managing bad debt write-offs and charity care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. ## 2. Purpose
Mandates annual budget development, Governing Body approval, and ongoing variance monitoring per 42 CFR § 484.105 (Governing Body financial oversight) and GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The CFO shall prepare an annual operating budget for the upcoming fiscal year no later than 60 calendar days before fiscal year start.
4.2 The budget shall include: projected revenue by payer, projected expenses by category, capital expenditure plan, staffing plan with costs, and projected net operating margin.
4.3 The Governing Body shall review and approve the budget no later than 30 calendar days before fiscal year start per GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.1.
4.4 Monthly variance monitoring: the CFO shall compare actual results to budget monthly and report variances to the Administrator. Variance >10% from budget in any major category triggers corrective action.
4.5 Quarterly budget-to-actual reports presented to Governing Body per GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.2.
Appendices: A — Annual Budget Template; B — Monthly Variance Report; C — Policy Acknowledgment.

# FN-FP-007 — Financial Compliance & Fraud Monitoring Controls
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | FN-FP-007 |
| Title | Financial Compliance & Fraud Monitoring Controls |
| Domain | FN — Finance & Revenue Cycle |
| Subdomain | FP — Financial Planning & Performance |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Policy Owner/Steward | CFO / Revenue Cycle Director |
| Access Tier | Tier 3 — Confidential |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Alignment | 42 CFR § 484.100, 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b (AKS), 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d), OIG Compliance Program Guidance |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the agency's financial monitoring controls for detecting, preventing, and reporting billing anomalies, fraudulent patterns, and aberrant financial activity. Effective financial fraud monitoring is a core requirement of the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies, which mandates that agencies implement internal controls to detect billing irregularities. This policy integrates billing pattern analysis, outlier detection, internal financial audits, and escalation procedures to ensure the agency identifies potential fraud, waste, and abuse at the earliest possible stage.
## 3. Scope
CFO / Revenue Cycle Director, Compliance Officer, Administrator, billing coordinators, certified coders, QAPI Coordinator.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The agency shall maintain a financial fraud monitoring program that includes: (a) monthly billing pattern analysis; (b) outlier detection for utilization, coding, and payment patterns; (c) quarterly internal financial audits; (d) integration with the corporate compliance program (CO-CP-001) and FWA prevention program (CO-FA-003).
4.2 The Revenue Cycle Director and Compliance Officer shall jointly conduct monthly billing pattern analysis comparing agency metrics against national and state benchmarks.
4.3 The following billing patterns shall be monitored as potential fraud/abuse indicators:

| Indicator | Monitoring Metric | Trigger Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Average visits per episode | Agency avg vs. national avg | >20% above national average |
| PDGM case-mix weight | Agency avg vs. national avg | >15% above national average |
| LUPA rate | Agency rate vs. national avg | Significantly below national average (may indicate visit padding) |
| Therapy utilization | % episodes with therapy | >20% above national average |
| Diagnosis coding concentration | Top 10 diagnoses % of total | Unusual concentration in high-paying clinical groups |
| Admission source distribution | Institutional vs. community % | Significant deviation from regional norms |
| Referral source concentration | % from single referral source | >40% from any single source (AKS indicator) |
| Episode length | Avg days on service | >20% above national average |
| Clinician productivity | Visits per clinician per day | >8 visits/day (productivity may affect quality) |
| Staff-to-patient ratio | Clinician caseload | Unusual ratios |

4.4 Quarterly internal financial audits shall include: (a) sample of claims tested for documentation support; (b) referral relationship financial analysis (AKS screening per CO-FA-001); (c) clinician productivity analysis; (d) cost report accuracy review.
4.5 Any billing pattern or financial anomaly that may indicate fraud, abuse, or systematic improper billing shall be reported to the Compliance Officer within 24 hours for investigation per CO-CP-007.
4.6 Financial monitoring results shall be reported to the CFO monthly, the Compliance Officer monthly, and the Governing Body quarterly.
## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Monthly Billing Pattern Analysis

| Step | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | The Revenue Cycle Director shall produce the Monthly Financial Monitoring Report (Appendix A) comparing agency billing patterns against CMS benchmarks and prior periods. | Revenue Cycle Director | Monthly — by 20th of following month |
| 6.1.2 | The Compliance Officer shall review the report for patterns indicating potential FWA. | Compliance Officer | Within 5 business days |
| 6.1.3 | Any indicator exceeding its trigger threshold shall be flagged for investigation. The investigation shall determine whether the pattern reflects: (a) legitimate clinical/operational factors; (b) data/system error; (c) potential inappropriate billing or fraud. | Revenue Cycle Director + Compliance Officer | Within 14 calendar days of identification |
| 6.1.4 | Investigation findings shall be documented. If the pattern cannot be explained by legitimate factors, escalate per §6.3. | Compliance Officer | Upon investigation completion |

### 6.2 Quarterly Internal Financial Audit

| Step | Action | Responsible Party | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Select audit sample: minimum 5% of claims billed in the quarter (minimum 15 claims). | Compliance Officer | Quarterly |
| 6.2.2 | For each sampled claim: (a) verify all services billed were actually rendered; (b) verify documentation supports all billed services; (c) verify coding accuracy per FN-CM-001/002; (d) verify PDGM classification accuracy; (e) verify physician certification on file; (f) verify no duplicate billing. | Audit Lead | During audit |
| 6.2.3 | Analyze referral source financial data for AKS risk per CO-FA-001: (a) identify all referral sources; (b) review any financial arrangements with referral sources; (c) flag any referral source accounting for >40% of admissions. | Compliance Officer | During audit |
| 6.2.4 | Document findings in the Quarterly Financial Audit Report (Appendix B). | Audit Lead | Within 30 calendar days of quarter end |
| 6.2.5 | Report results to CFO, Compliance Officer, and Governing Body. | Compliance Officer | Quarterly |

### 6.3 Escalation Matrix

| Condition | Escalation Path | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billing pattern exceeds trigger threshold | Revenue Cycle Director and Compliance Officer investigate | Within 14 calendar days |
| Pattern cannot be explained by legitimate factors | Compliance Officer initiates investigation per CO-CP-007 | Within 7 calendar days |
| Potential fraud identified | Compliance Officer, Administrator, CFO, legal counsel | Within 24 hours |
| Referral relationship with financial arrangement flagged | Compliance Officer and legal counsel review per CO-FA-001 | Within 30 calendar days |
| Financial audit reveals claim not supported by documentation | Compliance Officer evaluates for overpayment per FN-BC-004 | Within 24 hours |
| Governing Body requires briefing | CFO presents at next quarterly meeting or special meeting | Per GV-GB-001 |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly analysis | Monthly Financial Monitoring Report (Appendix A) | Revenue Cycle Director | Financial/compliance records | 7 years |
| Quarterly audit | Quarterly Financial Audit Report (Appendix B) | Compliance Officer | Compliance/financial records | 7 years |
| Investigation files | Investigation documentation per CO-CP-007 | Compliance Officer | Compliance file (may be privileged) | 10 years |
| Policy acknowledgments | Signed Appendix C | Revenue Cycle Director | Policy acknowledgment file | 7 years |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly financial monitoring report completed | Report on file | 100% (12 per year) |
| Quarterly financial audit completed | Report on file | 100% (4 per year) |
| All flagged patterns investigated within 14 days | Investigation log | 100% |
| Potential fraud escalated within 24 hours | Investigation timeline | 100% |
| Financial monitoring results reported to Governing Body quarterly | GB minutes | 100% |
| Zero undetected systematic billing anomalies | Audit and monitoring outcomes | Zero |

## 9. References
42 CFR § 484.100, 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733 (FCA), 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b (AKS), OIG Compliance Program Guidance.
Cross-referenced: FN-BC-001–007, FN-CM-001–005, FN-FP-001–006, CO-CP-001, CO-CP-007, CO-FA-001, CO-FA-002, CO-FA-003, FN-BC-004, QA-PI-002, GV-GB-001, EN-TG-001.
## 10–11. Training and Version Control
Per standard format. Annual training on financial monitoring, FWA indicators, reporting obligations. Appendix C acknowledgment. EN-LC-001 version control.

| Regulatory Alignment | 42 CFR § 484.205 (HH PPS), CMS PDGM rate updates, OIG Compliance Program Guidance for HHAs |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for accurate charge capture for all services delivered by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and for the maintenance of the agency fee schedule. The policy ensures that:
- All billable services are captured with correct charge codes, amounts, and dates of service.
- The agency fee schedule is reviewed and updated annually in alignment with CMS rate changes.
- Charges are reconciled against services delivered through the visit log and clinical documentation.
- Charge capture errors are identified, investigated, and corrected on a routine basis.

## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
- All billing coordinators and billing specialists.
- The Revenue Cycle Director.
- The CFO.
- Clinical scheduling coordinators responsible for visit logging.
- Any contracted billing service performing charge capture functions on behalf of the agency.

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All billable services rendered by the agency shall be captured in the billing system with the correct charge code, charge amount, and date of service.
4.2 The agency fee schedule shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, no later than January 1 of each calendar year, to reflect current CMS PDGM payment rates and any payer-specific rate changes governed under FN-FP-001.
4.3 Charge capture shall be reconciled against the visit log and clinical documentation for every 30-day payment period prior to final claim release per FN-BC-001.
4.4 Any charge capture error identified shall be corrected through the documented charge correction process and tracked to closure by the Revenue Cycle Director.
4.5 A formal charge capture audit shall be performed quarterly by the Revenue Cycle Director with results reported to the CFO.
4.6 Charge accuracy shall meet or exceed 99% for any rolling quarterly review period; any deviation triggers root cause analysis per QA-AE-002.
4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy and the current fee schedule shall be considered valid; superseded versions must not be used for billing or compliance purposes.

## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Charge Capture | The process of recording all billable services delivered to a patient with the correct charge code, charge amount, and date of service for inclusion on a claim. |
| Fee Schedule | The agency's master list of charge codes and corresponding charge amounts for all billable services. |
| Charge Capture Reconciliation | The structured comparison of charges recorded against the visit log and clinical documentation to confirm completeness and accuracy. |
| Charge Correction | The documented process of adjusting a charge previously recorded in error, including reason, authorising party, and audit trail. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Charge Capture Workflow
6.1.1 At the time each visit is completed and documentation is finalised, the assigned clinician shall close the visit in the EHR which generates the billable charge for that encounter.
6.1.2 The Billing Coordinator shall verify that every visit logged for the 30-day payment period has a corresponding charge captured in the billing system before the period is closed.
6.1.3 Any visit completed without a corresponding charge, or any charge captured without a corresponding documented visit, shall be flagged on the Charge Capture Reconciliation Log (Appendix B) for investigation within 5 business days.

### 6.2 Annual Fee Schedule Update
6.2.1 The Revenue Cycle Director shall obtain the CMS PDGM final rule rate update each year and apply the corresponding charge amount changes to the agency fee schedule no later than January 1.
6.2.2 Payer-specific rates derived from contracts maintained under FN-FP-001 shall be reviewed at the same time and updated where applicable.
6.2.3 The CFO shall approve the updated fee schedule before it is activated in the billing system.

### 6.3 Charge Reconciliation Against Visit Log
6.3.1 Prior to final claim release per FN-BC-001 §6.1, the Billing Coordinator shall reconcile charges to the visit log and clinical documentation for the 30-day payment period.
6.3.2 Discrepancies shall be resolved before claim release; unresolved discrepancies shall trigger a billing hold per FN-BC-001 §4.5.

### 6.4 Charge Correction Process
6.4.1 Identified charge errors shall be corrected only through the documented charge correction process with a recorded reason, authorising party, and date.
6.4.2 Corrections shall be retained in the billing system audit trail and shall not overwrite the original record.

### 6.5 Quarterly Charge Capture Audit
6.5.1 The Revenue Cycle Director shall perform a quarterly charge capture audit on a representative sample drawn from each clinical discipline.
6.5.2 Audit results, error rate, and corrective actions shall be reported to the CFO and integrated into the QAPI program per QA-PI-002.

## 7. Documentation Requirements
- Current agency fee schedule (Appendix A) with version date and CFO approval signature.
- Charge Capture Reconciliation Log (Appendix B) for each 30-day payment period.
- Quarterly charge capture audit reports retained for the period required by CO-HP-007.
- Signed Policy Acknowledgment (Appendix C) for all personnel within scope.

## 8. Compliance & Audit
- 100% of services delivered shall have a corresponding captured charge.
- Charge accuracy shall be ≥ 99% on any quarterly audit.
- Fee schedule shall be updated and CFO-approved annually no later than January 1.
- Charge capture and reconciliation logs shall be available for survey, payer audit, and internal compliance review at all times.

## 9. References
- 42 CFR § 484.205 — Basis of payment.
- CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Pub. 100-04, Chapter 10.
- OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.

### 9.1 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies
- FN-BC-001 — Medicare Billing & Claims Submission.
- FN-CM-001 — Claims Management & Resubmission.
- FN-FP-001 — Payer Contract Management.
- FN-FP-003 — Revenue Cycle Performance Monitoring.
- OP-SL-001 — Scheduling & Visit Logging.
- CO-HP-007 — Record Retention & Destruction.
- EN-TG-001 — Enterprise Policy Taxonomy & Classification Governance.

## 10. Training Requirements
All billing coordinators and clinical scheduling coordinators shall be trained on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment, and annually thereafter. Training shall cover the charge capture workflow, the reconciliation process, the charge correction process, and the quarterly audit cycle. Completion shall be tracked in the LMS per HR-TR-101.

## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

## APPENDICES
- Appendix A — Fee Schedule
- Appendix B — Charge Capture Reconciliation Log
- Appendix C — Policy Acknowledgment Form

## Policies/extracted_full/FN-FP-004 — Bad Debt & Charity Care.md

# FN-FP-004 — Bad Debt & Charity Care
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | FN-FP-004 |
| Title | Bad Debt & Charity Care |
| Domain | FN — Finance & Revenue Cycle |
| Subdomain | FP — Financial Planning |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Policy Owner/Steward | CFO |
| Access Tier | Tier 3 — Confidential |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Alignment | 42 CFR § 484.105 (Governing Body financial oversight); CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual Pub. 15-1, Chapter 3 (Bad Debts, Charity, and Courtesy Allowances); IRS § 501(r) (where applicable); HHS Federal Poverty Level Guidelines |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes criteria for classifying and managing bad debt write-offs and charity care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The policy ensures that:
- No patient is denied medically necessary services due to inability to pay.
- Financial hardship screening is performed before any patient account is referred for collection.
- Charity care eligibility is determined consistently against published Federal Poverty Level (FPL) guidelines.
- Bad debt write-offs occur only after the agency has exhausted reasonable collection efforts per FN-BC-003 §6.6.
- All write-offs require CFO authorisation and are documented for audit and Governing Body reporting.
- Annual reporting of bad debt and charity care is provided to the Governing Body for fiscal oversight.

## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
- The CFO (authorising party for all write-offs).
- The Revenue Cycle Director.
- Patient Account / billing personnel responsible for collections and write-off processing.
- The Compliance Officer (oversight of charity care policy application).
- The Governing Body (annual reporting recipient).
- Any contracted collection agency engaged on behalf of the agency.

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall not deny medically necessary services to any patient on the basis of inability to pay.
4.2 Every patient account that becomes financially distressed shall undergo financial hardship screening prior to any referral for external collection.
4.3 Charity care eligibility shall be determined using the published HHS Federal Poverty Level (FPL) guidelines and the agency's Charity Care Application (Appendix A).
4.4 Bad debt write-offs shall occur only after reasonable collection efforts have been exhausted in accordance with FN-BC-003 §6.6.
4.5 No patient account shall be written off as bad debt or approved as charity care without written authorisation from the CFO recorded on the Bad Debt Write-Off Authorisation form (Appendix B).
4.6 Bad debt and charity care totals shall be reported to the Governing Body at least annually, with quarterly trending reviewed by the CFO and Administrator.
4.7 Patient accounts being actively considered for charity care shall not be referred to collection during the eligibility determination period.
4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy and the current FPL thresholds shall be considered valid; superseded versions must not be used for eligibility determination.

## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Bad Debt | Amounts owed by patients which the agency has determined to be uncollectible after reasonable collection effort, written off in accordance with this policy and FN-BC-003. |
| Charity Care | Health care services provided without expectation of payment to patients meeting the agency's published financial hardship eligibility criteria. |
| Financial Hardship Screening | The structured assessment of a patient's household income against published FPL guidelines used to determine eligibility for charity care or other financial assistance. |
| FPL | Federal Poverty Level — the income thresholds published annually by HHS used as the baseline for charity care eligibility determination. |
| Reasonable Collection Effort | The documented sequence of patient billing notices, contact attempts, and external collection activity required by FN-BC-003 §6.6 before an account may be written off as bad debt. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Financial Hardship Screening
6.1.1 When a patient indicates inability to pay, or when an account becomes 90 days past due without payment, the Patient Account representative shall offer financial hardship screening using the Charity Care Application (Appendix A).
6.1.2 The patient or responsible party shall provide household income documentation as requested on the application.
6.1.3 The Revenue Cycle Director shall compare reported household income against the current published FPL thresholds and assign the appropriate eligibility category.

### 6.2 Charity Care Determination
6.2.1 Completed Charity Care Applications shall be reviewed by the Revenue Cycle Director and submitted to the CFO with a recommendation.
6.2.2 The CFO shall approve, modify, or deny each charity care request and document the determination on the application.
6.2.3 Approved charity care shall be applied to the account and the patient notified in writing.

### 6.3 Bad Debt Write-Off Authorisation
6.3.1 Accounts that have completed reasonable collection effort per FN-BC-003 §6.6 without recovery shall be presented to the CFO for write-off review on the Bad Debt Write-Off Authorisation form (Appendix B).
6.3.2 The CFO shall authorise or deny each write-off in writing; no write-off shall be processed without authorisation.
6.3.3 Authorised write-offs shall be posted to the patient account with the authorisation reference retained in the audit trail.

### 6.4 Reporting
6.4.1 The CFO shall track bad debt and charity care totals quarterly and present trended results to the Administrator.
6.4.2 An annual bad debt and charity care report shall be presented to the Governing Body for review consistent with the Governing Body's financial oversight role under GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.

## 7. Documentation Requirements
- Completed Charity Care Application (Appendix A) for each financial hardship screening.
- Signed Bad Debt Write-Off Authorisation (Appendix B) for every account written off.
- Quarterly bad debt and charity care trend reports retained per CO-HP-007.
- Annual Governing Body report retained in the governance file per GV-GB-001.
- Signed Policy Acknowledgment (Appendix C) for all personnel within scope.

## 8. Compliance & Audit
- 100% of bad debt write-offs shall have CFO authorisation on file.
- 100% of charity care determinations shall have a completed Charity Care Application on file with FPL comparison.
- No patient shall be denied medically necessary services on the basis of inability to pay.
- Annual bad debt and charity care report shall be presented to the Governing Body each fiscal year.

## 9. References
- 42 CFR § 484.105 — Governing Body financial oversight.
- CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual, Pub. 15-1, Chapter 3 — Bad Debts, Charity, and Courtesy Allowances.
- HHS Federal Poverty Level Guidelines (annually published).

### 9.1 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies
- FN-BC-003 — Patient Statements & Collections (reasonable collection effort).
- FN-FP-003 — Revenue Cycle Performance Monitoring.
- FN-FP-005 — Annual Budget & Financial Planning.
- CO-HP-007 — Record Retention & Destruction.
- GV-GB-001 — Governing Body Authority & Responsibilities.
- EN-TG-001 — Enterprise Policy Taxonomy & Classification Governance.

## 10. Training Requirements
All Revenue Cycle and Patient Account personnel shall be trained on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment, and annually thereafter. Training shall cover the financial hardship screening process, charity care eligibility determination using current FPL thresholds, and the bad debt write-off authorisation process. Completion shall be tracked in the LMS per HR-TR-101.

## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

## APPENDICES
- Appendix A — Charity Care Application
- Appendix B — Bad Debt Write-Off Authorisation
- Appendix C — Policy Acknowledgment Form

# FN-FP-006 — Supply & Equipment Cost Management
## 1. Policy Header

| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Regulatory Alignment | 42 CFR § 484.105 (Governing Body financial oversight); OIG Compliance Program Guidance for HHAs (procurement integrity); CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual cost-allocation principles |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes procurement standards, cost controls, and inventory management requirements for medical supplies and equipment used by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The policy ensures that:
- Procurement follows a standardised, documented process.
- Vendor competitive bidding is performed for purchases exceeding $2,500.
- Inventory is tracked and waste is prevented.
- Equipment is maintained and replaced on a defined schedule.
- Annual supply cost analysis is performed.
- All supply and equipment expenditures are aligned with the approved annual budget under FN-FP-005.

## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
- The CFO (final procurement authorising party for purchases above defined thresholds).
- The Administrator.
- The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (for clinical supply and equipment requisition).
- Any designated Procurement Coordinator or Operations Manager.
- All staff who request, receive, store, or use agency-procured supplies and equipment.

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All procurement of medical supplies and equipment shall follow the agency's standardised procurement process documented in this policy and shall not be initiated outside the approved process.
4.2 Any single procurement action with an expected value greater than $2,500 shall be subject to documented competitive bidding from at least three qualified vendors where available.
4.3 All supplies and equipment received shall be entered into the Inventory Tracking Log (Appendix B) at the point of receipt.
4.4 Equipment requiring scheduled maintenance shall be maintained on the documented preventive maintenance and replacement schedule.
4.5 An annual supply cost analysis shall be performed by the CFO and presented as part of the budget development cycle under FN-FP-005.
4.6 Supply and equipment expenditure shall remain aligned with the approved annual budget; any line item projected to exceed budget by more than 10% shall trigger corrective action under FN-FP-005 §4.4.
4.7 No vendor relationship shall be established with an entity appearing on the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) or the SAM exclusion database, per HR-TA-003.
4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid; superseded versions must not be used for any procurement or financial control purpose.

## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Procurement | The process by which the agency acquires medical supplies, equipment, and related goods from external vendors. |
| Competitive Bidding | The structured solicitation of price and service offers from at least three qualified vendors for a single procurement action above the threshold. |
| Inventory | The complete set of supplies and equipment owned or controlled by the agency at any point in time, recorded in the Inventory Tracking Log. |
| Preventive Maintenance | Scheduled servicing of equipment performed at defined intervals to maintain operational reliability and clinical safety. |
| Annual Supply Cost Analysis | The yearly review of supply expenditure performed by the CFO as input to the next budget cycle. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Procurement Authorisation
6.1.1 The requesting party shall complete a Procurement Authorisation Form (Appendix A) identifying the supply or equipment, quantity, expected unit cost, justification, and applicable budget line.
6.1.2 Requests below the competitive bidding threshold shall be approved by the Administrator or designee. Requests at or above $2,500 shall be approved by the CFO.

### 6.2 Competitive Bidding
6.2.1 For any single procurement action above $2,500, the Procurement Coordinator shall obtain price and service quotations from at least three qualified vendors where available.
6.2.2 Bids shall be summarised on the Procurement Authorisation Form with a documented selection rationale; selection shall be on the basis of total value (price, service, quality, and risk), not lowest price alone.
6.2.3 If three qualified vendors cannot be identified, the rationale shall be documented and the CFO shall approve the sole-source or limited-source selection.

### 6.3 Vendor Eligibility Verification
6.3.1 Prior to establishing a new vendor relationship, the Procurement Coordinator shall verify that the vendor does not appear on the OIG LEIE or SAM exclusion lists per HR-TA-003.
6.3.2 Vendor eligibility shall be re-verified at contract renewal.

### 6.4 Receiving and Inventory Tracking
6.4.1 All supplies and equipment received shall be inspected against the purchase order and entered into the Inventory Tracking Log (Appendix B) at the point of receipt.
6.4.2 Discrepancies between order and receipt shall be reported to the Procurement Coordinator within 1 business day for vendor follow-up.
6.4.3 Issuance of supplies and equipment to clinical staff shall be logged so that on-hand quantities remain accurate and waste can be detected.

### 6.5 Equipment Maintenance and Replacement
6.5.1 Equipment requiring scheduled maintenance shall be entered on the preventive maintenance schedule with assigned responsibility and due dates.
6.5.2 Equipment past its defined replacement interval, or unserviceable, shall be removed from clinical use and dispositioned per the replacement schedule.

### 6.6 Annual Supply Cost Analysis
6.6.1 The CFO shall perform an annual supply cost analysis comparing the prior year's supply expenditure to budget and to clinical volume.
6.6.2 Results shall feed into the next budget cycle under FN-FP-005.

## 7. Documentation Requirements
- Completed Procurement Authorisation Form (Appendix A) for each procurement action.
- Inventory Tracking Log (Appendix B) maintained on a continuous basis.
- Bid summaries for all procurements above the competitive bidding threshold.
- Preventive maintenance and equipment replacement schedules retained per CO-HP-007.
- Vendor exclusion screening records per HR-TA-003.
- Signed Policy Acknowledgment (Appendix C) for all personnel within scope.

## 8. Compliance & Audit
- 100% of procurement actions above $2,500 shall have documented competitive bidding (or a CFO-approved sole-source rationale).
- 100% of new vendors shall have OIG LEIE / SAM exclusion verification on file before any purchase order is issued.
- Inventory variance shall be investigated and resolved within 5 business days of identification.
- Supply expenditure variance from budget shall be reviewed monthly per FN-FP-005 §4.4.

## 9. References
- 42 CFR § 484.105 — Governing Body financial oversight.
- OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies — procurement integrity.
- CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual cost-allocation principles.

### 9.1 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies
- FN-FP-005 — Annual Budget & Financial Planning.
- FN-FP-007 — Financial Compliance & Fraud Monitoring Controls.
- HR-TA-003 — OIG/SAM Exclusion Screening.
- CO-HP-007 — Record Retention & Destruction.
- GV-GB-001 — Governing Body Authority & Responsibilities.
- EN-TG-001 — Enterprise Policy Taxonomy & Classification Governance.

## 10. Training Requirements
All personnel with procurement, receiving, or inventory management responsibilities shall be trained on this policy within 14 calendar days of assignment and annually thereafter. Training shall cover the procurement authorisation workflow, the competitive bidding threshold, vendor eligibility verification, and inventory tracking. Completion shall be tracked in the LMS per HR-TR-101.

## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

## APPENDICES
- Appendix A — Procurement Authorisation Form
- Appendix B — Inventory Tracking Log
- Appendix C — Policy Acknowledgment Form

# Governing Body Authority & Responsibilities
## 1. Policy Header

| Domain | GV — Governance & Administration |
| Subdomain | GB — Governing Body |

| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the authority, composition, functions, and oversight responsibilities of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Governing Body is the ultimate authority accountable for the operation, management, fiscal viability, and regulatory compliance of the home health agency. This policy ensures the agency satisfies the requirements set forth in 42 CFR § 484.105 — Condition of Participation: Organization and Administration of Services, which mandates that a home health agency must have a governing body that assumes full legal authority and responsibility for the agency's overall operation and management.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All members of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (including voting and non-voting members)
The Agency Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Compliance Officer
All senior leadership personnel who report directly to the Governing Body or Administrator
All contracted management entities performing governing body functions on behalf of the agency
This policy does not apply to day-to-day clinical or operational staff except to the extent that Governing Body decisions establish requirements, standards, or directives that govern their work.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a designated Governing Body that holds full legal authority and responsibility for the overall operation, management, and regulatory compliance of the home health agency, as required by 42 CFR § 484.105(a).
4.2 The Governing Body shall be responsible for ensuring that Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. operates in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and licensure requirements at all times.
4.3 The Governing Body shall appoint a qualified Administrator who is authorized to act on behalf of the Governing Body in the day-to-day management of the agency and who meets the qualifications defined in agency policy GV-OG-002 and applicable California state requirements.
4.4 The Governing Body shall ensure the appointment and ongoing oversight of a qualified Clinical Manager (Director of Nursing) responsible for all clinical services, in compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105(c).
4.5 The Governing Body shall approve and oversee the agency's:
Scope of services (GV-OG-003)
Organizational structure and reporting lines (GV-OG-001)
Annual strategic plan and operational goals (GV-OG-004)
Policy framework and all REQUIRED-tier policies (GV-PM-001, GV-PM-002)
QAPI program (QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002)
Corporate compliance program (CO-CP-001)
Annual operating budget (FN-FP-005)
Emergency preparedness plan (OP-FM-005)
4.6 The Governing Body shall meet at a frequency sufficient to fulfill its oversight responsibilities, but not less than quarterly, with meetings documented in formal minutes per policy GV-GB-002.
4.7 The Governing Body shall not delegate its ultimate accountability for regulatory compliance, patient safety, or fiscal integrity. Delegation of specific authority shall comply with policy GV-OG-005.
4.8 All members of the Governing Body shall disclose and manage conflicts of interest in accordance with policy GV-GB-003.
4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose. Any revision to this policy requires re-acknowledgment by all Governing Body members and senior leadership within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Governing Body | The individual(s), board of directors, trustees, partnership, corporation, or other legally constituted authority that has ultimate responsibility for the management and operation of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., as defined by 42 CFR § 484.2 and § 484.105. |
| Administrator | The individual appointed by the Governing Body who is responsible for managing the agency's day-to-day operations and who meets all qualifications specified in agency policy GV-OG-002 and applicable California state law. |
| Clinical Manager | The registered nurse (or qualified individual per California state law) designated by the Governing Body to oversee clinical services including patient care delivery, clinical staff supervision, and OASIS compliance. Also referred to as Director of Nursing (DON). |
| Fiduciary Duty | The legal obligation of Governing Body members to act in good faith, with due diligence, and in the best interest of the agency and the patients it serves. |
| Quorum | The minimum number of Governing Body members required to be present (physically or via approved teleconference) to conduct official business, as defined in the agency's bylaws or operating agreement. |
| QAPI | Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement — the structured program required by 42 CFR § 484.65 for ongoing quality monitoring and improvement. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Establishment and Composition of the Governing Body

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Agency Owner / Corporate Entity | Formally establish the Governing Body through articles of incorporation, operating agreement, partnership agreement, or equivalent legal instrument for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The establishing document must identify: (a) the legal form of the Governing Body; (b) the minimum and maximum number of members; (c) the quorum requirement; (d) the terms of appointment or election. | Prior to initial Medicare certification and maintained continuously thereafter. |
| 6.1.2 | Governing Body Chair | Maintain a current roster of all Governing Body members including: full legal name, title/role, date of appointment, term expiration date, voting status, and contact information. | Updated within 7 calendar days of any membership change. |
| 6.1.3 | Governing Body | Ensure composition includes, at minimum, individuals with competency in: (a) healthcare operations or clinical services; (b) financial management; (c) regulatory compliance. If any competency area is not represented by a current member, the Governing Body shall retain qualified advisory counsel within 30 calendar days of identifying the gap. | Ongoing; reviewed annually at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Verify that no Governing Body member appears on the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) or the System for Award Management (SAM) exclusion database at the time of appointment and monthly thereafter, per policy HR-TA-003. | At appointment and monthly thereafter. |

### 6.2 Core Responsibilities of the Governing Body
The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall fulfill the following responsibilities directly and shall not delegate ultimate accountability for any of these functions:
#### 6.2.1 — Legal Authority and Agency Operations

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1.1 | Governing Body | Assume and maintain full legal authority for the overall operation, management, and fiscal viability of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. | Continuous. |
| 6.2.1.2 | Governing Body | Ensure the agency maintains current and valid: (a) California home health license — HCAI License No. 406412878; (b) Medicare certification; (c) Medicaid enrollment (if applicable); (d) accreditation (if applicable) — per policy GV-EA-004. | Continuous; verified at each quarterly meeting. |
| 6.2.1.3 | Governing Body | Review and approve the agency's defined scope of services (policy GV-OG-003) at least annually. Ensure the agency does not provide services beyond those for which it is licensed, staffed, and competent to deliver. | Annually, within 30 calendar days of the start of the fiscal year. |

#### 6.2.2 — Appointment and Oversight of Key Personnel

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.2.1 | Governing Body | Appoint a qualified Administrator and document the appointment in Governing Body minutes. The Administrator must meet all qualifications defined in policy GV-OG-002 and applicable California state law. | Prior to agency operation and within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.2.2.2 | Governing Body | Appoint or confirm the appointment of a qualified Clinical Manager (Director of Nursing) responsible for all clinical services, per 42 CFR § 484.105(c). | Prior to agency operation and within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.2.2.3 | Governing Body | Appoint or confirm the designation of a Compliance Officer with authority and independence to operate the corporate compliance program, per policy CO-CP-002. | Prior to agency operation and within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.2.2.4 | Governing Body | Conduct or commission an annual performance evaluation of the Administrator. Results and any corrective directives shall be documented in executive session minutes. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of the end of each fiscal year. |
| 6.2.2.5 | Governing Body | Review and approve the agency's succession plan for the Administrator, Clinical Manager, and Compliance Officer, per policy GV-GB-004. | Annually at the second quarterly meeting; updated within 14 calendar days of any key leadership vacancy. |

#### 6.2.3 — Policy and Compliance Oversight

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.3.1 | Governing Body | Approve all REQUIRED-tier policies prior to implementation and ensure a defined policy review cycle exists per policies GV-PM-001 and GV-PM-002. | Prior to implementation of each REQUIRED policy; review cycle approved annually. |
| 6.2.3.2 | Governing Body | Receive and review a compliance status report from the Compliance Officer at each quarterly meeting. The report must address: (a) active compliance investigations; (b) audit findings; (c) regulatory changes affecting the agency; (d) training completion rates. | Quarterly. |
| 6.2.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Prepare and submit the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body no fewer than 7 calendar days before each scheduled quarterly meeting. | 7 calendar days before each quarterly meeting. |
| 6.2.3.4 | Governing Body | Review and act upon any compliance deficiency identified as high-risk within 14 calendar days of receiving the compliance report. Action must be documented in meeting minutes or a special resolution. | Within 14 calendar days of report receipt. |

#### 6.2.4 — Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) Oversight

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.4.1 | Governing Body | Approve the agency's QAPI plan, per policy QA-PG-002, and ensure that the plan includes measurable quality indicators, performance improvement projects, and patient safety initiatives. | Annually; approved at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year. |
| 6.2.4.2 | Clinical Manager / QA Designee | Present a QAPI performance report to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting including: (a) quality indicator trends; (b) status of active PIPs; (c) adverse event summary; (d) patient satisfaction data; (e) Star Rating / Home Health Compare trends (policy QA-SM-004). | Quarterly. |
| 6.2.4.3 | Governing Body | Review, discuss, and document its response to the QAPI report. If any quality indicator falls below the defined threshold for 2 consecutive reporting periods, the Governing Body shall direct corrective action and assign accountability with a defined resolution deadline. | At each quarterly meeting; corrective action directive within 14 calendar days if thresholds are breached. |

#### 6.2.5 — Financial Oversight

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.5.1 | Governing Body | Review and approve the annual operating budget per policy FN-FP-005. | Annually; approved no later than 30 calendar days before the start of each fiscal year. |
| 6.2.5.2 | Administrator | Present a financial performance report to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting including: (a) revenue vs. budget variance; (b) accounts receivable aging; (c) claims denial rate and trending; (d) cash flow position. | Quarterly. |
| 6.2.5.3 | Governing Body | Review financial reports and direct corrective action if: (a) actual revenue deviates more than 10% below budget for 2 consecutive months; (b) claims denial rate exceeds 5%; (c) days in accounts receivable exceed 60. Directives must be documented in meeting minutes. | At each quarterly meeting. |

#### 6.2.6 — Emergency Preparedness

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.6.1 | Governing Body | Approve the agency's Emergency Operations and Business Continuity Plan per policy OP-FM-005 and 42 CFR § 484.102. | Annually; approved at the third quarterly meeting. |
| 6.2.6.2 | Administrator | Report the results of the most recent emergency preparedness drill or exercise to the Governing Body, including identified gaps and corrective actions. | At the quarterly meeting following each drill (minimum 2 drills per year). |

### 6.3 Governing Body Meetings

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Governing Body Chair | Schedule and convene regular Governing Body meetings no fewer than 4 times per calendar year (quarterly). The meeting schedule for the upcoming year must be established and distributed to all members by December 15 of the preceding year. | Quarterly; schedule distributed by December 15. |
| 6.3.2 | Governing Body Chair | Convene special meetings when urgent matters arise, including but not limited to: (a) CMS survey findings requiring immediate corrective action; (b) serious adverse events; (c) regulatory enforcement actions; (d) key leadership vacancies. Notice of a special meeting must be provided to all members at least 48 hours in advance unless the matter constitutes an imminent threat to patient safety, in which case notice may be shortened to the minimum practicable. | As needed; notice within 48 hours or shorter for imminent patient safety threats. |
| 6.3.3 | Designated Secretary / Administrator | Prepare and distribute the meeting agenda to all Governing Body members no fewer than 7 calendar days before each scheduled meeting. The agenda must include standing items: (a) approval of prior minutes; (b) Administrator report; (c) compliance report; (d) QAPI report; (e) financial report; (f) old business; (g) new business. | 7 calendar days before each meeting. |
| 6.3.4 | Designated Secretary | Record formal minutes for each meeting per policy GV-GB-002. Minutes must document: (a) date, time, and location; (b) members present and absent; (c) quorum determination; (d) all motions, seconds, and voting outcomes; (e) all directives issued with assigned responsible parties and deadlines; (f) executive session topics (without protected details). | Draft minutes completed within 14 calendar days of the meeting; approved at the next regular meeting. |
| 6.3.5 | Governing Body Chair | Ensure a quorum is present before conducting any official business. If quorum is not achieved, the meeting shall be rescheduled within 14 calendar days. | At the start of each meeting. |

### 6.4 Conflict of Interest Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | All Governing Body Members | Complete and submit the Conflict of Interest Disclosure Form (Appendix B) at the time of appointment, annually thereafter, and within 7 calendar days of any change in circumstances that could create a new conflict, per policy GV-GB-003. | At appointment; annually; within 7 days of change. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Review all submitted conflict of interest disclosures within 14 calendar days of receipt and present a summary to the Governing Body with recommendations for management or recusal. | Within 14 calendar days of receipt. |
| 6.4.3 | Governing Body | Act on conflict of interest recommendations. Any member with a disclosed conflict shall recuse from discussion and voting on the affected matter. Recusals must be documented in meeting minutes. | At the meeting where the affected matter is addressed. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Governing Body fails to meet quarterly | Administrator notifies all members and the Compliance Officer in writing. | Administrator schedules a make-up meeting. If Governing Body does not convene within 30 calendar days, the Compliance Officer documents the deficiency and initiates corrective action per QA-AE-003. | Make-up meeting within 30 calendar days of the missed quarter. |
| Quorum not achieved for 2 consecutive scheduled meetings | Governing Body Chair escalates to the full membership in writing. | Chair initiates membership recruitment or replacement per the agency's bylaws. Issue must be resolved before the next scheduled meeting. | Within 30 calendar days. |
| Key leadership vacancy (Administrator, Clinical Manager, Compliance Officer) exceeds 30 days unfilled | Governing Body Chair | Governing Body must appoint an interim designee within 14 calendar days of vacancy and document the appointment. Permanent appointment must occur within 90 calendar days. | Interim: 14 days. Permanent: 90 days. |
| CMS survey results in Condition-level deficiency | Administrator convenes a special Governing Body meeting. | Governing Body directs development of a Plan of Correction within CMS-required timeframes (typically 10 calendar days). Governing Body receives weekly status updates until resolution is confirmed. | Special meeting within 48 hours of receipt of findings; Plan of Correction per CMS deadline. |
| Compliance Officer reports fraud, waste, or abuse concern to Governing Body | Governing Body Chair | Governing Body directs investigation per CO-CP-007 and ensures non-retaliation per CO-CP-005. Governing Body receives investigation status updates at each meeting until resolution. | Investigation initiated within 7 calendar days; updates at each meeting. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Governing Body is legally established and documented. | Review of establishing documents (articles, bylaws, operating agreement). | Current, complete, and on file at all times. |
| Governing Body meets at least quarterly. | Review of meeting minutes with dates and attendance. | 4 or more meetings per calendar year with quorum present at each. |
| Key personnel (Administrator, Clinical Manager, Compliance Officer) are appointed and documented. | Review of Governing Body minutes; personnel files; appointment letters. | Current appointments documented; no vacancy exceeds 30 days without interim designee. |
| QAPI plan is reviewed and approved annually. | Review of Governing Body minutes for documented approval. | Annual approval documented at first quarterly meeting. |
| Compliance reports are presented quarterly. | Review of Governing Body agendas and minutes; compliance report files. | Reports submitted 7 days before each meeting; discussion documented in minutes. |
| Conflict of Interest disclosures are current. | Review of Appendix B forms for each member; annual renewal dates. | 100% completion rate; no lapsed disclosures. |
| Budget is approved annually. | Review of Governing Body minutes; budget document. | Approved no later than 30 days before fiscal year start. |
| Governing Body members are screened for exclusion. | Review of OIG/SAM screening logs. | Initial screening at appointment; monthly screening documented. |
| Policy acknowledgments are current. | Review of signed Appendix C forms. | 100% acknowledgment within 14 calendar days of effective date or new appointment. |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify:
Evidence that a Governing Body exists and is functioning. Surveyors will request establishing documents and a current membership roster. A sole proprietor must demonstrate individual acceptance of governing body responsibilities.
Evidence that the Governing Body has appointed a qualified Administrator. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for appointment documentation and verify qualifications per California state requirements.
Evidence of Clinical Manager oversight. Surveyors will look for Governing Body minutes documenting appointment, reporting, and oversight of clinical services leadership.
Evidence that the Governing Body oversees QAPI. Surveyors will examine whether the Governing Body has reviewed, approved, and acted upon quality data. Passive receipt of reports without documented action is a common deficiency.
Evidence of policy oversight. Surveyors will verify that the Governing Body has approved the agency's policies and that a review cycle exists.
Evidence of fiscal oversight. Surveyors will review whether the Governing Body monitors the agency's financial viability and acts on adverse trends.
Meeting frequency and documentation quality. Surveyors will request all meeting minutes for the survey look-back period and assess completeness, including attendance, quorum, and documented decisions.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No documented evidence that a Governing Body exists or functions. | Condition-level deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.105. Potential termination of Medicare certification. | Maintain establishing documents, current roster, and quarterly minutes on file and readily accessible. |
| Governing Body meetings are held but not documented. | Surveyor will treat undocumented meetings as not having occurred. | Use Appendix D template; complete draft minutes within 14 calendar days. |
| Governing Body "rubber stamps" reports without documented discussion or action. | Surveyors will cite passive governance as failure to exercise oversight. | Minutes must document specific discussion points, questions, directives, and assigned follow-up. |
| Key leadership vacancies are unfilled for extended periods. | Surveyor will cite failure to ensure adequate management. | Fill or designate interim within 14 calendar days per Section 6.5. |
| No documented conflict of interest disclosures. | OIG compliance program requirement; potential survey finding. | Enforce annual disclosure per Appendix B; Compliance Officer tracks compliance. |
| QAPI plan approved but no evidence of Governing Body review of quality data. | Surveyor will cite failure of governing body oversight of QAPI (42 CFR § 484.65 cross-reference). | Require quarterly QAPI report presentation and document Governing Body response. |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All Governing Body members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall receive orientation to this policy within 14 calendar days of appointment. Orientation shall be conducted by the Administrator or Compliance Officer and must cover: (a) the legal authority and responsibilities of the Governing Body; (b) meeting and quorum requirements; (c) conflict of interest obligations; (d) QAPI, compliance, and financial oversight expectations; (e) CMS survey process and surveyor expectations for governance documentation.
10.2 All Governing Body members and senior leadership personnel within scope of this policy (Section 3) shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.
10.3 The Administrator shall maintain a tracking log of all policy acknowledgments and report any non-compliance to the Governing Body Chair within 7 calendar days of the acknowledgment deadline. Failure to acknowledge within the required timeframe shall result in written notification from the Governing Body Chair with a mandatory completion deadline of 7 additional calendar days.
10.4 Annual refresher training on governing body responsibilities shall be conducted at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year. Attendance shall be documented in meeting minutes.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope, within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.
